447	## Render a frame
448	
449	With no arguments it draws the frame under the playhead at the canvas's size and writes a PNG to a temporary file.
450	
451	```json
452	{ "t": 1200000, "path": "/tmp/shot.png", "max_width": 960 }
453	```
454	
455	The picture comes back two ways: as an image the model can see, and as a file on disk. The text beside it says what was drawn and ends by naming the file:
456	
457	```
458	Frame at 1200000 ticks of a 1920×1080 px canvas, rendered at 960×540 px. Written to /tmp/shot.png.
459	```
460	
461	It uses the same writer as [**File ▸ Save Frame…**](/export/save-frame/), so a PNG from either one is identical, byte for byte.
462	
463	With a [nest](/mcp/nests/) open, it draws that nest at its own size, from its own zero, without the nest clip's position, scale or opacity. It takes no `scope`, so open the nest with `set_scope` to look inside.
464	
465	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does | Default |
466	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
467	| [`t`](#t) | integer | No | The moment to render, in ticks. | The playhead |
468	| [`path`](#path) | string | No | Where to write the file. | A temporary file |
469	| [`format`](#format) | string | No | `png`, `jpeg` or `heic`. | From the path, else `png` |
470	| [`max_width`](#max_width) | integer | No | Caps the width in pixels, 16 to 8192. | The canvas's width |
471	| [`burn_in_timecode`](#burn_in_timecode) | boolean | No | Draws the project timecode over the picture. | `false` |
472	| [`ungraded`](#ungraded) | boolean | No | Draws every clip as if it weren't graded. | `false` |
473	| [`selection`](#selection) | integer | No | Draws what an adjustment clip's qualifier selects. | None |
474	| [`sdr_version`](#sdr_version) | boolean | No | Draws an HDR project's SDR version. | `false` |
475	| [`waveform`](#waveform-parade-and-histogram) | boolean | No | Also measures the waveform. | `false` |
476	| [`parade`](#waveform-parade-and-histogram) | boolean | No | Also measures the RGB parade. | `false` |
477	| [`histogram`](#waveform-parade-and-histogram) | boolean | No | Also measures the histogram. | `false` |
478	| [`vectorscope`](#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom) | boolean | No | Also measures the vectorscope. | `false` |
479	| [`vectorscope_zoom`](#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom) | integer | No | 1, 2 or 4. Needs `vectorscope`. | 1 |
480	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on. | The frontmost project |
481	
482	## Choose the moment and the file
483	
484	### `t`
485	
486	The moment to render, in ticks, 600,000 to the second. It's rounded to the project's frame grid. Leave it out for the playhead. A time before zero draws the first frame, and a time past the end returns an [error](#when-it-wont-render).
487	
488	With a nest open, `t` and the playhead are the nest's own time.
489	
490	### `path`
491	
492	Where to write the file, for example `~/Desktop/shot.png`. The folder must already exist, because Frame Job won't create one. An empty `path` is an error.
493	
494	Leave it out for a temporary file. Either way, the last sentence of the text names the file written.
495	
496	### `format`
497	
498	The kind of file to write.
499	
500	| `format` | What you get |
501	| --- | --- |
502	| `png` | Lossless, keeping the canvas's transparency. |
503	| `jpeg` | Quality 0.9. JPEG has no transparency, so a transparent canvas is flattened onto black, and the text always says so. |
504	| `heic` | Quality 0.9, keeping the canvas's transparency. |
505	
506	With no `format`, the path's extension decides: `.jpg` and `.jpeg` both mean JPEG, and `.heic` means HEIC. Any other path writes a PNG.
507	
508	An explicit `format` wins, and the path's extension is replaced rather than added to, so `{"path": "shot.jpg", "format": "png"}` writes `shot.png`. Only an extension Frame Job knows is replaced: `Talk v1.2` becomes `Talk v1.2.png`, not `Talk v1.png`. A JPEG always ends `.jpg`, so `shot.jpeg` is written as `shot.jpg`.
509	
510	`jpg` also works as a `format`, and capitals don't matter.
511	
512	### `max_width`
513	
514	Caps the image's width in pixels, from 16 to 8192. The picture keeps its shape and is never made larger than the canvas. Leave it out for the canvas's own size.
515	
516	A smaller frame is quicker to send and to look at. The [scopes](#measure-the-frame) measure the frame as written, so their counts cover fewer pixels too.
517	
518	## Change what's drawn
519	
520	These four draw something other than the plain picture. The view switches in the window never reach this tool or an export, so an agent asks here.
521	
522	### `burn_in_timecode`
523	
524	Draws the project timecode over the picture, on top of everything, as the export sheet's **Burn in timecode** does. It's the project's own timecode, in the toolbar's spelling. An export from the in/out range shows project time too, so the number always matches the timeline. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/).
525	
526	### `ungraded`
527	
528	Draws every clip as if it weren't graded: Light, Color, wheels and curves neutral, and no look. It's the picture **View ▸ Show Ungraded** gives. See [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/).
529	
530	### `selection`
531	
532	Takes an adjustment clip's id and draws what its qualifier selects, in place of grading. It's the picture **View ▸ Show Selection** gives.
533	
534	- White is fully graded, and black is untouched.
535	- It's the blurred selection when the qualifier has a blur, and it's multiplied by any matte cutting the clip.
536	- The clip's strength isn't applied.
537	- Every layer in front of the clip is left out.
538	- Where the clip isn't on the frame, the picture is black.
539	
540	Frame Job won't do this for any other kind of clip. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).
541	
542	### `sdr_version`
543	
544	Draws an [HDR project's](/hdr/dynamic-range/) SDR version, the picture **View ▸ Show SDR Version** gives. White titles come back near white, and highlights above reference white roll off. It's what the SDR exports and JPEG frames hold.
545	
546	In an SDR project it changes nothing, and the frame comes out identical. See [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/).
547	
548	## Measure the frame
549	
550	Each scope argument measures the rendered frame through the same analyser as the [**View ▸ Scopes**](/color/scopes/) panel, so the two can't count differently. The text gives the headline figures, and a JSON file beside the image holds the counts, named after it: `shot.png` gets `shot.png.waveform.json`.
551	
552	The scopes read the frame as it was drawn, so `max_width`, `burn_in_timecode`, `ungraded` and `selection` all change what they count.
553	
554	If the measurement can't run, the call comes back as an error, but the image is already written and the error names it: "Wrote …, but its waveform could not be measured: the GPU pass did not run."
555	
556	### `waveform`, `parade` and `histogram`
557	
558	- **`waveform`** measures luma. The text gives the share of pixels clipping high and low.
559	- **`parade`** measures R′, G′ and B′ the way the waveform measures luma. The text gives the share clipping high and low for each channel.
560	- **`histogram`** counts R′, G′, B′ and Y′ at 256 levels. The text gives the share clipping high and low, read from Y′.
561	
562	For example: "Waveform: highlights clipped in 0.4 % of pixels, shadows in 0.0 %; its 256 × 256 counts are in …". A pixel clips high at level 255 and low at level 0.
563	
564	| JSON key | `waveform` | `parade` | `histogram` |
565	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
566	| `width`, `height` | The frame measured | The frame measured | The frame measured |
567	| `levels` | 256 | 256 | 256 |
568	| `columns` | 256 | 256 | |
569	| `counts` | 256 column bins, each 256 levels | The same, under `red`, `green` and `blue` | |
570	| `red`, `green`, `blue`, `luma` | | | 256 counts each |
571	| `clipped_high`, `clipped_low` | Pixels clipping | Pixels clipping, by channel | Pixels clipping, by Y′ |
572	| `marks_high`, `marks_low` | The column bins where at least 0.5 % of the column clips | The same, by channel | |
573	| `highlights`, `shadows` | Percentages | | Percentages |
574	
575	### `vectorscope` and `vectorscope_zoom`
576	
577	`vectorscope` measures Rec. 709 Cb and Cr of the encoded values in 256 × 256 bins centred on neutral, bin 128. The text gives the share of pixels that are neutral.
578	
579	`vectorscope_zoom` is 1, 2 or 4, like the 1×, 2× and 4× cells on a [vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) slot, and it needs `vectorscope: true`. Zooming spreads a near-grey picture over more bins. At 2 and 4, a pixel off the plot isn't counted, and the text also gives the share that lie off it.
580	
581	| JSON key | What it holds |
582	| --- | --- |
583	| `width`, `height` | The frame measured. |
584	| `bins`, `centre` | 256 and 128. |
585	| `matrix`, `values` | `Rec. 709` and `encoded`. |
586	| `counts` | 256 arrays by Cr bin, each indexed by Cb bin. |
587	| `neutral` | Pixels in the neutral bin. |
588	| `zoom` | The zoom. |
589	| `off_plot` | Pixels left off the plot. Always 0 at 1. |
590	| `targets` | The six 75 % colour targets, `R`, `Mg`, `B`, `Cy`, `G` and `Yl`, each `[cb, cr]` in bins at this zoom, or `null` off the plot. |
591	| `skin_line_degrees` | The skin line's angle. |
592	
593	## Read what the answer says
594	
595	The text always starts with the frame's time and sizes and ends with "Written to …". Anything else worth saying sits between the two.
596	
597	### Graphic problems in the answer
598	
599	When a [graphic](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/) in the frame had a problem, the answer names it, with its frame and what went wrong:
600	
601	- `Graphic "lower-third" failed at frame 12: …`
602	- `Graphic "lower-third" warned at frame 12: …`
603	- `Graphic "lower-third" does not compile: …`
604	
605	A failed graphic draws its error card in the picture.
606	
607	### Waiting for cutout masks
608	
609	A clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) waits up to 30 s for the masks the frame needs. Frame Job starts making them as soon as the cutout is set, on your Mac.
610	
611	Past 30 s the clip is drawn whole, and the answer says so: "Clip 12 is drawn uncut: its person masks were not ready within 30 s." For a picture with its subject set to foreground, it says "its foreground masks".
612	
613	So after setting a cutout, read that sentence before trusting the frame. [`analyze_cutout`](/mcp/tools-analysis/) can wait for the masks first.
614	
615	### A cursor that can't be drawn
616	
617	A screen recording's cursor is drawn from its cursor file. When the file can't be read, the clip draws without one and the answer says "The cursor of media 5 is not drawn: …".
618	
619	## Frames from an HDR project
620	
621	In an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), the frame depends on the format:
622	
623	| What you ask for | What you get |
624	| --- | --- |
625	| `png` | 16-bit, labelled BT.2100 HLG |
626	| `heic` | 10-bit, labelled BT.2100 HLG |
627	| `jpeg` | The project's SDR version, labelled BT.709 |
628	| Any format with `sdr_version` | The project's SDR version, labelled BT.709 |
629	
630	Scopes read the picture drawn. On the HLG picture they read the HLG signal, and on the SDR version they read as an SDR project's do.
631	
632	On the HLG signal:
633	
634	- Each scope's JSON adds `signal: "hlg"`.
635	- The waveform, parade and histogram JSON add `scale`: `unit` (`cd/m²`), `ticks` (each with `percent`, `level` and `nits`), `reference_white_percent` (75) and `clip_percent` (100).
636	- Luma takes Rec. 2020's weights, and the vectorscope takes Rec. 2020's matrix and targets.
637	- The text says so. The waveform's reads "reference white at 75 %, 203 cd/m², and 100 % at 1,000 cd/m²".
638	
639	See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/) and [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/).
640	
641	## When it won't render
642	
643	Nothing is drawn in these cases, and the answer says why.
644	
645	| It says | What to do |
646	| --- | --- |
647	| "No frame at … Either the time is past the end of the timeline, the media is missing, or the timeline is empty." | Check `duration` and `missing_media` in [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/). |
648	| "There is no folder at … to write into." | Create the folder, or choose another `path`. |
649	| "path must name a file to write — omit it for a temporary one." | The `path` was empty. |
650	| "format must be one of png, jpeg, heic (got …)." | Use one of the three. |
651	| "max_width must be 16…8192 px (got …)." | Use a width in range. |
652	| "selection must name an adjustment clip of this project; clip … is not one." | Pass an adjustment clip's id. An adjustment clip can't be inside a nest, so close any open nest first. |
653	| "vectorscope_zoom must be 1, 2 or 4 (got …)." | Use one of the three. |
654	| "vectorscope_zoom needs vectorscope: true." | Add `vectorscope: true`. |

668	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
669	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
670	
671	Use these three tools to write the timeline to a file from an agent, follow the job and stop it. `export` doesn't wait for the file. It checks the request, puts a job on the Export Queue and returns at once, and the agent then asks how the job is going until it ends.
672	
673	<AtAGlance
674	  menu={['File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
675	  keys="⌘E"
676	  where="The export sheet's Add to Queue, and each row's Cancel in the Export Queue"
677	  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
678	/>
679	
680	## Write a file
681	
682	<Steps>
683	
684	1. Call `export` with a preset and a path. It returns straight away.
685	
686	   ```json
687	   { "preset": "h264", "path": "/Volumes/Edits/cut", "size": "1080p" }
688	   ```
689	
690	   ```json
691	   { "export_id": 3, "path": "/Volumes/Edits/cut.mp4", "status": "running" }
692	   ```
693	
694	2. Call `export_status` with that `export_id`, pause, and call it again until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
695	
696	3. Read the `done` result. It says what the file holds, including the loudness it measured and any warnings.
697	
698	</Steps>
699	
700	To stop the job, call `cancel_export`. The job shows in **Window ▸ Export Queue** like any other, but the window doesn't open by itself.
701	
702	## Export
703	
704	`export` does what **File ▸ Export…** does with **Add to Queue**, and it writes the file the same way, so an agent's file and a person's match. It takes the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)'s controls in the sheet's own terms, apart from the frame rate.
705	
706	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
707	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
708	| `preset` | string | Yes | The encoding: a container and a codec. See [Presets](#presets). |
709	| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write, such as `~/Movies/cut.mp4`. See [Path handling](#path-handling). |
710	| `size` | string or `[width, height]` | No | The output size. See [Size](#size). |
711	| `range` | string | No | `project` for the whole timeline, or `in_out` for the in and out range. See [Range](#range). |
712	| `video_bitrate` | integer | No | Target video rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
713	| `audio_bitrate` | integer | No | Target AAC or Opus rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
714	| `loudness_lufs` | number | No | Normalise the whole mix to this loudness, −70 to 0. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
715	| `peak_dbtp` | number | No | The master limiter's ceiling, −20 to 0. See [Peak dBTP](#peak-dbtp). |
716	| `audio_bits` | integer | No | 16 or 24, for WAV and AIFF. See [Audio bits](#audio-bits). |
717	| `stems` | string | No | `tracks` or `names`, to write stems beside an audio mix. See [Stems](#stems). |
718	| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draw the project timecode over the picture, on top of everything. Off by default. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
719	| `dynamic_range` | string | No | `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`, in an HLG project. See [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range). |
720	| `encoder_speed` | string | No | `faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`, for AV1. See [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
721	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to export, as `get_project` reports it. Without it, the frontmost project. |
722	
723	It returns `{export_id, path, status}`. `path` is the file that will be written, with `~` expanded and the extension corrected. `status` is `running` if the job started at once, or `queued` if it's waiting.
724	
725	Jobs in the queue run one at a time, behind anything already there. A job writes the project as it stood when `export` was called, so later edits don't reach it. Calling `export` pauses playback in that project's window.
726	
727	`export` takes no `scope`. With a [nest](/mcp/nests/) open it still writes the project's timeline, not the nest's.
728	
729	## Export status
730	
731	`export_status` reports how a job is going, as its row in the Export Queue does, and it never waits. Pass the `export_id`, which is an integer of 1 or more.
732	
733	Every result carries `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or from then to the finish once the job has ended. The rest depends on the status.
734	
735	| `status` | Also carries |
736	| --- | --- |
737	| `queued` | `waiting` while an AV1 or VP9 job is held for memory. `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`. |
738	| `running` | `progress`, from 0 to 1. `phase` while the export names one, which is "Measuring loudness…" during the first pass over the mix. `estimated_seconds` on the same four presets. |
739	| `done` | What the file holds, in the next table. |
740	| `failed` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
741	| `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
742	
743	`estimated_seconds` is the export sheet's estimate of the whole export in whole seconds, and it's only an estimate.
744	
745	`waiting` is a sentence such as "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.1 GB of the 8.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 7.0 GB." AV1 and VP9 exports may hold a quarter of this Mac's memory between them, though a job with no other running always starts. While one is held, a later job in the queue may run first.
746	
747	A `done` result adds these keys.
748	
749	| Key | What it holds |
750	| --- | --- |
751	| `ok` | `true`. |
752	| `bytes` | The file's size. |
753	| `preset`, `container`, `codec` | What was written. |
754	| `width`, `height` | The file's size in pixels. These are reported on audio presets too, where they mean nothing. |
755	| `fps` | The rate as `[num, den]`, such as `[30, 1]`. |
756	| `start`, `duration` | The part of the timeline written, in [ticks](/mcp/units-and-ids/). |
757	| `burn_in_timecode` | Whether the argument was on. |
758	| `dynamic_range` | The picture written: `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. Only for a video preset in an HLG project. |
759	| `encoder_speed` | The speed used. Only on `av1` and `av1_webm`. |
760	| `audio_bits` | The depth written. Only on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. |
761	| `stems` | `[{name, tracks, path}]`, one per file beside the mix. Only when `stems` was asked for. |
762	| `loudness` | What the mix measured. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
763	| `graphic_warnings` | `[{name, frame, message}]`, each distinct warning a graphic gave while the file was drawn. Collecting stops after 64 distinct reports, so a noisy graphic's list can be cut short. `frame` is the graphic's own frame, or `null`. Absent when there were none. |
764	| `cursor_warnings` | `[{media, path, message}]`, each media whose cursor file couldn't be drawn. Its clips were written without a cursor. Absent when there were none. |
765	
766	## Cancel export
767	
768	`cancel_export` stops a job, as the row's **Cancel** does, and returns what `export_status` would. Pass the `export_id`.
769	
770	| The job is | What happens |
771	| --- | --- |
772	| Queued | It's cancelled before it starts. The result reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled before it started." |
773	| Running | It stops and its half-written file is removed. The result may still read `running` until writing has stopped, and `export_status` then reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled." |
774	| Finished | It's left alone, and its file stays. The result is the finished job's. |
775	
776	## Export id and its lifetime
777	
778	An `export_id` is known until Frame Job quits. Removing a finished row from the Export Queue, or choosing **Clear Finished**, doesn't lose it, so an agent can still read how that job ended.
779	
780	An id belongs to the launch, not to a project, so `export_status` and `cancel_export` don't need `project`. Only ids that `export` returned are known. A job a person queued from the sheet has no id an agent can follow. Any other number returns the error "No export this launch has export_id 7 — ids come from export and last until Frame Job quits."
781	
782	## Refusals and failures
783	
784	A problem Frame Job can see from the request comes back from `export` itself as an error, and nothing is queued.
785	
786	| The request | What stops it |
787	| --- | --- |
788	| An empty timeline | "There is nothing on the timeline to export." |
789	| A folder that doesn't exist | "There is no folder at … to write into." Frame Job never creates the folder. |
790	| An unknown preset | The error lists all the presets. |
791	| An unknown `size`, or one it can't read | The error lists the sizes. See [Size](#size). |
792	| `range` of `in_out` with no range set | "This project has no in/out range — set one with set_range `{start, end}`, or export with range \"project\"." |
793	| A number out of range, or a word it doesn't know | The error names the argument and the value. |
794	| An option the preset doesn't have | See [Audio bits](#audio-bits), [Stems](#stems), [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range) and [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
795	| A graphic clip in the range with no module, or a module that doesn't compile | "The export was not started: the graphic "…" does not compile — …. Fix the module and export again." A clip with no module reads "has no module in graphics/" in place of "does not compile — …". It names each graphic and its first error, and it covers graphics inside nests. An audio-only preset draws no graphics, so it isn't stopped by one. |
796	
797	Anything that goes wrong after that comes back from `export_status` as `failed`, with the sentence in `reason`. Check for it even when `export` answered cleanly.
798	
799	| What went wrong | The `reason` |
800	| --- | --- |
801	| A size of another shape on a transparent preset | "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…". See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets). |
802	| A stem's file would be one of the project's media | "The stem “…” would replace media this project uses; export under another name." |
803	| A graphic fails while it's drawn | "The export was stopped at frame … of the graphic "…": …. No file was written." |
804	| A retimed clip's sound, an isolated voice or a voice effect couldn't be rendered | The sentence names the clip and the reason. |
805	| A cut-out clip's masks couldn't be made | "Clip …'s person masks could not be made: …." A picture cut out by **Foreground** says foreground masks. |
806	| A clip's gate, leveller or de-esser needs a loudness that hasn't been measured | "Clip …'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…". Wait for the clip's analysis, then export again. |
807	| This Mac has no encoder for the preset | "This Mac cannot export with the “…” preset." |
808	
809	A graphic's warnings are different: they don't stop the export, and they arrive as `graphic_warnings` in the `done` result.
810	
811	## Presets
812	
813	There are 15 presets, one per encoding. A preset says nothing about size. These are the rows of the sheet's **Format** control, described in [Choose a format](/export/formats/). A wrong id's error lists them all.
814	
815	| Preset | In the sheet | File | Picture | Sound |
816	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
817	| `h264` | H.264 (MP4) | `.mp4` | 8-bit. The sheet's first row. | AAC |
818	| `hevc` | HEVC (MP4) | `.mp4` | 8-bit | AAC |
819	| `hevc_alpha` | HEVC with Alpha (MOV) | `.mov` | 8-bit with transparency. Safari's transparent movie. | AAC |
820	| `hevc_10bit` | HEVC 10-bit (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
821	| `av1` | AV1 (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
822	| `av1_webm` | AV1 (WebM) | `.webm` | 10-bit | Opus |
823	| `vp9_webm` | VP9 (WebM) | `.webm` | 8-bit (Profile 0) for an SDR picture, 10-bit (Profile 2) for HLG and PQ. One speed. | Opus |
824	| `vp9_alpha_webm` | VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | `.webm` | Always 8-bit, with transparency. The transparent movie Chrome and Firefox play. | Opus |
825	| `prores_422` | ProRes 422 (MOV) | `.mov` | 10-bit. An editing master. | 16-bit LPCM |
826	| `prores_4444` | ProRes 4444 (MOV) | `.mov` | 12-bit with transparency. A master. | 16-bit LPCM |
827	| `audio_m4a` | Audio only (M4A) | `.m4a` | None | AAC |
828	| `audio_wav` | Audio only (WAV) | `.wav` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
829	| `audio_aiff` | Audio only (AIFF) | `.aiff` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
830	| `gif` | Animated GIF | `.gif` | 256 colours. Fits inside 480 × 270 unless `size` says otherwise. | None |
831	| `apng` | Animated PNG | `.png` | Lossless, with transparency. Fits inside 960 × 540 unless `size` says otherwise. | None |
832	
833	Macs before M3 can't play `av1` and `av1_webm` back.
834	
835	## Frame rate
836	
837	There's no frame-rate argument, so the sheet's [frame rate](/export/frame-rate/) control has no agent equivalent. An export runs at the project's rate, `gif` at 12.5 fps and `apng` at 25 fps. The `done` result's `fps` says which, with 12.5 fps as `[25, 2]`.
838	
839	## Path handling
840	
841	The folder must exist. A `~` at the start is expanded, and an existing file at the path is replaced.
842	
843	The file always ends in the preset's extension.
844	
845	| `path` | `preset` | Writes | Why |
846	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
847	| `cut.mp4` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | The extension is already right. |
848	| `cut` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | With no extension, it's added. |
849	| `cut.mov` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | A different media extension is replaced. |
850	| `Talk v1.2` | `h264` | `Talk v1.2.mp4` | Any other suffix stays part of the name. |
851	| `cut.webm` | `h264` | `cut.webm.mp4` | `.webm` isn't one of the extensions Frame Job replaces. |
852	| `cut.mp4` | `av1_webm` | `cut.webm` | `.mp4` is. |
853	
854	The extensions it replaces are `.mov`, `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.m4a`, `.mp3`, `.wav`, `.aif`, `.aiff`, `.caf`, `.framejob`, `.srt`, `.vtt`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.heic` and `.gif`. The returned `path` is always the file that gets written.
855	
856	## Size
857	
858	`size` is the sheet's **Size** control. See [Export size](/export/size/) for what the sizes mean to a person.
859	
860	| `size` | In the sheet | What it writes |
861	| --- | --- | --- |
862	| `document` | Document size | The project's own size. The default on every movie preset. |
863	| `2160p` | 4K | A short edge of 2160 pixels. |
864	| `1440p` | 1440p | A short edge of 1440 pixels. |
865	| `1080p` | 1080p | A short edge of 1080 pixels. |
866	| `720p` | 720p | A short edge of 720 pixels. |
867	| `preset` | GIF default, APNG default | The format's cap. `gif` and `apng` only, where it's the default. |
868	| `[width, height]` | Custom… | Exactly this size, from 16 to 8192 pixels on each edge. |
869	
870	The number is always the short edge, and the long edge follows the project's shape, rounded to an even number. A vertical project's `1080p` is 1080 × 1920. Every size means the same on every project, so a 1920 × 1080 project's `1080p` is its own size, and a size larger than the project scales it up.
871	
872	A movie is written at exactly the size asked for. If the shape differs from the project's by more than a pixel, the picture is letterboxed. Within a pixel, it fills the frame instead.
873	
874	- **Even edges.** Every preset but `prores_4444`, `gif` and `apng` needs even dimensions, so an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller. That covers `document` on a project with an odd edge. The `done` result's `width` and `height` are the file's.
875	- **GIF and APNG.** A size is a box the picture is fitted inside, keeping its shape and never scaling up. A vertical 1080 × 1920 project's GIF default comes out at 152 × 270.
876	- **Audio presets.** A size has no effect, and `preset` isn't one of their sizes.
877	- **Transparent movies.** A `[width, height]` of another shape fails. See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets).
878	
879	An unknown size returns an error with the list, for example "No export size is called "480p" for h264. The sizes are: document, 2160p, 1440p, 1080p, 720p — or pass [width, height]." A custom size outside 16 to 8192 pixels is an error too. It isn't clamped.
880	
881	## Range
882	
883	`range` is the sheet's **Range** control. `project`, the default, writes the whole timeline. `in_out` writes the range set with `set_range`, and `export` returns an error when there's no range. See [Export a range](/export/range/).
884	
885	The range is snapped to the export's frame grid and kept inside the project. A range that comes to nothing is an error too.
886	
887	`burn_in_timecode` shows project time even in a range export, so a file written from 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 with a burn-in that reads 00:00:10:00.
888	
889	## Exact bitrates
890	
891	The sheet offers [quality](/export/quality/) tiers. An agent sets the rates directly, in bits per second, so 8 Mbps is `8000000`. Each must be a whole number from 1 to 4,294,967,295.
892	
893	`video_bitrate` is the target video rate. Without it, Frame Job works out a rate from the frame size and frame rate. ProRes, GIF and APNG ignore it, because ProRes is fixed by its profile and the other two have no bitrate.
894	
895	On the AV1 and VP9 presets it works differently:
896	
897	- **`av1` and `av1_webm`.** It's a soft cap. The encoder works at a constant quality matched to HEVC at that rate, and the file usually comes in well under it. Very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over. Without it, the quality is matched to HEVC at 0.07 bits per pixel per frame.
898	- **`vp9_webm`.** It's a soft cap too, matched to HEVC, or HEVC 10-bit in an HDR export. Up to about 1.15 times over was measured.
899	- **`vp9_alpha_webm`.** It's the same soft cap on the picture's stream alone. The transparency's stream comes on top, at a constant quality.
900	
901	`audio_bitrate` is the AAC or Opus rate, 192 kbps when absent. Opus takes the nearest rate its encoder offers. ProRes, WAV and AIFF ignore it, because they write LPCM.
902	
903	## The loudness report
904	
905	Every export with sound measures its own mix and reports it as `loudness` in the `done` result, normalised or not. GIF and APNG have no sound, and a timeline with no sound has nothing to measure, so `loudness` is absent from both.
906	
907	`loudness_lufs` normalises the whole mix to an integrated loudness, from −70 to 0. The sheet's [Loudness](/export/loudness/) rows are −14 for streaming, −16 for podcasts and −23 for EBU R 128 broadcast, and an agent can ask for any value, such as −14.5. The export measures itself first, then applies one gain to everything, through the master limiter. The file lands on the target with its loudest peaks limited, rather than the whole mix held down. GIF and APNG ignore it.
908	
909	| Key | What it holds |
910	| --- | --- |
911	| `summary` | The same line the queue row and the progress sheet show, such as "Peak −1.0 dBTP · −16.0 LUFS", with " · peaks limited by 8.6 dB" when the limiter took 0.05 dB or more. |
912	| `integrated_lufs` | The file's integrated loudness. Absent when it has none, and `summary` then says "loudness not measurable". |
913	| `true_peak_dbtp` | The file's true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
914	| `sample_peak_dbfs` | The file's sample peak, never above the true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
915	| `gain_db` | The gain applied to reach the target. |
916	| `ceiling_dbtp` | The master limiter's ceiling. |
917	| `limited_db` | How far the limiter turned the loudest peak down. |
918	| `capped_by_gain` | `true` when the +40 dB limit on the gain decided it, so the file may be short of the target. |
919	| `target_lufs` | The `loudness_lufs` asked for. Absent when none was. |
920	
921	A programme shorter than one 400 ms measuring block, or one too quiet to pass the standard's gate, has a peak and no integrated loudness. Digital silence reads "Silent" in `summary`.
922	
923	## Peak dBTP
924	
925	Every export with sound goes through a master limiter, so the file's true peak stays at or under a ceiling. `peak_dbtp` sets that ceiling, from −20 to 0. It's −1 when absent, which is the sheet's fixed value. 0 is the loosest, and there's no way to turn the limiter off.
926	
927	You can pass it with or without `loudness_lufs`. `limited_db` in the [report](#the-loudness-report) says how far the limiter turned the loudest peak down.
928	
929	## Audio bits
930	
931	`audio_bits` is the sheet's [Bit depth](/export/bit-depth/) control: 16, the default, or 24. It's rounded once from the mix and never dithered, and the `done` result repeats it.
932	
933	It works on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only. On any other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no bit depth; audio_bits applies to audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset. ProRes keeps 16-bit sound. Any other number is an error, whatever the preset.
934	
935	## Stems
936	
937	`stems` also writes [stems](/export/stems/) beside the mix, on `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. It's the sheet's **Stems** control.
938	
939	| `stems` | What it writes |
940	| --- | --- |
941	| `tracks` | One file per heard track. |
942	| `names` | One file per track name. Heard tracks whose names match, ignoring case, share a file, and an unnamed track gets its own. |
943	
944	A track is heard when it has sound in it and isn't muted or silenced by another track's solo. Each stem is named `<file> - <track name>.<ext>`, beside the mix, so `mix.wav` and a track called Voice give `mix - Voice.wav`. An unnamed track is `Track N`, and [Stem file names](/export/stems/#stem-file-names) has the other cases.
945	
946	A stem holds its tracks' sound before the master, with no loudness gain and no limiter, so the stems add up to the mix wherever the master changed nothing. Any file already at a stem's name is replaced.
947	
948	The `done` result lists each one as `stems [{name, tracks, path}]`. `tracks` holds the ids of the timeline tracks in that stem.
949	
950	- On any other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no stems; stems applies to audio_m4a, audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset.
951	- With no track heard, the error is "stems: no track is heard, so there is no stem to write".
952	- If a stem's file would be one of the project's media, the job fails before any stem is written, and `export_status` gives the reason.
953	- A failed or cancelled job leaves neither the mix nor any stem behind.
954	
955	## Dynamic range
956	
957	`dynamic_range` chooses the picture an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/) writes. It's the sheet's **Dynamic Range** control.
958	
959	| `dynamic_range` | What it writes |
960	| --- | --- |
961	| `hlg` | BT.2100 HLG, with no Dolby Vision. The default on the presets that carry HDR. |
962	| `pq` | HDR10: BT.2100 PQ at 1,000 cd/m², with a P3-D65 mastering display of 0.005–1,000 cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000 and MaxFALL 0. |
963	| `sdr` | The project's SDR version. |
964	
965	The presets that carry HDR are `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444`. Every other video preset in an HLG project writes the SDR version, `vp9_alpha_webm` included, and audio presets ignore the argument.
966	
967	- `hlg` or `pq` on another video preset returns the error "h264 is 8-bit and writes the SDR version; export dynamic_range "pq" as hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 or prores_4444".
968	- `hlg` or `pq` in an SDR project returns the error "dynamic_range "pq" needs an HLG project; set_canvas output "hlg" first".
969	- `sdr` in an SDR project changes nothing.
970	
971	Once a job is `done`, `dynamic_range` in the result names the picture that was written. An SDR project's result has no such key.
972	
973	## Encoder speed
974	
975	`encoder_speed` trades export time for file size on `av1` and `av1_webm`. It's the sheet's [Speed](/export/encoder-speed/) control, and the `done` result names the one used.
976	
977	| `encoder_speed` | SVT-AV1 preset | What it does |
978	| --- | --- | --- |
979	| `faster` | 8 | The quickest. |
980	| `balanced` | 6 | The default. |
981	| `smaller` | 4 | The smallest file for the picture, and the slowest. |
982	
983	On every other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm", naming the preset. That includes `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`, which have one speed.
984	
985	## Transparent presets
986	
987	Four presets keep a transparent canvas transparent: `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`, `vp9_alpha_webm` and `apng`. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). A GIF can show a fully transparent pixel, but it has no alpha channel, so nothing partial survives.
988	
989	On the three movie presets, a `[width, height]` of a different shape from the canvas can't be written, because the padding would destroy the alpha channel. `export` queues the job, and `export_status` then reads `failed` with a reason that names both sizes. The shape is judged after an odd edge is evened, and within a pixel the picture fills the frame, so a size in the canvas's own proportions always works, at any scale. Every named size already has the canvas's shape.
990	
991	`apng` fits its picture inside the size instead, so this doesn't apply to it.

7	
8	Frame Job serves its whole editor as MCP tools, so an AI agent such as Claude Code can open projects, cut, style, check its work frame by frame and export, as you do in the window. MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is the open standard that gives an AI agent tools it can call.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ MCP"
12	  needs="An MCP client, such as Claude Code."
13	/>
14	
15	## The whole editor as tools
16	
17	A shipped Frame Job publishes 125 tools. Every edit you can make in the window has one, and the rest cover what sits around an edit: opening and saving projects, moving the playhead, reading the project, rendering a frame, exporting. [All tools](/mcp/tools/) lists them.
18	
19	An agent's edit goes through the same place your own clicks go. It shows in the window at once, marks the project as edited, and is one undo step you can take back with <kbd>⌘Z</kbd>.
20	
21	A tool checks what it's given before it does anything. If it gets an argument it doesn't take, it stops, names that argument and lists what it does take, so a model can read the reply and correct itself. [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/) has the rest.
22	
23	To connect a client, see [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).
24	
25	## The framejob-mcp helper
26	
27	Most MCP clients start a small server of their own and talk to it over standard input and output. For them, the app carries one:
28	
29	```
30	Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp
31	```
32	
33	It's called `framejob-mcp`, and it's the way a client such as Claude Code connects. There's no runtime to install. The client starts the helper, and the helper reaches Frame Job over a [local socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#the-local-agent-socket), a private connection point that exists only on your Mac.
34	
35	The helper does three things beyond passing messages along: it answers a client that's starting up, it [lists the tools when Frame Job can't](#the-tool-list-with-frame-job-closed), and it [opens Frame Job on the first tool call](#opening-on-the-first-tool-call).
36	
37	Register it at its path inside the app. Anywhere else it can't open Frame Job or list the tools while Frame Job is closed. See [The helper stays in the bundle](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#the-helper-stays-in-the-bundle).
38	
39	## The tool list with Frame Job closed
40	
41	Starting an MCP client never opens the video editor. The helper answers the client's first messages itself, so a session starts with nothing on screen, and asking for the tool list never launches Frame Job either.
42	
43	When a client asks for the tool list, the helper asks the running app first. It falls back to a copy of the list stored in the app when:
44	
45	- Frame Job isn't running.
46	- Frame Job doesn't answer within 5 seconds, for example because another client's long call is holding it.
47	
48	So a client always sees every tool, and if the stored list turns out to differ from the running app's, [the helper says so](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#tool-list-changes).
49	
50	## Opening on the first tool call
51	
52	If a tool call finds Frame Job not running, the helper launches its own copy of the app in the background and waits for it. The app doesn't come to the front. Once it's listening, the call runs as usual.
53	
54	- The helper waits up to 60 seconds. See [The launch wait](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#the-launch-wait), and [Failed launches](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#failed-launches) for what happens when that runs out.
55	- Several clients calling at once start only one copy.
56	- This also happens if you quit Frame Job in the middle of a session: the next tool call opens it again.
57	
58	## Who can connect
59	
60	Only programs running under your own account can connect, and any of them can while Frame Job is running. There's no password or per-client approval, and no network port, so nothing on another machine can reach it.
61	
62	The permissions on the socket (`0600`) and its folder (`0700`) are the whole of this protection, so Frame Job is strict about them. If they're wrong it doesn't open the socket at all. See [The socket's folder and permissions](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#the-sockets-folder-and-permissions).
63	
64	## Assistant rules do not bind an MCP client
65	
66	The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) inside Frame Job works under rules of its own. It can't call some tools, and it asks you before it calls others. Those rules belong to the Assistant, not to the tools. A client connected over MCP calls every tool directly, and nothing asks you first.
67	
68	| Tool | The Assistant | An MCP client |
69	| --- | --- | --- |
70	| `record_screen`, `close_project`, `transcribe_for_fillers` | Can't call it | Calls it directly |
71	| `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine | Can't call it | Calls it directly |
72	| `export`, `export_captions`, `save_project`, `consolidate_media`, `export_graphic` | Asks you first | Calls it directly |
73	| `new_project_from_range`, `make_vertical_version` when the call names a path | Asks you first | Calls it directly |
74	
75	So a connected agent can spend your AssemblyAI credit, or replace a file with an export, without a question from Frame Job. Any check on that has to come from your MCP client.
76	
77	## Settings has no tool
78	
79	No MCP tool reads or writes anything in [Settings](/reference/settings/). An agent can't set a key, the Assistant's model, the AssemblyAI region or Background render, and no tool reports their values. Only a person sets those, in **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>).
80	
81	An agent's cloud tools do use what's saved there. `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine and `transcribe_for_fillers` send with your key and region, so you have to set the key first. Without one they stop with "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." The key never appears in a result, but `transcribe` does name the server a run's requests went to, and that server shows the region.
82	
83	## Good to know
84	
85	- Calls run one at a time, across every connected client and the Assistant, so a long call holds the next one until it ends.
86	- A tool call never asks you anything. Anything that needs a question answered or a system permission granted has to be done by a person first. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).

99	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
100	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
101	
102	An MCP client connects to Frame Job through `framejob-mcp`, a helper inside the app. You register the helper once, and Frame Job's tools are there whenever the client runs.
103	
104	<AtAGlance
105	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
106	  keys="⌘,"
107	  where="The MCP section, at the top of Settings"
108	  needs="An MCP client that starts a stdio server, such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop."
109	/>
110	
111	## Connect Claude Code
112	
113	<Steps>
114	
115	1. Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>). The **MCP** section is at the top.
116	
117	2. Choose **Copy MCP Command**. The section reads "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press Return."
118	
119	3. Paste the command into Terminal and press <kbd>Return</kbd>.
120	
121	</Steps>
122	
123	For a copy of Frame Job in `/Applications`, the command is:
124	
125	```sh
126	claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'
127	```
128	
129	`--scope user` makes Frame Job's tools available in every Claude Code project.
130	
131	Frame Job doesn't have to be open. Claude Code can start and list the tools with the app closed, and the first tool call [opens it in the background](/mcp/overview/#opening-on-the-first-tool-call).
132	
133	## Claude Desktop and other stdio clients
134	
135	Any MCP client that starts a stdio server, one it talks to over standard input and output, can use the same helper, by its path. Copy MCP Command writes the Claude Code command only, so for anything else you enter the path by hand.
136	
137	For Claude Desktop, add it to `claude_desktop_config.json`:
138	
139	```json
140	{
141	  "mcpServers": {
142	    "framejob": {
143	      "command": "/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp"
144	    }
145	  }
146	}
147	```
148	
149	If your copy of Frame Job lives somewhere else, use [the path Settings shows](#the-helper-path-in-settings). A client that can speak HTTP over a Unix socket can skip the helper and [connect directly](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#streamable-http-over-the-socket).
150	
151	## The MCP section in Settings
152	
153	**MCP** is the first of the sections in Settings. From top to bottom it holds two short paragraphs on how a client reaches Frame Job, the helper's path, **Copy MCP Command** and a status line.
154	
155	### The helper path in Settings
156	
157	The section shows the full path of `framejob-mcp` inside the copy of Frame Job you're running, ending `Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp`. You can select it and copy it.
158	
159	### Copy MCP Command
160	
161	**Copy MCP Command** puts the Claude Code command for this copy of Frame Job on the clipboard, with the path filled in and quoted for the shell. It always names the helper inside the copy you opened Settings from, so a copy in `~/Applications` or a build folder registers itself.
162	
163	The path doesn't follow the app. If you move Frame Job, copy the command again and register the new path.
164	
165	The button isn't an edit, so no agent tool does the same thing.
166	
167	### The missing helper warning
168	
169	If the helper is missing from this copy of Frame Job, or can't be run, **Copy MCP Command** is dimmed and the status line reads "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job."
170	
171	Frame Job checks each time Settings opens. If the helper disappears while the window is open, pressing the button copies nothing and shows the same line.
172	
173	## Testing a second copy
174	
175	This is for testing, not everyday use. Setting the environment variable `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` to a path moves the socket there, so a test copy of Frame Job stays apart from your everyday one. Set it for both Frame Job and `framejob-mcp`.
176	
177	Setting it for the helper alone is often enough. When a tool call finds nothing at that path, the helper launches the copy it belongs to and passes the path on. See [A custom socket path](/mcp/helper-and-socket/#a-custom-socket-path) for the rules.
178	
179	To start a test copy yourself, run its executable from Terminal with the variable set:
180	
181	```sh
182	RC_AGENT_SOCKET="$HOME/framejob-test/agent.sock" '/path/to/Frame Job.app/Contents/MacOS/Frame Job'
183	```

192	title: The helper and the socket
193	description: How framejob-mcp reaches Frame Job, what it launches and how long it waits, the local socket and its permissions, and what each error means.
194	---
195	
196	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
197	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
198	
199	This page is the detail behind the connection: what the helper will and won't launch, how the socket is guarded, and what to read when a client can't get through. To set up a client, see [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).
200	
201	<AtAGlance
202	  where={['Helper: Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp', 'Socket: ~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock']}
203	/>
204	
205	## The helper stays in the bundle
206	
207	The helper launches only the Frame Job it belongs to, so each copy of the app opens itself and never another copy. Always register it at its path inside the app.
208	
209	A helper moved out of the app can neither read the stored tool list nor launch Frame Job. A client can still start a session with it, but asking for the tool list returns an error when no Frame Job is running, and a tool call that finds no Frame Job fails with a message naming the executable:
210	
211	```
212	framejob-mcp is not inside a Frame Job bundle: <path> is not <X>.app/Contents/Helpers/<name>, so there is no Frame Job to launch
213	```
214	
215	The helper doesn't check which copy answers on the socket. If you have two copies of Frame Job and one is already running, the other's helper talks to the running one.
216	
217	## The local agent socket
218	
219	Frame Job opens a local Unix socket every time it launches, at:
220	
221	```
222	~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock
223	```
224	
225	There's no switch to turn it on or off, and no network port. See [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/) for the folders around it.
226	
227	### The socket's folder and permissions
228	
229	The socket sits in the `Agent` folder, and those permissions are its only protection. The folder is `0700` and the socket is `0600`, so only programs running as you can open it. Frame Job makes the folder that way when it's missing.
230	
231	The folder has to be a real folder, not a symlink. It has to be owned by you, with no permissions for group or others. If it isn't, Frame Job reports the problem in the [log](#socket-status-in-the-log) and doesn't open the socket. It never loosens or repairs the folder itself, so wrong permissions are yours to fix.
232	
233	### Streamable HTTP over the socket
234	
235	The socket serves MCP as streamable HTTP, so a client that can speak HTTP over a Unix socket can connect directly, without the helper.
236	
237	Each request is one JSON-RPC `POST /mcp`, and the reply is a single JSON response. There's no event stream and no session id.
238	
239	| The client sends | The reply |
240	| --- | --- |
241	| Any HTTP method but `POST` | HTTP 405 |
242	| A request body over 8 MiB | HTTP 413 |
243	| A message that isn't JSON | HTTP 400 with error `-32700` |
244	| A notification | HTTP 202 with no body |
245	| A batch | A JSON array with a reply for each request in it. Notifications get no entry, and a batch of only notifications gets HTTP 202. The helper, by contrast, doesn't take batches. |
246	
247	A direct client gets none of the helper's help. It has no stored tool list, and nothing launches Frame Job for it.
248	
249	### One copy holds the socket
250	
251	With several copies of Frame Job open, the first owns the socket. A later copy finds another one already listening, leaves the socket alone and doesn't open its own. The later copy works normally in its window, but no agent can reach it.
252	
253	If the file at the path isn't a socket at all, Frame Job leaves that alone too, and opens nothing.
254	
255	### Stale socket cleanup
256	
257	A socket file left behind by a copy that crashed is removed and replaced automatically. Only a socket that responds counts as another copy, so a leftover never stops the next launch.
258	
259	### The socket released at quit
260	
261	Quitting removes the socket file if it's still this copy's. A tool call in flight can't hold up the quit.
262	
263	### Socket status in the log
264	
265	A launch that can't open the socket logs why and carries on, with no dialog. Frame Job works as usual, and no agent can reach that copy. Look in the Console app for a line starting "Frame Job agent socket".
266	
267	| The log says | What it means |
268	| --- | --- |
269	| `Frame Job agent socket listening at <path>` | The socket is open. |
270	| `… not bound: another instance answers at <path>; this one binds none` | [Another copy](#one-copy-holds-the-socket) holds the socket. |
271	| `… not bound: <folder> is mode 0755; the socket's folder must be its owner's alone (0700)` | The folder lets someone else in. The mode shown is the one it has. |
272	| `… not bound: <folder> is not a folder (a symlink is refused)` | The folder is a symlink. |
273	| `… not bound: could not make the folder <folder>: <reason>` | The folder is missing and can't be made, or a file is in its place. |
274	| `… not bound: <folder> is owned by uid 501, not this user (502)` | Someone else owns the folder. |
275	| `… not bound: <path> exists and is not a socket; it is left alone` | Something else is at the socket's path. Frame Job won't delete it. |
276	| `… not bound: socket path is 110 bytes; macOS allows 103: <path>` | A [custom path](#a-custom-socket-path) is too long. |
277	| `… not bound: socket path must be absolute: <path>` | A custom path doesn't start at the root. |
278	
279	### A custom socket path
280	
281	The environment variable `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` moves the socket, for both the app and the helper. It's for [testing a second copy](/mcp/connect-a-client/#testing-a-second-copy).
282	
283	- The path must be absolute, and at most 103 bytes. That's a macOS limit.
284	- An empty value means the default path.
285	- The path's folder follows the same [rules](#the-sockets-folder-and-permissions) as the default one. A folder that already exists with mode `0755` won't do. A missing folder is made with the right mode.
286	- Only the socket moves. The test copy still shares your everyday copy's preferences.
287	
288	When the helper launches Frame Job for a custom socket, it passes the path on, tells macOS not to restore the app's windows from last time, and writes the app's error output to `framejob-launch.log` beside the socket. A launch for your own socket does none of this, so your Frame Job opens as yours.
289	
290	## When the helper launches Frame Job
291	
292	The helper launches Frame Job when a [tool call finds nothing listening](/mcp/overview/#opening-on-the-first-tool-call). It runs `open -n -g` on its own app, so the app stays in the background. Nothing else launches it: not a client starting up, not `ping`, not a request for the tool list.
293	
294	### One launch between several clients
295	
296	Two clients that both find no Frame Job launch one copy between them, not two. A lock file, `agent.launch.lock`, sits beside the socket, and the helper holds it until the launched copy responds or the wait ends. Another helper waiting on that lock looks again once it gets it, and finds the copy already running.
297	
298	Calls made at the same moment in one client session also launch at most once.
299	
300	### The launch wait
301	
302	The helper waits up to 60 seconds for a launched Frame Job to start listening. To change that, set the environment variable `RC_MCP_LAUNCH_WAIT` for the helper to a positive whole number of seconds. Any other value means 60.
303	
304	### Failed launches
305	
306	If a launched Frame Job never starts listening, the call fails with:
307	
308	```
309	Frame Job did not answer at <socket> within 60 s of launching <bundle>
310	```
311	
312	That client session then stops launching. While nothing responds on the socket, its later calls fail with the same message with this added, and start no more copies:
313	
314	```
315	that instance may still be running, so this session will not launch another — quit it and check <folder>
316	```
317	
318	One cause is the socket's folder: a copy that can't open the socket keeps running in the background and [logs why](#socket-status-in-the-log). To recover:
319	
320	<Steps>
321	
322	1. Quit the stray copy of Frame Job.
323	
324	2. Check the folder the message names, and the log.
325	
326	3. Open Frame Job yourself, or start a new client session. The session that failed won't launch again, but it does use a Frame Job that's already listening.
327	
328	</Steps>
329	
330	## While a client is connected
331	
332	Once a session is running, the helper passes calls to Frame Job and reports what goes wrong.
333	
334	### Long calls are never timed out
335	
336	A forwarded tool call can take as long as it needs, so a long recording or analysis is never cut off by the helper. Only the helper's own request for the tool list has a limit, the [5 seconds](/mcp/overview/#the-tool-list-with-frame-job-closed) before it falls back to the stored list.
337	
338	A `ping` gets a reply even while a long call holds the app, because the helper handles it itself.
339	
340	If the client closes, the helper exits at once, without waiting for a call in flight.
341	
342	### Errors from the helper
343	
344	A call the helper couldn't deliver comes back as an ordinary tool result with `isError: true` and a plain sentence, so a model can read it.
345	
346	| The result says | What it means |
347	| --- | --- |
348	| `could not connect to Frame Job at <path>: <reason>` | The socket is there but can't be reached, for example because of its permissions. |
349	| `/usr/bin/open <bundle> failed (<status>): <reason>` | macOS couldn't launch the app. |
350	| `Frame Job did not answer at <socket> within …` | See [Failed launches](#failed-launches). |
351	| `could not read Frame Job's answer at <path>: the answer is over 8 MiB` | The helper won't read a reply larger than 8 MiB. |
352	| `HOME is not set, so the agent socket's path is unknown` | The helper started with no home folder in its environment, and no custom path. |
353	
354	Other failures are JSON-RPC errors:
355	
356	| Code | When |
357	| --- | --- |
358	| `-32700` | The line isn't JSON. The reply has a null id. |
359	| `-32600` | The message is a batch or isn't a JSON object, and the reply has a null id. A method that isn't a string gets this too. |
360	| `-32601` | Frame Job isn't responding and the method is one the helper can't handle itself, or Frame Job doesn't know the method. |
361	| `-32603` | The tool list couldn't be read from the app or from the stored copy, `Contents/Resources/agent-catalog.json`, and the message names both reasons. A forwarded method whose reply couldn't be read gets this too. |
362	
363	The helper passes any method but `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call` to the app when it responds. Notifications and responses from a client are dropped and never forwarded.
364	
365	The helper's standard output carries protocol only. Everything else it says goes to standard error, each line starting `framejob-mcp: `, so that's where to look in a client's logs.
366	
367	### Protocol versions
368	
369	Frame Job speaks three MCP protocol revisions: `2024-11-05`, `2025-03-26` and `2025-06-18`. It uses the revision a client asks for, or `2025-06-18` if it asks for any other. The app and the helper work from the same list.
370	
371	The helper's reply to `initialize` names the server `framejob`, gives the version of the Frame Job it belongs to, and declares tools with `listChanged`. A direct connection to the socket declares tools without it, because only the helper sends that notice.
372	
373	### Tool list changes
374	
375	A list from the stored copy can differ from the running app's, for example when another copy of Frame Job holds the socket. So after a client gets the stored list, or after a launch, the helper asks the app for its list following the next forwarded call. If it differs from what the client was last given, the helper sends `notifications/tools/list_changed` and the client can read it again.
376	
377	The lists are compared by their content, so a difference in key order doesn't count.

387	title: How tool calls behave
388	description: What to expect while an agent works in Frame Job. Calls run one at a time, wait for your drag, never put up a question, make one undo step each, and show in the window at once.
389	---
390	
391	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
392	
393	A tool call is one request from an AI agent connected to Frame Job, such as splitting a clip or reading the project. Every call follows the same rules, whichever client sends it. This page says what an agent can rely on, and what you'll see if you work in the window while it does.
394	
395	<AtAGlance
396	  menu={['Edit ▸ Undo', 'Edit ▸ Redo']}
397	  keys={['⌘Z', '⇧⌘Z']}
398	  tools={['undo', 'redo', 'close_project', 'import_media', 'relink_media', 'open_project', 'record_screen', 'get_media_analysis', 'split_at_shots', 'switch_by_speaker', 'reframe_clip', 'make_vertical_version']}
399	/>
400	
401	## Edits show live
402	
403	An agent's edit goes through the same place your own clicks go. It shows in the window at once, marks the document as edited, and can be undone with <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> like anything you did yourself. Frame Job doesn't need to be the active app for any of this.
404	
405	## One call at a time
406	
407	Frame Job runs one tool call at a time, across every connected client and the [Assistant](/assistant/chat/). A call that arrives while another is running waits its turn. It doesn't fail.
408	
409	So a long call holds up the ones behind it. The usual long calls are `record_screen`, which runs for as long as it records, `transcribe`, and an analysis call, which can wait up to [60 seconds](#analysis-tools-wait-60-seconds-then-resume). `export` isn't one of them: it answers straight away and works in the background. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).
410	
411	A question the Assistant is waiting for you to answer doesn't hold up an MCP client, or the Assistant in another window. It's asked before the call joins the queue.
412	
413	While a long call runs, a client's request for the tool list can't reach Frame Job either. [`framejob-mcp`](/mcp/helper-and-socket/) waits 5 seconds, then answers from its own copy of the list.
414	
415	## Calls wait for your drag
416	
417	A call made while you're dragging a clip, a canvas handle or an inspector slider, in any open project, waits until you let go of the mouse. It then runs as its own undo step, after the drag's.
418	
419	There's no time limit on this wait. The call, and every call queued behind it, waits for as long as you hold the mouse button down.
420	
421	## A tool call never asks
422	
423	A tool call never puts up an alert or asks for a permission, so a call can't get stuck behind a question nobody can see. Where the app would stop and ask you, the call comes back with a message instead.
424	
425	| In the window, Frame Job… | A tool call… |
426	| --- | --- |
427	| Offers to convert a file with ffmpeg | Treats the offer as declined |
428	| Prompts for a system permission | Is refused, saying where to give it |
429	| Asks whether to save a project you're closing | Is refused unless it passes `discard: true` |
430	| Asks before removing a track that holds clips | Is refused, naming `with_clips: true` |
431	| Asks before a speed past ×12 drops the sound | Goes ahead, and the answer lists the clips under `audio_left_out` with an `audio_note` |
432	
433	An edit that fails comes back as a message too. The beep or alert sheet you'd get in the window never appears. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
434	
435	Anything that needs a question answered or a permission given has to be done by a person first. The rule belongs to the call, not to the app: `import_media`, `relink_media`, `open_project` and `record_screen` never ask, but if you add a file yourself while one of them runs, you still get the question.
436	
437	:::note
438	This is the rule for clients connected over MCP. The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) works under rules of its own, and asks you in its tab before it calls certain tools.
439	:::
440	
441	### The ffmpeg offer is declined
442	
443	An agent's import never shows the ffmpeg question. Unless you've chosen to convert automatically, the file is refused with the reason. If ffmpeg is installed, the message also says how to get past it. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#with-an-agent).
444	
445	### System grants are refused, never requested
446	
447	`record_screen` never asks for the Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera or Input Monitoring grant, and never opens the picker or System Settings. A missing grant is refused, and the message names the System Settings pane. If macOS hasn't asked about the microphone or camera yet, the message says to press **Record** in **File ▸ New Recording…** once, so that a person can give the grant from the recorder panel. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
448	
449	A Frame Job started from a terminal runs under the terminal's grants, not the app's. The refusal then also names the launching process and the way out: relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"`, or give the terminal the grant.
450	
451	### Closing a project refuses rather than asks
452	
453	`close_project` won't close a project with unsaved changes, and nothing is written:
454	
455	> Interview has unsaved changes, so close_project left it open: save_project saves them, or close_project with discard: true closes it and loses them.
456	
457	Nor will it close a window with a sheet open, even with `discard: true`:
458	
459	> Interview has a sheet open on its window, so close_project left it open: finish or cancel the sheet first.
460	
461	## Which project a call acts on
462	
463	Every tool takes an optional `project`: the path of an open project, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out and the call goes to the frontmost open project, by window order, whether or not Frame Job is the active app.
464	
465	| Situation | What happens |
466	| --- | --- |
467	| The path is an open project's | The call acts on it. `~` is expanded, and different spellings of one path match. |
468	| The path names no open project | "No open project is at *path*. get_project reports the open project's path; open_project opens another." |
469	| `project` is left out and no project is open | "No project is open. Call open_project or new_project first." |
470	
471	A movie opened as a project is addressed by the movie's path. A project that has never been saved and didn't come from a file has no path, so `get_project` reports `null` and only the frontmost-project rule can reach it.
472	
473	The Assistant's calls are held to its own window's project. A `project` naming any other is refused.
474	
475	To edit inside a nest, most tools that edit also take `scope`. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
476	
477	## One call, one undo step
478	
479	Every tool that edits the project makes exactly one undo step, however many clips it touched. So `undo` takes back exactly one call, and the step's name in the **Edit** menu is the name the tool gives it, such as "Split at Shot Changes".
480	
481	`undo` and `redo` walk the same history as <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> and <kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd>, so they take back the last step whoever made it. Each answers the step's name, `can_undo`, `can_redo` and the project summary, and it's an error when there's nothing to walk back. Any new edit clears the redo history.
482	
483	Some tools make no step:
484	
485	- **View state:** `set_playhead`, `set_range`, `set_selection` and `set_scope` change what the window shows, not the project.
486	- **Reads:** a tool that only answers, such as `get_project` or `detect_silence`, changes nothing. So does a call that made no change, which is [safe to retry](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/#a-no-change-answer).
487	- **File writes in the graphics folder:** `write_graphic`, `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset`, `delete_graphic`, `restore_graphic` and `import_graphic` can't be undone, and each tool says so. See [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/).
488	
489	## Analysis tools wait 60 seconds, then resume
490	
491	Some tools need Frame Job to analyse a file first, on your Mac. A call waits at most 60 seconds for that, and the others wait behind it. What was analysed is kept in the project's cache, so calling again carries on from there and a part already analysed answers at once.
492	
493	What happens at 60 seconds depends on the tool:
494	
495	| Tool | Past 60 seconds |
496	| --- | --- |
497	| `get_media_analysis` | Refused, saying how much was covered: "The faces analysis of media 12 covered 41.0 s of the window's 120.0 s in the 60 s a call waits; what it covered is kept — call again to continue." |
498	| `split_at_shots` | Refused: "The shots analysis of media 12 did not finish in the 60 s a call waits; what it covered is kept — call split_at_shots again to continue." Nothing is split. |
499	| `switch_by_speaker` | The same, for the faces analysis. It only waits when one microphone is shared by two or more cameras. |
500	| `reframe_clip`, `make_vertical_version` | Not refused. The call answers `ok: true`, an `analyzing` object and a `note`, makes no edit, and the analysis carries on without it. Call again to apply. |
501	
502	`analyzing` holds `media`, the ids still being analysed, and `covered`, the share done from 0 to 1.
503	
504	`analyze_cutout` works differently. It waits for as many seconds as its `wait` says, from 0 to 60, and answers the state it reached. It's never refused for time.
505	
506	Keep `get_media_analysis` answers small on long media. An answer over 512 KiB is refused, naming the largest `to` that fits, so read faces and subjects in `from` and `to` windows of about 2 minutes. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
507	
508	## Calls and Background render
509	
510	An MCP call counts as activity when it edits a project or moves a playhead, so it stops [Background render](/graphics/playback-and-memory/#what-stops-background-render), which starts again after its usual wait. A call that only reads, such as `get_project`, doesn't count.

520	title: Units and ids
521	description: The units an agent's arguments are written in. Times in ticks, ids, track order, colours, booleans, keys that must be sent, list arguments and speed rates.
522	---
523	
524	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
525	
526	Every tool writes its arguments the same way. This page is the reference for what a number, a colour or a list means in an argument, and what happens when one is out of bounds.
527	
528	<AtAGlance
529	  tools={['get_project', 'add_track', 'move_track', 'set_canvas', 'set_transition', 'add_zoom_action', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'paste_attributes', 'copy_pieces', 'set_speed', 'add_speed_ramp']}
530	/>
531	
532	## Times in ticks
533	
534	Every time argument is in ticks, 600,000 to the second.
535	
536	| Length | Ticks |
537	| --- | --- |
538	| 1 second | 600000 |
539	| 1 minute | 36000000 |
540	| 1 frame at 24 fps | 25000 |
541	| 1 frame at 25 fps | 24000 |
542	| 1 frame at 30 fps | 20000 |
543	| 1 frame at 60 fps | 10000 |
544	
545	A time you send is rounded to the project's frame grid. Times in a `set_audio` patch, such as fades and the attack and release of ducking and the compressor, are the exception: they're lengths of sound, so they stay exactly as sent.
546	
547	What a time is measured from depends on the argument:
548	
549	- **Most times** are timeline times, from the start of the timeline. With `scope`, they're from the start of the nest.
550	- **Action times** are clip time, measured from the clip's own start. `add_action`'s `at`, `add_zoom_action`'s `at`, and `add_speed_ramp`'s `from` and `to` are examples.
551	- **Source times** are measured in the media file, played forwards. `get_media_analysis` takes its `from` and `to` this way, not snapped to the grid, and `get_cursor_events` answers in them when you ask with `media`.
552	
553	A few arguments aren't times on the timeline and take plain seconds, such as `record_screen`'s `seconds` and `analyze_cutout`'s `wait`. Each tool's table says so.
554	
555	## One id space
556	
557	Clip, track, marker and media ids share one number space, so an id names one thing on its own. `get_project` lists them, and an edit's answer [names any it creates](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/#a-landed-edit).
558	
559	An id nothing has is answered with where to look: "No clip has id 17. get_project lists the clips." A number that isn't whole isn't an id.
560	
561	## Track order
562	
563	`tracks[0]` is the back of the layer stack and the bottom lane of the timeline. A higher index draws in front.
564	
565	A `track` argument is a track's id, not its place in the stack. The place is `index`, which `add_track` and `move_track` take: 0 is the back. Left out of `add_track`, the new track goes to the front.
566	
567	## Colour formats
568	
569	Colours are spelled differently depending on what they belong to.
570	
571	| Colour | Spelling | Example |
572	| --- | --- | --- |
573	| Clips and the canvas: text, shapes, shadows, outlines, `set_canvas`'s `background` | Four numbers `[r, g, b, a]`, each from 0 to 1 | `[1, 0.35, 0.21, 1]` |
574	| A chroma key, `video.chroma.key` | Three numbers `[r, g, b]`, each from 0 to 1 | `[0, 1, 0]` |
575	| A marker's `color`, a clip's `label` | A colour name: red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple | `"red"` |
576	| A graphic's colour props | A CSS colour string, usually hex | `"#ff5a36"` |
577	
578	Three numbers where four belong, or a component out of range, is refused. Nothing is filled in or clamped. A number from 0 to 255 is the usual mistake.
579	
580	A marker's colour and a clip's label aren't checked against the six. Any other name is kept, and draws in the neutral text colour.
581	
582	A graphic's colour may also be written as `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()`, `hsla()` or a CSS colour name. Frame Job stores it as lowercase hex.
583	
584	## Boolean spellings
585	
586	A tool's boolean argument may be sent as `true` or `false`, or as the strings `"true"`, `"1"`, `"false"` or `"0"`. Any other string, a list or an object is refused: "discard must be true or false."
587	
588	This covers a tool's own arguments. Inside a [patch](/mcp/patches/), a boolean must be a real `true` or `false`, and so must a graphic's boolean prop.
589	
590	## Keys that must be sent even when null
591	
592	Two arguments are required even though null is a valid value, because null means something:
593	
594	| Tool | Argument | Null means |
595	| --- | --- | --- |
596	| `set_transition` | `kind` | Remove the transition |
597	| `add_zoom_action` | `region` | Zoom back out to the clip's own scale and position |
598	
599	Leaving either out is refused, so a forgotten value can't remove a transition or zoom back by accident.
600	
601	## No empty lists
602	
603	An empty list argument names nothing to act on, so it's refused by name.
604	
605	| Argument | Tools | The answer |
606	| --- | --- | --- |
607	| `clips` | Tools that act on clips, such as `set_video`, `detect_silence` and `analyze_cutout` | "clips is empty — name at least one clip." |
608	| `ranges` | `ripple_delete_ranges`, `copy_pieces` | "ranges is empty — name at least one [from, to] pair." |
609	| `groups` | `paste_attributes` | "groups is empty — name at least one of…", followed by the group names. Leave `groups` out to paste the default set. |
610	
611	Where a tool takes `clips`, a single id is accepted in place of a list. In `set_selection` an empty list means something: it selects nothing.
612	
613	A frame-rate term of 0 in `set_canvas`'s `fps` is refused too, as is a fraction: each term is a whole number from 1 to 4294967295, so 29.97 fps is `[30000, 1001]`.
614	
615	Lists inside a patch are different. `filters: []` is how you clear a filter stack. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/#how-a-patch-merges).
616	
617	## Speed rates are clamped
618	
619	Most values out of range are refused. A speed rate is different: `set_speed` and `add_speed_ramp` bring a `rate` outside ×0.1–×1000 into that range. A rate of zero or less is refused.
620	
621	On a clip with a speed ramp, `set_speed` scales every rate in the ramp, so the ramp keeps its shape, and the scale stops where any of those rates would pass the limits.
622	
623	Above ×12 a clip's sound is left out of the mix. The answer says so with `audio_left_out` and `audio_note`. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
624
