631	---
632	title: Patches
633	description: How an agent changes a clip's properties. What a patch merges and clears, how a bad key or value is refused, and how unknown arguments are named.
634	---
635	
636	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
637	
638	A patch is an object holding only the properties you want to change. The property tools take one and merge it into what the clip already has, so an agent never has to send a clip's whole state back.
639	
640	<AtAGlance
641	  tools={['set_video', 'set_audio', 'set_text', 'set_shape', 'set_graphic', 'set_clip', 'set_action_end', 'add_text_clip', 'add_shape_clip']}
642	/>
643	
644	## How a patch merges
645	
646	Each property tool takes a `patch` argument. Three rules cover it:
647	
648	- **Keys you leave out keep their values, at every depth.** A patch of `{shadow: {blur: 20}}` keeps the shadow's colour, angle and distance.
649	- **A key set to `null` clears it**, if it's a key that can be cleared. A required key refuses null.
650	- **A list replaces the whole list.** To change one filter, send the whole `filters` stack. Send `[]` to clear it.
651	
652	```json
653	{
654	  "clips": [12, 15],
655	  "patch": {
656	    "opacity": 0.8,
657	    "shadow": { "blur": 20 },
658	    "reflection": null,
659	    "filters": [{ "kind": "sepia", "amount": 0.5 }]
660	  }
661	}
662	```
663	
664	This sets the opacity of clips 12 and 15, changes only the shadow's blur, removes the reflection and replaces the filter stack with one sepia filter. It's one undo step.
665	
666	Each entry in `filters` must name both `kind` and `amount`, because a list replaces whole and nothing else would fill the gap.
667	
668	| Tool | What its patch changes | What null clears |
669	| --- | --- | --- |
670	| `set_video` | Position, scale, opacity, crop, colour and the other picture properties | Such as `shadow`, `chroma`, `reflection`, `spotlight` and `motion` |
671	| `set_audio` | Volume, fades, ducking, compression and the other sound properties | Such as `duck` and `compressor` |
672	| `set_text` | The words and typography | Such as `outline`, `backdrop`, and `width`, which restores auto-sizing |
673	| `set_shape` | Geometry and paint | Such as `stroke` and `fill` |
674	| `set_graphic` | `name`, `width`, `height`, `length` and `props`, with `props` merged key by key | A prop's key, and `length`, which ends the graphic with its clip |
675	| `set_clip` | `name` and `label` | Either key. An empty or blank name clears it too. |
676	| `set_action_end` | What an action animates to: `video`, `audio`, `text`, `graphic` and `speed` | Removes the key from the end state, so that property stops animating |
677	
678	`set_action_end` differs in two ways. A null there means "stop animating this", so to switch something off at the end of an action, name it in `off` instead. And its values aren't range-checked, because an animation may aim past what a stored property can hold. Its keys and their kinds are still checked, and a graphic's props are held to their minimum and maximum as in `set_graphic`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
679	
680	`set_graphic` has one exception to its null rule. If an action on the clip animates that prop, the prop is set to its default rather than removed, so the animation keeps its start.
681	
682	## Patch refusals name the path
683	
684	A key the property doesn't have, or a value of the wrong kind, is refused. The answer gives the dotted path, array indices included, and for a bad value, the value you sent. Nothing is dropped, corrected or clamped on the way.
685	
686	| What went wrong | The answer |
687	| --- | --- |
688	| A key that doesn't exist | `unknown key "gate.knee" in an audio patch` |
689	| The wrong kind of value | `bad value at "shadow" in a video patch: expected an object, not 5` |
690	| A value outside its range | `audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21` |
691	| A key missing from a list entry | `missing key "filters[1].amount" in a video patch` |
692	
693	A bad entry deep in a list is named by its place, such as `filters[1].kind`. In `set_action_end` the path also carries the group, as in `video.filters[1].kind`.
694	
695	A refused patch changes nothing, on any of the clips it named.
696	
697	## Unknown arguments are refused by name
698	
699	An argument a tool doesn't take is refused before anything runs, and the answer lists what it does take:
700	
701	> trim_start does not take speed. It takes alone, clip, to, project and scope.
702	
703	This holds for every tool, and for an unknown argument sent as null. So a misspelt optional argument can't be dropped in silence while the edit lands without it.
704	
705	A value a tool can't read under the right name is refused by name too:
706	
707	- `discard must be true or false.`
708	- `at must be a time in ticks (600000 per second).`
709	- `fit must be one of fit, fill (got "cover").`
710	
711	A required argument you left out is named the same way: `Missing required argument: clip (an id)`.
712	
713	## Text and shape shorthands
714	
715	`add_text_clip` and `add_shape_clip` take a patch for the new clip, and each has a shorthand. A plain string stands for the one key you'd most often set.
716	
717	| Tool | Shorthand | Means |
718	| --- | --- | --- |
719	| `add_text_clip` | `"text": "Hello"` | `"text": {"content": "Hello"}`, the words |
720	| `add_shape_clip` | `"shape": "ellipse"` | `"shape": {"kind": "ellipse"}`, the kind: `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `line` or `arrow` |
721	
722	You can also pass an object, which works like the patch for `set_text` or `set_shape`. Both arguments are optional. Leave `shape` out and you get a rectangle.
723

731	---
732	title: What a call answers
733	description: How to read a tool's answer. A landed edit, a call that changed nothing, a refusal, an error, what a cloud tool says with no key, and which tools never touch the network.
734	---
735	
736	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
737	
738	A call tells you what happened in its answer, in words a model can act on. An edit lands, changes nothing, is refused, or is an error, and each reads differently.
739	
740	<AtAGlance
741	  tools={['transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers', 'get_media_analysis', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript', 'detect_fillers', 'detect_silence', 'split_at_shots', 'analyze_cutout']}
742	  needs="Your AssemblyAI key, only for a tool that sends to AssemblyAI."
743	/>
744	
745	## Answers come back as tool results
746	
747	Every answer comes back as the tool's result, so a model can read it and correct itself. A refused or invalid call is an ordinary tool result with `isError: true`, and its text is the message. It isn't a transport or JSON-RPC error. A call that changed nothing is marked the same way, and its message says the project is already in that state.
748	
749	JSON-RPC errors are for the protocol itself. An MCP method the server doesn't know gets "method not found", and a `tools/call` with no tool name is an error too. A tool name that doesn't exist is an ordinary result: "Unknown tool: *name*".
750	
751	| The answer | `isError` | Undo step | What to do |
752	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
753	| [A landed edit](#a-landed-edit) | false | One | Read the ids and carry on |
754	| [No change](#a-no-change-answer) | true | None | Nothing. The project already says that. |
755	| [A refusal](#a-refusal) | true | None | Act on the reason, then call again |
756	| [An error](#an-error) | true | None | Fix the argument it names, then call again |
757	
758	## A landed edit
759	
760	An edit that landed answers `ok: true`, the ids it created, anything the tool adds of its own, and a short `project` summary. A model doesn't need to read the whole project back to see what it did.
761	
762	```json
763	{
764	  "ok": true,
765	  "new_clips": [42],
766	  "project": {
767	    "name": "Interview",
768	    "path": "/Volumes/Work/Interview.framejob",
769	    "width": 1920,
770	    "height": 1080,
771	    "fps": [30, 1],
772	    "duration": 1800000,
773	    "playhead": 600000,
774	    "tracks": 3,
775	    "clips": 7,
776	    "markers": 2,
777	    "media": 4,
778	    "selection": [],
779	    "unsaved_changes": true
780	  }
781	}
782	```
783	
784	The ids appear only when the edit created something:
785	
786	| Key | What it lists |
787	| --- | --- |
788	| `new_clips` | Clips the edit created, inside any nest too |
789	| `new_tracks` | Tracks the edit created, inside any nest too |
790	| `new_markers` | Markers the edit created |
791	| `new_media` | Media the edit added |
792	| `new_actions` | Actions, from the tools that add them, such as `add_action` |
793	
794	The summary holds:
795	
796	| Key | What it is |
797	| --- | --- |
798	| `name`, `path` | The project's name and its path, which is `null` for a project with no file yet |
799	| `width`, `height`, `fps` | The canvas. `fps` is `[numerator, denominator]`. |
800	| `duration`, `playhead` | Both in [ticks](/mcp/units-and-ids/#times-in-ticks) |
801	| `tracks`, `clips`, `markers`, `media` | How many of each, counted on the top-level timeline |
802	| `selection` | The ids of the selected clips |
803	| `unsaved_changes` | Whether the project has changes to save |
804	| `missing_media` | The ids of media whose file is gone. It only appears when there are some, and `relink_media` points one at its new place. |
805	
806	An edit made inside a nest also answers `scope`, the nest it landed in. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). A speed edit that takes a clip past ×12 adds `audio_left_out` and `audio_note`.
807	
808	Every edit is exactly [one undo step](/mcp/tool-calls/#one-call-one-undo-step), however many clips it touched.
809	
810	## A no-change answer
811	
812	> Video Properties made no change: the project is already in that state.
813	
814	This means nothing was wrong. The project already says what you asked, so no undo step was made and it's safe to retry. The message opens with the name the step would have had in the **Edit** menu.
815	
816	## A refusal
817	
818	> Remove Track was refused at remove_track: track 3 still holds clip 12; pass with_clips: true to remove the track and its clips
819	
820	A rule declined the edit. The message reads *step* was refused at *edit*: *reason*. The reason names what you can act on:
821	
822	- a track that's locked
823	- the clips still using a media file
824	- how far two clips would overlap
825	- the argument that lets the call through, such as `with_clips: true` or `ripple: true`
826	
827	The project is untouched and no undo step is made, so you can fix the cause and call again.
828	
829	## An error
830	
831	An argument Frame Job can't use is an error, and it's marked and treated like a refusal: nothing changes and no undo step is made. The message names the argument.
832	
833	| What went wrong | Example |
834	| --- | --- |
835	| An id nothing has | `No clip has id 17. get_project lists the clips.` |
836	| A required argument left out | `Missing required argument: clip (an id)` |
837	| An argument the tool doesn't take | `trim_start does not take speed. It takes alone, clip, to, project and scope.` |
838	| A bad key or value in a patch | `unknown key "gate.knee" in an audio patch` |
839	
840	A message starting "internal error:" means something went wrong inside Frame Job. The project is unchanged.
841	
842	[Patches](/mcp/patches/#patch-refusals-name-the-path) has more of these, and [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/) gives the rules they come from.
843	
844	## Keyed tools with no key
845	
846	Two tools can send to AssemblyAI, and both use the key and region saved in **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription**. A person has to set the key first, because [no tool can set or read it](/captions/assemblyai-key/#only-a-person-sets-the-key).
847	
848	A tool needs the key only at the moment it would send. Without one it refuses there, before anything is uploaded:
849	
850	> No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription.
851	
852	| Tool | Needs the key | Doesn't need the key |
853	| --- | --- | --- |
854	| `transcribe` | With `engine: "assemblyai"` when a file has no usable transcript, or with `refresh: true` | The default `apple` engine, or when every file already has a current transcript in the project |
855	| `transcribe_for_fillers` | When it has to upload the file | When the file already has a transcript made with filler words |
856	
857	No tool needs an Anthropic key. That key is only for the [Assistant](/assistant/set-up/) inside Frame Job.
858	
859	## Tools that never reach the network
860	
861	These tools read what's on your Mac. They never make a network request, upload anything or need a key, whatever you pass them.
862	
863	| Tool | What it reads |
864	| --- | --- |
865	| `get_media_analysis` | Analysis made on your Mac and kept in the project's cache |
866	| `split_at_shots` | The same analysis, for shot changes |
867	| `analyze_cutout` | Masks made on your Mac |
868	| `detect_silence` | The cached waveform and voice detection |
869	| `detect_fillers` | An AssemblyAI transcript already in the project. A file with no such transcript is listed under `needs_transcript`. |
870	| `get_transcript` | A cached transcript, or your Mac's own speech recogniser |
871	| `get_timeline_transcript` | A cached transcript, or your Mac's own speech recogniser |

2	title: "Editing inside a nest"
3	description: "Open a nest with set_scope or name one on a single call with scope, and see what follows the open nest and what won't work inside one."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A [nest](/editing/nests/) is a group of clips collapsed into one clip, and it has its own tracks, clips and clock. An agent can work inside one in two ways: open it, as you would, or name it on a single call.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['Clip ▸ Open Nest', 'Clip ▸ Close Nest']}
13	  keys={['⌘↓', '⌘↑']}
14	  where="Double-click a nest clip"
15	  tools="set_scope"
16	/>
17	
18	## Choose how to get in
19	
20	| | Open it with `set_scope` | Name it with `scope` |
21	| --- | --- | --- |
22	| What it is | A change of view, like double-clicking the nest clip | An argument on one edit tool |
23	| How long it lasts | Until `set_scope` with no arguments | That one call |
24	| What it reaches | A nest a clip shows, at any depth | Any nest in the project, shown or not |
25	| Who it affects | Every later call, and what the window shows | Only that call. The window stays where it is |
26	| When to use it | You want to look: `get_project`, `render_frame`, or a tool that takes no `scope` | You want one edit, from wherever you are |
27	
28	Editing doesn't need the nest open. Opening it is how you see what an edit did.
29	
30	## Open and close a nest with `set_scope`
31	
32	`set_scope` does what double-clicking a nest clip does, or **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>). Called with no arguments it comes back out, as **Clip ▸ Close Nest** (<kbd>⌘↑</kbd>) does, but all the way to the timeline in one call.
33	
34	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
35	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
36	| `clip` | integer | No | The nest clip to open. Works at any depth, and is the precise choice. |
37	| `nest` | integer | No | The nest to open, by id. A clip on the timeline has to show it. |
38	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
39	
40	Give `clip` or `nest`, never both. Giving neither means the timeline.
41	
42	**`clip` is the one to prefer.** Two clips can show one nest, and each measures the times inside from its own start, so only the clip says which of them you mean. It finds the clip in the timeline or in any nest, and the call means the same thing wherever you are now, so there's no need to step down one level at a time.
43	
44	**`nest` looks at the timeline only.** Where two timeline clips show the nest, the earliest is entered, and a tie goes to the lower id. A nest that's shown only from inside another nest can't be reached this way. Name its nest clip with `clip`, or send the edit with `scope`, which needs no view at all.
45	
46	### While a nest is open
47	
48	- [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/#the-report-while-a-nest-is-open) reports the nest as if it were the project, and [`render_frame`](/mcp/render-frame/) draws it at its own size.
49	- Every edit lands inside the nest, unless the call has a `scope` of its own or is one of the [document edits](#document-edits-while-a-nest-is-open).
50	- The playhead, the selection and the range all belong to the nest. Times you send and read are measured from the nest's own zero.
51	
52	`set_scope` moves the view and edits nothing, so it adds no undo step. The playhead moves with it so the frame under it stays the same, as it does [for you](/editing/inside-a-nest/#where-the-playhead-goes). Every change of nest clears the in and out range. Going in clears the selection, and coming out selects the nest clip you went in through.
53	
54	If an edit or an undo takes away the nest that's open, Frame Job falls back to the nearest level that still exists.
55	
56	### What it returns
57	
58	| Key | What it holds |
59	| --- | --- |
60	| `ok` | `true`. |
61	| `scope` | The open nest's id, the number an edit's `scope` takes. `null` at the timeline. |
62	| `scope_clip` | The nest clip it was entered through. |
63	| `scope_path` | The trail from the timeline, one `{nest, clip, name}` for each level. |
64	| `playhead` | The playhead, in the nest's own time. |
65	| `project` | The project summary. |
66	
67	`scope_clip` and `scope_path` appear only while a nest is open. `get_project` reports the same three keys.
68	
69	### When a nest won't open
70	
71	| It says | Why |
72	| --- | --- |
73	| "Pass nest or clip, not both…" | Both arguments were given. |
74	| "No clip has id 17, in this timeline or in any of its nests…" | No clip anywhere has that id. |
75	| "Clip 17 does not show a nest, so there is nothing to open inside it…" | The clip exists but isn't a nest clip. Its `source.kind` isn't `nest`. |
76	| "no nest with id 4…" | The project has no such nest. |
77	| "No clip on the timeline shows nest 4, so the view cannot reach it in one step…" | The nest is shown only from inside another nest, or by no clip at all. |
78	
79	## The `scope` argument
80	
81	Every edit tool takes an optional `scope`, a nest id, so one call edits inside that nest from wherever the window is looking. It's the same edit and still one undo step.
82	
83	```json
84	{ "clips": [41], "at": 1200000, "scope": 4 }
85	```
86	
87	Sent to `split`, that cuts clip 41 inside nest 4, at 2 s on the nest's own clock.
88	
89	To find the id, read `nests` in `get_project`, or the `source.project` of the nest clip that shows it.
90	
91	With `scope`:
92	
93	- Every clip, track and action id is looked up in that nest, not on the timeline.
94	- Every time is the nest's own, measured from its zero. To turn a timeline time into a nest time, subtract the nest clip's start. A nest has no speed, so nothing else changes it.
95	- Media ids don't change, because a nest shares the project's media.
96	- It outranks any nest that's open. To edit the timeline while a nest is open you can't name the timeline, so call `set_scope` with no arguments first.
97	
98	Leave `scope` out, or send `null`, to edit whatever is open: the timeline, or the nest `set_scope` entered.
99	
100	The answer carries `scope`, the nest the edit landed in, so you can tell it from an edit on the timeline. Clips and tracks the edit made are listed in `new_clips` and `new_tracks` wherever they landed. The `project` summary in the same answer counts the timeline's tracks and clips, so it doesn't move when an edit lands in a nest.
101	
102	### When a `scope` isn't accepted
103	
104	A `scope` is checked before any other argument, because it decides what the rest of the call means.
105	
106	| It says | Why |
107	| --- | --- |
108	| "no nest with id 4. get_project lists them under nests, and a nest clip's source.project names the one it shows." | The project has no such nest. |
109	| "scope must be a nest id, not …" | The value isn't a whole number that could be an id. A negative number, a fraction, a true or false and a number written as a string all fail. |
110	| "No clip has id 17 inside nest 4…" | The id isn't in that nest. The sentence goes on to say how to get back: drop the `scope`, or, when the nest is only open, call `set_scope` with no arguments. Tracks work the same way. |
111	| "detect_silence does not take scope. It takes …" | The tool isn't an edit tool. See [below](#tools-that-follow-the-open-nest). |
112	
113	## Tools that follow the open nest
114	
115	Tools that aren't plain edits take no `scope`, and a call that gives them one returns an error naming the argument. They work in whatever nest `set_scope` has open, and on the timeline otherwise, so open the nest first to measure or place inside it.
116	
117	| What it does | Tools |
118	| --- | --- |
119	| Measure and read | `detect_silence`, `detect_fillers`, `get_timeline_transcript`, `get_media_analysis`, `get_cursor_events` |
120	| Sound | `normalize_clip`, `enhance_voice`, `match_audio`, `sync_audio` |
121	| Captions and words | `transcribe`, `transcribe_for_fillers`, `import_captions`, `export_captions`, `relay_captions` |
122	| Picture and timing | `split_at_shots`, `analyze_cutout`, `auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `switch_angle`, `switch_by_speaker` |
123	| Adding things | `insert_graphic`, which places its clip in the nest, and `record_screen`, which does the same |
124	| View state | `set_playhead`, `set_range`, `set_selection` |
125	
126	A tool that takes a while reads the project first and checks it again before it edits. If the project or the open nest changed meanwhile, it stops and changes nothing, and says to call it again.
127	
128	Three tools work on the top-level timeline only. With a nest open they stop with an error that tells you to call `set_scope` with no nest first:
129	
130	- `text_behind_subject`
131	- `new_project_from_range`
132	- `make_vertical_version`
133	
134	`rename_graphic` won't run with a nest open either, because it renames the module for every clip in the project. Call `set_scope` with no arguments, then rename.
135	
136	`export` and `save_project` ignore the open nest. `export` writes from the timeline, never the nest, and `save_project` saves the whole project.
137	
138	## `protected_nests` in `detect_silence`
139	
140	[Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) never cuts into a nest, so a quiet stretch that runs across one is left alone. `detect_silence` names those nest clips under `protected_nests`, because there may be dead air inside them.
141	
142	<Steps>
143	
144	1. Call `detect_silence`. Read `protected_nests`, a list of nest clip ids.
145	
146	2. Call `set_scope` with `clip` set to one of those ids.
147	
148	3. Call `detect_silence` again. It now measures inside the nest, and its times are the nest's own.
149	
150	4. Pass the ranges to `ripple_delete_ranges`, which lands in the open nest. Like any edit tool it also takes `scope`.
151	
152	5. Call `set_scope` with no arguments to come back out.
153	
154	</Steps>
155	
156	## What doesn't work inside a nest
157	
158	Some edits are about the whole project, so a nest has nothing for them to change. What happens depends on whether the nest was named with `scope` or is only open.
159	
160	| Edit | With `scope` | With the nest only open |
161	| --- | --- | --- |
162	| `add_marker` | Not allowed | Not allowed |
163	| `set_marker` with a `time` | Not allowed | Not allowed |
164	| `set_marker` without a `time` | Not allowed | Lands on the project |
165	| `remove_marker` | Not allowed | Lands on the project |
166	| `set_canvas` | Not allowed | Lands on the project |
167	| `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media` | Not allowed | Land on the project |
168	| `set_media_color`, `set_media_speech`, `set_media_cursor` | Not allowed | Land on the project |
169	| `add_adjustment_clip` | Not allowed | Not allowed |
170	| `set_track` with `compressor` or `limiter` | Not allowed | Not allowed |
171	
172	### Edit tools that won't take a `scope`
173	
174	Eleven tools have no meaning inside a nest. Give one a `scope` and it returns an error naming the tool, for example "add_marker has no meaning inside nest 4".
175	
176	| Tools | Why |
177	| --- | --- |
178	| `add_marker`, `set_marker`, `remove_marker` | A nest has no markers. Markers are project time, and they become chapters in the exported file. |
179	| `set_canvas` | The frame rate and background are the project's, and a nest's size was fixed when it was made. |
180	| `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color`, `set_media_speech`, `set_media_cursor` | A nest shares the project's one media list. |
181	| `add_adjustment_clip` | An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) grades what's behind it on the timeline only. This one won't work with a nest open either. |
182	
183	`set_track` works inside a nest, except that a track's `compressor` and `limiter` aren't allowed, with or without `scope`: a track's dynamics run on the timeline's own mix. A nest's whole sound goes through the track holding its nest clip, so set them there. Volume, pan and the rest of `set_track` mean the same inside a nest as outside.
184	
185	### Document edits while a nest is open
186	
187	When a nest is only open, and the call has no `scope`, nine of those tools apply to the whole project, because that's what they're about. It's the same as you choosing **File ▸ Add Media…** with a nest open.
188	
189	Those are `set_marker` without a `time`, `remove_marker`, `set_canvas`, `add_media`, `relink_media`, `remove_media`, `set_media_color`, `set_media_speech` and `set_media_cursor`.
190	
191	The answer lists what went to the project under `document_ops`, and leaves `scope` out because nothing landed in the nest:
192	
193	```json
194	{ "ok": true, "document_ops": ["set_canvas"], "project": { … } }
195	```
196	
197	`add_media` is the exception: it lands on the project all the same, but its own answer has no `document_ops`. `import_media` adds to the project in the same way, with a nest open or not, and its answer has none either.
198	
199	### Markers while a nest is open
200	
201	`add_marker`, and `set_marker` with a `time`, return an error while a nest is open, whatever time you send. A marker sits at project time, and every tick in the call is measured from the nest's own zero, so the marker would land somewhere else on the timeline. It's the reason **Mark ▸ Add Marker** is greyed out in there.
202	
203	Leave the nest with `set_scope` and no arguments, then send the time in project ticks. A marker's name, chapter setting and colour mean the same in either place, so `set_marker` still changes those. See [Markers](/timeline/markers/#good-to-know).
204	
205	### Document-wide limits inside a nest
206	
207	An edit can be valid inside the nest and still fail for the project's sake, because these limits count every nest and the timeline together:
208	
209	| Limit | Counted over |
210	| --- | --- |
211	| 4,096 clips | The timeline and every nest |
212	| 64 tracks | The timeline and every nest |
213	| 8 levels of nesting | The deepest chain of nests |
214	
215	So read the answer rather than assuming the edit landed. The error names the limit, for example "too many tracks: 65 (max 64)".

227	description: "The order an agent works in, from opening a project through placing, changing and checking clips to saving and exporting."
228	---
229	
230	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
231	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
232	
233	An agent works in Frame Job the way you do: bring the media in, place it, change it, look at the result, then save and export. What's different is that it can't see the window, so it reads the project for the ids it needs and renders a frame to check each step.
234	
235	<AtAGlance
236	  tools={['new_project', 'open_project', 'get_project', 'import_media', 'add_clip', 'render_frame', 'save_project', 'export', 'export_status']}
237	/>
238	
239	## Work through a session
240	
241	<Steps>
242	
243	1. **Open.** Call `open_project` with a path, or `new_project` for a blank 1920 × 1080, 30 fps project with one track. See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).
244	
245	2. **Read.** Call `get_project`. It returns the canvas, the playhead and every id. Every other tool names things by those ids.
246	
247	3. **Import.** Call `import_media` with the file's path. It returns the new `media` id and what the file holds: its kind, duration, size, frame rate, and whether it has video, sound or transparency. The file is in the project now, but not on the timeline.
248	
249	4. **Place.** Call `add_clip` with `track`, `media` and `at`. The answer lists the new clip's id under `new_clips`.
250	
251	5. **Change.** Use the edit tools. Each call is one undo step. See [All tools](/mcp/tools/).
252	
253	6. **Check.** Call `render_frame` at the moment that matters, and look at the picture. Do this before and after an edit.
254	
255	7. **Save.** Call `save_project`, with a `path` the first time. It returns once the package is on disk.
256	
257	8. **Export.** Call `export` with a `preset` and a `path`. It returns at once with an `export_id`. Then call `export_status` until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
258	
259	</Steps>
260	
261	Steps 5 and 6 are the loop. An edit that comes back `ok` says the project changed, and only a frame says it looks right. If it doesn't, `undo` takes the last step back.
262	
263	## See one from start to finish
264	
265	Here's a short session, each call with its arguments. Times are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, so `1200000` is 2 s.
266	
267	```text
268	new_project   { "path": "~/Movies/Talk.framejob" }
269	get_project   { }
270	import_media  { "path": "~/Movies/talk.mov" }
271	add_clip      { "track": 1, "media": 2, "at": 0 }
272	split         { "clips": [3], "at": 1200000 }
273	render_frame  { "t": 1200000, "max_width": 960 }
274	save_project  { }
275	export        { "preset": "h264", "path": "~/Movies/Talk.mp4" }
276	export_status { "export_id": 1 }
277	```
278	
279	`media` and `clips` here stand for the ids the earlier answers gave. Read them from each answer rather than guessing, because ids come from one number series that clips, tracks, markers and media all share. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
280	
281	`save_project` needs no `path` here because `new_project` was given one. A project made without one stays an untitled draft until the first `save_project` that names a path.
282	
283	## Follow the export
284	
285	`export` puts the job on the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) and returns. It doesn't wait for the file.
286	
287	`export_status` never waits either, so pause between calls. While the job runs, its answer has `progress`, from 0 to 1. When `status` is `done`, the answer says what the file holds, including its size in `bytes`, its settings and its loudness. `failed` and `cancelled` come with a `reason`.
288	
289	To stop a job, call `cancel_export`. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).
290	
291	## Good to know
292	
293	- Tools act on the frontmost project. With more than one open, pass `project`, the path `get_project` reports. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).
294	- A call that can't do what it's asked comes back with the reason, and the project stays as it was. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
295	- `render_frame` and `export` differ inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/). With a nest open, `render_frame` draws the nest, but `export` still writes from the timeline.
296	- `export` replaces a file already at the path, and adds the container's extension when the path has none.
297	- `unsaved_changes` in `get_project` says whether there's anything still to save.

310	
311	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
312	
313	`get_project` returns the whole project as JSON, the same document every edit changes. Read it first, because every other tool names things by the ids it reports.
314	
315	<AtAGlance tools="get_project" />
316	
317	## Read the project
318	
319	The only argument is `project`, the path of the open project to read. Leave it out for the frontmost one. The call changes nothing.
320	
321	Three things hold for everything it returns:
322	
323	- Times are ticks, 600,000 to the second.
324	- Clip, track, marker and media ids share one number series, so an id means one thing on its own.
325	- `tracks[0]` is the back of the layer stack, the bottom lane of the timeline.
326	
327	See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
328	
329	## What it answers
330	
331	| Key | What it holds |
332	| --- | --- |
333	| `project` | The project itself. See [below](#what-project-holds). |
334	| `path` | Where the project is saved. Before its first save, a project opened from a movie, sound file or picture reports that file, and any other project reports `null`. |
335	| `name` | The project's name, as its window shows it. |
336	| `unsaved_changes` | `true` when there's something to save. |
337	| `duration` | The timeline's length in ticks. |
338	| `playhead` | The playhead, in ticks. |
339	| `selection` | The ids of the selected clips, lowest first. |
340	| `in_out_range` | `start` and `end` in ticks. Only there when a range is set. |
341	| `scope` | The id of the [open nest](#the-report-while-a-nest-is-open), or `null` at the timeline. |
342	| `missing_media` | The ids of media whose file has moved. Only there when one has. `relink_media` points one at its new place. |
343	| `graphics` | The project's [graphic modules](#the-graphics-summary). |
344	| `note` | A reminder of the rules above. With a nest open, it also says what's different. |
345	
346	`playhead`, `selection` and `in_out_range` are the app's own state. They aren't saved with the project, and setting them isn't an undo step.
347	
348	## What `project` holds
349	
350	| Key | What it holds |
351	| --- | --- |
352	| `canvas` | The picture's settings. See the next table. |
353	| `media` | Every file in the project, whether or not a clip uses it. |
354	| `tracks` | The timeline's tracks, back to front. |
355	| `clips` | The timeline's clips. |
356	| `markers` | The timeline's markers. |
357	| `nests` | Every nest, each with its own `id`, `name`, `width`, `height`, `tracks` and `clips`. |
358	| `next_id` | The id the next new thing will take. |
359	| `version` | The project file's version. |
360	
361	| `canvas` key | What it holds |
362	| --- | --- |
363	| `width`, `height` | The canvas size in pixels. |
364	| `fps` | The frame rate as `[num, den]`, so 29.97 fps is `[30000, 1001]`. |
365	| `background` | The canvas background. |
366	| `fit_new_clips` | Whether a new clip is scaled to fit when its source is bigger than the canvas. |
367	| `timecode_frames` | Whether timecode reads `HH:MM:SS:FF` rather than `HH:MM:SS.mmm`. |
368	| `output` | `hlg` in an [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/). Left out in an SDR project. |
369	| `blending` | `linear` with [linear-light blending](/hdr/blending/) on. Left out otherwise. |
370	
371	A media entry has `id`, `path`, `kind`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps`, `has_video`, `has_audio` and `has_alpha`, and sometimes more: `original` for a copy, `color` for [its colour setting](#read-a-files-camera-log), `speech` for saved speech spans and `cursor` for a recording's cursor file.
372	
373	A clip has `id`, `track`, `start`, `duration`, `source`, `enabled`, `speed` and `actions`. What it shows sits in `video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape` or `graphic`. `source.kind` says what kind of clip it is, and a nest clip's `source.project` is the id of the nest it shows.
374	
375	## The graphics summary
376	
377	`graphics` is a list with one entry for each module in the project's graphics folder, in name order:
378	
379	| Key | What it holds |
380	| --- | --- |
381	| `name` | The module's name. |
382	| `revision` | The module's revision. It changes when the text does. |
383	| `ok` | `true` when the module compiles. |
384	| `clips` | The ids of the clips drawn by it, on the timeline and in every nest. |
385	
386	`ok: false` means the module doesn't compile. Fix it before exporting, because `export` won't start while a graphic clip's module doesn't compile. See [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/).
387	
388	The list is empty in a project with no modules, and in a project that has no window.
389	
390	## Read a file's Camera Log
391	
392	A file's colour setting is in `color` on its media entry. A file with no setting has no `color`, and each key below appears only when it's set.
393	
394	| Key | What it holds |
395	| --- | --- |
396	| `log` | The curve: `apple_log`, `apple_log2`, `slog3`, `vlog`, `canon_log2` or `canon_log3`. |
397	| `gamut` | The gamut: `bt2020`, `apple_wide_gamut`, `s_gamut3_cine`, `s_gamut3`, `v_gamut` or `cinema_gamut`. |
398	| `lut` | The media id of a [LUT](/hdr/log-luts/) used as the conversion, in place of `log`. |
399	| `detected` | `true` when Frame Job read the setting from the file at import. |
400	| `pq` | An HDR10 file's peak: `file` is what import read, in cd/m², `from` is where it read it (`max_cll` or `mastering_display`), and `peak` is an override. An empty `pq` still marks the file as HDR10. |
401	
402	`detected: true` is how to tell a setting the file declared from one a person or an agent chose. Setting the Camera Log with `set_media_color` replaces it and drops `detected`. See [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/).
403	
404	## The report while a nest is open
405	
406	While `set_scope` has a nest open, `get_project` reports the nest as if it were the project, so the ids you read are the ones the next edit can name.
407	
408	- `project.tracks` and `project.clips` are the nest's own.
409	- `project.canvas` has the nest's fixed size. Its other settings are the project's.
410	- `project.markers` is empty, because a nest has no markers.
411	- `project.media` and `project.nests` are still the whole project's, but the open nest's own row under `nests` has no tracks or clips, because they're at the top level here.
412	- `duration`, `playhead`, `selection` and `in_out_range` are the nest's, measured from its own zero.
413	
414	Two more keys say where you are:
415	
416	| Key | What it holds |
417	| --- | --- |
418	| `scope_clip` | The nest clip it was entered through. |
419	| `scope_path` | The trail of nests from the timeline, one `{nest, clip, name}` for each level. |
420	
421	`scope` is the nest's id, the same number an edit's `scope` argument takes. At the timeline `scope` is `null`, and the two keys above aren't there.
422	
423	Every edit now lands inside the nest, unless the call has a `scope` of its own or is one of the [document edits](/mcp/nests/#document-edits-while-a-nest-is-open). `render_frame` follows the same view and draws the nest at its own size. Opening a nest is a change of view, not an undo step. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).

438	
439	`render_frame` draws one frame of the finished timeline, so an agent can see what it has done. It's drawn the same way an export draws it, so the picture is what the file will contain at that moment, not a preview of it.
440	
441	<AtAGlance
442	  menu="File ▸ Save Frame…"
443	  keys="⌥⌘E"
444	  tools="render_frame"
445	/>
446	
447	## Render a frame
448	
449	With no arguments it draws the frame under the playhead at the canvas's size and writes a PNG to a temporary file.
450	
451	```json
452	{ "t": 1200000, "path": "/tmp/shot.png", "max_width": 960 }
453	```
454	
455	The picture comes back two ways: as an image the model can see, and as a file on disk. The text beside it says what was drawn and ends by naming the file:
456	
457	```
458	Frame at 1200000 ticks of a 1920×1080 px canvas, rendered at 960×540 px. Written to /tmp/shot.png.
459	```
460	
461	It uses the same writer as [**File ▸ Save Frame…**](/export/save-frame/), so a PNG from either one is identical, byte for byte.
462	
463	With a [nest](/mcp/nests/) open, it draws that nest at its own size, from its own zero, without the nest clip's position, scale or opacity. It takes no `scope`, so open the nest with `set_scope` to look inside.
464	
465	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does | Default |
466	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
467	| [`t`](#t) | integer | No | The moment to render, in ticks. | The playhead |
468	| [`path`](#path) | string | No | Where to write the file. | A temporary file |
469	| [`format`](#format) | string | No | `png`, `jpeg` or `heic`. | From the path, else `png` |
470	| [`max_width`](#max_width) | integer | No | Caps the width in pixels, 16 to 8192. | The canvas's width |
471	| [`burn_in_timecode`](#burn_in_timecode) | boolean | No | Draws the project timecode over the picture. | `false` |
472	| [`ungraded`](#ungraded) | boolean | No | Draws every clip as if it weren't graded. | `false` |
473	| [`selection`](#selection) | integer | No | Draws what an adjustment clip's qualifier selects. | None |
474	| [`sdr_version`](#sdr_version) | boolean | No | Draws an HDR project's SDR version. | `false` |
475	| [`waveform`](#waveform-parade-and-histogram) | boolean | No | Also measures the waveform. | `false` |
476	| [`parade`](#waveform-parade-and-histogram) | boolean | No | Also measures the RGB parade. | `false` |
477	| [`histogram`](#waveform-parade-and-histogram) | boolean | No | Also measures the histogram. | `false` |
478	| [`vectorscope`](#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom) | boolean | No | Also measures the vectorscope. | `false` |
479	| [`vectorscope_zoom`](#vectorscope-and-vectorscope_zoom) | integer | No | 1, 2 or 4. Needs `vectorscope`. | 1 |
480	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on. | The frontmost project |
481	
482	## Choose the moment and the file
483	
484	### `t`
485	
486	The moment to render, in ticks, 600,000 to the second. It's rounded to the project's frame grid. Leave it out for the playhead. A time before zero draws the first frame, and a time past the end returns an [error](#when-it-wont-render).
487	
488	With a nest open, `t` and the playhead are the nest's own time.
489	
490	### `path`
491	
492	Where to write the file, for example `~/Desktop/shot.png`. The folder must already exist, because Frame Job won't create one. An empty `path` is an error.
493	
494	Leave it out for a temporary file. Either way, the last sentence of the text names the file written.
495	
496	### `format`
497	
498	The kind of file to write.
499	
500	| `format` | What you get |
501	| --- | --- |
502	| `png` | Lossless, keeping the canvas's transparency. |
503	| `jpeg` | Quality 0.9. JPEG has no transparency, so a transparent canvas is flattened onto black, and the text always says so. |
504	| `heic` | Quality 0.9, keeping the canvas's transparency. |
505	
506	With no `format`, the path's extension decides: `.jpg` and `.jpeg` both mean JPEG, and `.heic` means HEIC. Any other path writes a PNG.
507	
508	An explicit `format` wins, and the path's extension is replaced rather than added to, so `{"path": "shot.jpg", "format": "png"}` writes `shot.png`. Only an extension Frame Job knows is replaced: `Talk v1.2` becomes `Talk v1.2.png`, not `Talk v1.png`. A JPEG always ends `.jpg`, so `shot.jpeg` is written as `shot.jpg`.
509	
510	`jpg` also works as a `format`, and capitals don't matter.
511	
512	### `max_width`
513	
514	Caps the image's width in pixels, from 16 to 8192. The picture keeps its shape and is never made larger than the canvas. Leave it out for the canvas's own size.
515	
516	A smaller frame is quicker to send and to look at. The [scopes](#measure-the-frame) measure the frame as written, so their counts cover fewer pixels too.
517	
518	## Change what's drawn
519	
520	These four draw something other than the plain picture. The view switches in the window never reach this tool or an export, so an agent asks here.
521	
522	### `burn_in_timecode`
523	
524	Draws the project timecode over the picture, on top of everything, as the export sheet's **Burn in timecode** does. It's the project's own timecode, in the toolbar's spelling. An export from the in/out range shows project time too, so the number always matches the timeline. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/).
525	
526	### `ungraded`
527	
528	Draws every clip as if it weren't graded: Light, Color, wheels and curves neutral, and no look. It's the picture **View ▸ Show Ungraded** gives. See [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/).
529	
530	### `selection`
531	
532	Takes an adjustment clip's id and draws what its qualifier selects, in place of grading. It's the picture **View ▸ Show Selection** gives.
533	
534	- White is fully graded, and black is untouched.
535	- It's the blurred selection when the qualifier has a blur, and it's multiplied by any matte cutting the clip.
536	- The clip's strength isn't applied.
537	- Every layer in front of the clip is left out.
538	- Where the clip isn't on the frame, the picture is black.
539	
540	Frame Job won't do this for any other kind of clip. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).
541	
542	### `sdr_version`
543	
544	Draws an [HDR project's](/hdr/dynamic-range/) SDR version, the picture **View ▸ Show SDR Version** gives. White titles come back near white, and highlights above reference white roll off. It's what the SDR exports and JPEG frames hold.
545	
546	In an SDR project it changes nothing, and the frame comes out identical. See [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/).
547	
548	## Measure the frame
549	
550	Each scope argument measures the rendered frame through the same analyser as the [**View ▸ Scopes**](/color/scopes/) panel, so the two can't count differently. The text gives the headline figures, and a JSON file beside the image holds the counts, named after it: `shot.png` gets `shot.png.waveform.json`.
551	
552	The scopes read the frame as it was drawn, so `max_width`, `burn_in_timecode`, `ungraded` and `selection` all change what they count.
553	
554	If the measurement can't run, the call comes back as an error, but the image is already written and the error names it: "Wrote …, but its waveform could not be measured: the GPU pass did not run."
555	
556	### `waveform`, `parade` and `histogram`
557	
558	- **`waveform`** measures luma. The text gives the share of pixels clipping high and low.
559	- **`parade`** measures R′, G′ and B′ the way the waveform measures luma. The text gives the share clipping high and low for each channel.
560	- **`histogram`** counts R′, G′, B′ and Y′ at 256 levels. The text gives the share clipping high and low, read from Y′.
561	
562	For example: "Waveform: highlights clipped in 0.4 % of pixels, shadows in 0.0 %; its 256 × 256 counts are in …". A pixel clips high at level 255 and low at level 0.
563	
564	| JSON key | `waveform` | `parade` | `histogram` |
565	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
566	| `width`, `height` | The frame measured | The frame measured | The frame measured |
567	| `levels` | 256 | 256 | 256 |
568	| `columns` | 256 | 256 | |
569	| `counts` | 256 column bins, each 256 levels | The same, under `red`, `green` and `blue` | |
570	| `red`, `green`, `blue`, `luma` | | | 256 counts each |
571	| `clipped_high`, `clipped_low` | Pixels clipping | Pixels clipping, by channel | Pixels clipping, by Y′ |
572	| `marks_high`, `marks_low` | The column bins where at least 0.5 % of the column clips | The same, by channel | |
573	| `highlights`, `shadows` | Percentages | | Percentages |
574	
575	### `vectorscope` and `vectorscope_zoom`
576	
577	`vectorscope` measures Rec. 709 Cb and Cr of the encoded values in 256 × 256 bins centred on neutral, bin 128. The text gives the share of pixels that are neutral.
578	
579	`vectorscope_zoom` is 1, 2 or 4, like the 1×, 2× and 4× cells on a [vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) slot, and it needs `vectorscope: true`. Zooming spreads a near-grey picture over more bins. At 2 and 4, a pixel off the plot isn't counted, and the text also gives the share that lie off it.
580	
581	| JSON key | What it holds |
582	| --- | --- |
583	| `width`, `height` | The frame measured. |
584	| `bins`, `centre` | 256 and 128. |
585	| `matrix`, `values` | `Rec. 709` and `encoded`. |
586	| `counts` | 256 arrays by Cr bin, each indexed by Cb bin. |
587	| `neutral` | Pixels in the neutral bin. |
588	| `zoom` | The zoom. |
589	| `off_plot` | Pixels left off the plot. Always 0 at 1. |
590	| `targets` | The six 75 % colour targets, `R`, `Mg`, `B`, `Cy`, `G` and `Yl`, each `[cb, cr]` in bins at this zoom, or `null` off the plot. |
591	| `skin_line_degrees` | The skin line's angle. |
592	
593	## Read what the answer says
594	
595	The text always starts with the frame's time and sizes and ends with "Written to …". Anything else worth saying sits between the two.
596	
597	### Graphic problems in the answer
598	
599	When a [graphic](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/) in the frame had a problem, the answer names it, with its frame and what went wrong:
600	
601	- `Graphic "lower-third" failed at frame 12: …`
602	- `Graphic "lower-third" warned at frame 12: …`
603	- `Graphic "lower-third" does not compile: …`
604	
605	A failed graphic draws its error card in the picture.
606	
607	### Waiting for cutout masks
608	
609	A clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) waits up to 30 s for the masks the frame needs. Frame Job starts making them as soon as the cutout is set, on your Mac.
610	
611	Past 30 s the clip is drawn whole, and the answer says so: "Clip 12 is drawn uncut: its person masks were not ready within 30 s." For a picture with its subject set to foreground, it says "its foreground masks".
612	
613	So after setting a cutout, read that sentence before trusting the frame. [`analyze_cutout`](/mcp/tools-analysis/) can wait for the masks first.
614	
615	### A cursor that can't be drawn
616	
617	A screen recording's cursor is drawn from its cursor file. When the file can't be read, the clip draws without one and the answer says "The cursor of media 5 is not drawn: …".
618	
619	## Frames from an HDR project
620	
621	In an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), the frame depends on the format:
622	
623	| What you ask for | What you get |
624	| --- | --- |
625	| `png` | 16-bit, labelled BT.2100 HLG |
626	| `heic` | 10-bit, labelled BT.2100 HLG |
627	| `jpeg` | The project's SDR version, labelled BT.709 |
628	| Any format with `sdr_version` | The project's SDR version, labelled BT.709 |
629	
630	Scopes read the picture drawn. On the HLG picture they read the HLG signal, and on the SDR version they read as an SDR project's do.
631	
632	On the HLG signal:
633	
634	- Each scope's JSON adds `signal: "hlg"`.
635	- The waveform, parade and histogram JSON add `scale`: `unit` (`cd/m²`), `ticks` (each with `percent`, `level` and `nits`), `reference_white_percent` (75) and `clip_percent` (100).
636	- Luma takes Rec. 2020's weights, and the vectorscope takes Rec. 2020's matrix and targets.
637	- The text says so. The waveform's reads "reference white at 75 %, 203 cd/m², and 100 % at 1,000 cd/m²".
638	
639	See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/) and [Export HDR](/hdr/export-hdr/).
640	
641	## When it won't render
642	
643	Nothing is drawn in these cases, and the answer says why.
644	
645	| It says | What to do |
646	| --- | --- |
647	| "No frame at … Either the time is past the end of the timeline, the media is missing, or the timeline is empty." | Check `duration` and `missing_media` in [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/). |
648	| "There is no folder at … to write into." | Create the folder, or choose another `path`. |
649	| "path must name a file to write — omit it for a temporary one." | The `path` was empty. |
650	| "format must be one of png, jpeg, heic (got …)." | Use one of the three. |
651	| "max_width must be 16…8192 px (got …)." | Use a width in range. |
652	| "selection must name an adjustment clip of this project; clip … is not one." | Pass an adjustment clip's id. An adjustment clip can't be inside a nest, so close any open nest first. |
653	| "vectorscope_zoom must be 1, 2 or 4 (got …)." | Use one of the three. |
654	| "vectorscope_zoom needs vectorscope: true." | Add `vectorscope: true`. |

670	
671	Use these three tools to write the timeline to a file from an agent, follow the job and stop it. `export` doesn't wait for the file. It checks the request, puts a job on the Export Queue and returns at once, and the agent then asks how the job is going until it ends.
672	
673	<AtAGlance
674	  menu={['File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
675	  keys="⌘E"
676	  where="The export sheet's Add to Queue, and each row's Cancel in the Export Queue"
677	  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
678	/>
679	
680	## Write a file
681	
682	<Steps>
683	
684	1. Call `export` with a preset and a path. It returns straight away.
685	
686	   ```json
687	   { "preset": "h264", "path": "/Volumes/Edits/cut", "size": "1080p" }
688	   ```
689	
690	   ```json
691	   { "export_id": 3, "path": "/Volumes/Edits/cut.mp4", "status": "running" }
692	   ```
693	
694	2. Call `export_status` with that `export_id`, pause, and call it again until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
695	
696	3. Read the `done` result. It says what the file holds, including the loudness it measured and any warnings.
697	
698	</Steps>
699	
700	To stop the job, call `cancel_export`. The job shows in **Window ▸ Export Queue** like any other, but the window doesn't open by itself.
701	
702	## Export
703	
704	`export` does what **File ▸ Export…** does with **Add to Queue**, and it writes the file the same way, so an agent's file and a person's match. It takes the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)'s controls in the sheet's own terms, apart from the frame rate.
705	
706	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
707	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
708	| `preset` | string | Yes | The encoding: a container and a codec. See [Presets](#presets). |
709	| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write, such as `~/Movies/cut.mp4`. See [Path handling](#path-handling). |
710	| `size` | string or `[width, height]` | No | The output size. See [Size](#size). |
711	| `range` | string | No | `project` for the whole timeline, or `in_out` for the in and out range. See [Range](#range). |
712	| `video_bitrate` | integer | No | Target video rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
713	| `audio_bitrate` | integer | No | Target AAC or Opus rate in bits per second. See [Exact bitrates](#exact-bitrates). |
714	| `loudness_lufs` | number | No | Normalise the whole mix to this loudness, −70 to 0. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
715	| `peak_dbtp` | number | No | The master limiter's ceiling, −20 to 0. See [Peak dBTP](#peak-dbtp). |
716	| `audio_bits` | integer | No | 16 or 24, for WAV and AIFF. See [Audio bits](#audio-bits). |
717	| `stems` | string | No | `tracks` or `names`, to write stems beside an audio mix. See [Stems](#stems). |
718	| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draw the project timecode over the picture, on top of everything. Off by default. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
719	| `dynamic_range` | string | No | `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`, in an HLG project. See [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range). |
720	| `encoder_speed` | string | No | `faster`, `balanced` or `smaller`, for AV1. See [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
721	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to export, as `get_project` reports it. Without it, the frontmost project. |
722	
723	It returns `{export_id, path, status}`. `path` is the file that will be written, with `~` expanded and the extension corrected. `status` is `running` if the job started at once, or `queued` if it's waiting.
724	
725	Jobs in the queue run one at a time, behind anything already there. A job writes the project as it stood when `export` was called, so later edits don't reach it. Calling `export` pauses playback in that project's window.
726	
727	`export` takes no `scope`. With a [nest](/mcp/nests/) open it still writes the project's timeline, not the nest's.
728	
729	## Export status
730	
731	`export_status` reports how a job is going, as its row in the Export Queue does, and it never waits. Pass the `export_id`, which is an integer of 1 or more.
732	
733	Every result carries `export_id`, `status`, `path` and `elapsed`, the seconds since `export` was called, or from then to the finish once the job has ended. The rest depends on the status.
734	
735	| `status` | Also carries |
736	| --- | --- |
737	| `queued` | `waiting` while an AV1 or VP9 job is held for memory. `estimated_seconds` on `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`. |
738	| `running` | `progress`, from 0 to 1. `phase` while the export names one, which is "Measuring loudness…" during the first pass over the mix. `estimated_seconds` on the same four presets. |
739	| `done` | What the file holds, in the next table. |
740	| `failed` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
741	| `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |
742	
743	`estimated_seconds` is the export sheet's estimate of the whole export in whole seconds, and it's only an estimate.
744	
745	`waiting` is a sentence such as "Waiting for memory: AV1 and VP9 exports running now hold about 2.1 GB of the 8.0 GB this Mac allows them, and this one needs about 7.0 GB." AV1 and VP9 exports may hold a quarter of this Mac's memory between them, though a job with no other running always starts. While one is held, a later job in the queue may run first.
746	
747	A `done` result adds these keys.
748	
749	| Key | What it holds |
750	| --- | --- |
751	| `ok` | `true`. |
752	| `bytes` | The file's size. |
753	| `preset`, `container`, `codec` | What was written. |
754	| `width`, `height` | The file's size in pixels. These are reported on audio presets too, where they mean nothing. |
755	| `fps` | The rate as `[num, den]`, such as `[30, 1]`. |
756	| `start`, `duration` | The part of the timeline written, in [ticks](/mcp/units-and-ids/). |
757	| `burn_in_timecode` | Whether the argument was on. |
758	| `dynamic_range` | The picture written: `hlg`, `pq` or `sdr`. Only for a video preset in an HLG project. |
759	| `encoder_speed` | The speed used. Only on `av1` and `av1_webm`. |
760	| `audio_bits` | The depth written. Only on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. |
761	| `stems` | `[{name, tracks, path}]`, one per file beside the mix. Only when `stems` was asked for. |
762	| `loudness` | What the mix measured. See [The loudness report](#the-loudness-report). |
763	| `graphic_warnings` | `[{name, frame, message}]`, each distinct warning a graphic gave while the file was drawn. Collecting stops after 64 distinct reports, so a noisy graphic's list can be cut short. `frame` is the graphic's own frame, or `null`. Absent when there were none. |
764	| `cursor_warnings` | `[{media, path, message}]`, each media whose cursor file couldn't be drawn. Its clips were written without a cursor. Absent when there were none. |
765	
766	## Cancel export
767	
768	`cancel_export` stops a job, as the row's **Cancel** does, and returns what `export_status` would. Pass the `export_id`.
769	
770	| The job is | What happens |
771	| --- | --- |
772	| Queued | It's cancelled before it starts. The result reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled before it started." |
773	| Running | It stops and its half-written file is removed. The result may still read `running` until writing has stopped, and `export_status` then reads `cancelled`, with the reason "Cancelled." |
774	| Finished | It's left alone, and its file stays. The result is the finished job's. |
775	
776	## Export id and its lifetime
777	
778	An `export_id` is known until Frame Job quits. Removing a finished row from the Export Queue, or choosing **Clear Finished**, doesn't lose it, so an agent can still read how that job ended.
779	
780	An id belongs to the launch, not to a project, so `export_status` and `cancel_export` don't need `project`. Only ids that `export` returned are known. A job a person queued from the sheet has no id an agent can follow. Any other number returns the error "No export this launch has export_id 7 — ids come from export and last until Frame Job quits."
781	
782	## Refusals and failures
783	
784	A problem Frame Job can see from the request comes back from `export` itself as an error, and nothing is queued.
785	
786	| The request | What stops it |
787	| --- | --- |
788	| An empty timeline | "There is nothing on the timeline to export." |
789	| A folder that doesn't exist | "There is no folder at … to write into." Frame Job never creates the folder. |
790	| An unknown preset | The error lists all the presets. |
791	| An unknown `size`, or one it can't read | The error lists the sizes. See [Size](#size). |
792	| `range` of `in_out` with no range set | "This project has no in/out range — set one with set_range `{start, end}`, or export with range \"project\"." |
793	| A number out of range, or a word it doesn't know | The error names the argument and the value. |
794	| An option the preset doesn't have | See [Audio bits](#audio-bits), [Stems](#stems), [Dynamic range](#dynamic-range) and [Encoder speed](#encoder-speed). |
795	| A graphic clip in the range with no module, or a module that doesn't compile | "The export was not started: the graphic "…" does not compile — …. Fix the module and export again." A clip with no module reads "has no module in graphics/" in place of "does not compile — …". It names each graphic and its first error, and it covers graphics inside nests. An audio-only preset draws no graphics, so it isn't stopped by one. |
796	
797	Anything that goes wrong after that comes back from `export_status` as `failed`, with the sentence in `reason`. Check for it even when `export` answered cleanly.
798	
799	| What went wrong | The `reason` |
800	| --- | --- |
801	| A size of another shape on a transparent preset | "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…". See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets). |
802	| A stem's file would be one of the project's media | "The stem “…” would replace media this project uses; export under another name." |
803	| A graphic fails while it's drawn | "The export was stopped at frame … of the graphic "…": …. No file was written." |
804	| A retimed clip's sound, an isolated voice or a voice effect couldn't be rendered | The sentence names the clip and the reason. |
805	| A cut-out clip's masks couldn't be made | "Clip …'s person masks could not be made: …." A picture cut out by **Foreground** says foreground masks. |
806	| A clip's gate, leveller or de-esser needs a loudness that hasn't been measured | "Clip …'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…". Wait for the clip's analysis, then export again. |
807	| This Mac has no encoder for the preset | "This Mac cannot export with the “…” preset." |
808	
809	A graphic's warnings are different: they don't stop the export, and they arrive as `graphic_warnings` in the `done` result.
810	
811	## Presets
812	
813	There are 15 presets, one per encoding. A preset says nothing about size. These are the rows of the sheet's **Format** control, described in [Choose a format](/export/formats/). A wrong id's error lists them all.
814	
815	| Preset | In the sheet | File | Picture | Sound |
816	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

818	| `hevc` | HEVC (MP4) | `.mp4` | 8-bit | AAC |
819	| `hevc_alpha` | HEVC with Alpha (MOV) | `.mov` | 8-bit with transparency. Safari's transparent movie. | AAC |
820	| `hevc_10bit` | HEVC 10-bit (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
821	| `av1` | AV1 (MP4) | `.mp4` | 10-bit | AAC |
822	| `av1_webm` | AV1 (WebM) | `.webm` | 10-bit | Opus |
823	| `vp9_webm` | VP9 (WebM) | `.webm` | 8-bit (Profile 0) for an SDR picture, 10-bit (Profile 2) for HLG and PQ. One speed. | Opus |
824	| `vp9_alpha_webm` | VP9 with Alpha (WebM) | `.webm` | Always 8-bit, with transparency. The transparent movie Chrome and Firefox play. | Opus |
825	| `prores_422` | ProRes 422 (MOV) | `.mov` | 10-bit. An editing master. | 16-bit LPCM |
826	| `prores_4444` | ProRes 4444 (MOV) | `.mov` | 12-bit with transparency. A master. | 16-bit LPCM |
827	| `audio_m4a` | Audio only (M4A) | `.m4a` | None | AAC |
828	| `audio_wav` | Audio only (WAV) | `.wav` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
829	| `audio_aiff` | Audio only (AIFF) | `.aiff` | None | 48 kHz LPCM, 16 or 24 bits |
830	| `gif` | Animated GIF | `.gif` | 256 colours. Fits inside 480 × 270 unless `size` says otherwise. | None |
831	| `apng` | Animated PNG | `.png` | Lossless, with transparency. Fits inside 960 × 540 unless `size` says otherwise. | None |
832	
833	Macs before M3 can't play `av1` and `av1_webm` back.
834	
835	## Frame rate
836	
837	There's no frame-rate argument, so the sheet's [frame rate](/export/frame-rate/) control has no agent equivalent. An export runs at the project's rate, `gif` at 12.5 fps and `apng` at 25 fps. The `done` result's `fps` says which, with 12.5 fps as `[25, 2]`.
838	
839	## Path handling
840	
841	The folder must exist. A `~` at the start is expanded, and an existing file at the path is replaced.
842	
843	The file always ends in the preset's extension.
844	
845	| `path` | `preset` | Writes | Why |
846	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
847	| `cut.mp4` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | The extension is already right. |
848	| `cut` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | With no extension, it's added. |
849	| `cut.mov` | `h264` | `cut.mp4` | A different media extension is replaced. |
850	| `Talk v1.2` | `h264` | `Talk v1.2.mp4` | Any other suffix stays part of the name. |
851	| `cut.webm` | `h264` | `cut.webm.mp4` | `.webm` isn't one of the extensions Frame Job replaces. |
852	| `cut.mp4` | `av1_webm` | `cut.webm` | `.mp4` is. |
853	
854	The extensions it replaces are `.mov`, `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.m4a`, `.mp3`, `.wav`, `.aif`, `.aiff`, `.caf`, `.framejob`, `.srt`, `.vtt`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.heic` and `.gif`. The returned `path` is always the file that gets written.
855	
856	## Size
857	
858	`size` is the sheet's **Size** control. See [Export size](/export/size/) for what the sizes mean to a person.
859	
860	| `size` | In the sheet | What it writes |
861	| --- | --- | --- |
862	| `document` | Document size | The project's own size. The default on every movie preset. |
863	| `2160p` | 4K | A short edge of 2160 pixels. |
864	| `1440p` | 1440p | A short edge of 1440 pixels. |
865	| `1080p` | 1080p | A short edge of 1080 pixels. |
866	| `720p` | 720p | A short edge of 720 pixels. |
867	| `preset` | GIF default, APNG default | The format's cap. `gif` and `apng` only, where it's the default. |
868	| `[width, height]` | Custom… | Exactly this size, from 16 to 8192 pixels on each edge. |
869	
870	The number is always the short edge, and the long edge follows the project's shape, rounded to an even number. A vertical project's `1080p` is 1080 × 1920. Every size means the same on every project, so a 1920 × 1080 project's `1080p` is its own size, and a size larger than the project scales it up.
871	
872	A movie is written at exactly the size asked for. If the shape differs from the project's by more than a pixel, the picture is letterboxed. Within a pixel, it fills the frame instead.
873	
874	- **Even edges.** Every preset but `prores_4444`, `gif` and `apng` needs even dimensions, so an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller. That covers `document` on a project with an odd edge. The `done` result's `width` and `height` are the file's.
875	- **GIF and APNG.** A size is a box the picture is fitted inside, keeping its shape and never scaling up. A vertical 1080 × 1920 project's GIF default comes out at 152 × 270.
876	- **Audio presets.** A size has no effect, and `preset` isn't one of their sizes.
877	- **Transparent movies.** A `[width, height]` of another shape fails. See [Transparent presets](#transparent-presets).
878	
879	An unknown size returns an error with the list, for example "No export size is called "480p" for h264. The sizes are: document, 2160p, 1440p, 1080p, 720p — or pass [width, height]." A custom size outside 16 to 8192 pixels is an error too. It isn't clamped.
880	
881	## Range
882	
883	`range` is the sheet's **Range** control. `project`, the default, writes the whole timeline. `in_out` writes the range set with `set_range`, and `export` returns an error when there's no range. See [Export a range](/export/range/).
884	
885	The range is snapped to the export's frame grid and kept inside the project. A range that comes to nothing is an error too.
886	
887	`burn_in_timecode` shows project time even in a range export, so a file written from 00:00:10:00 begins at 00:00 with a burn-in that reads 00:00:10:00.
888	
889	## Exact bitrates
890	
891	The sheet offers [quality](/export/quality/) tiers. An agent sets the rates directly, in bits per second, so 8 Mbps is `8000000`. Each must be a whole number from 1 to 4,294,967,295.
892	
893	`video_bitrate` is the target video rate. Without it, Frame Job works out a rate from the frame size and frame rate. ProRes, GIF and APNG ignore it, because ProRes is fixed by its profile and the other two have no bitrate.
894	
895	On the AV1 and VP9 presets it works differently:
896	
897	- **`av1` and `av1_webm`.** It's a soft cap. The encoder works at a constant quality matched to HEVC at that rate, and the file usually comes in well under it. Very detailed footage can go up to about 1.25 times over. Without it, the quality is matched to HEVC at 0.07 bits per pixel per frame.
898	- **`vp9_webm`.** It's a soft cap too, matched to HEVC, or HEVC 10-bit in an HDR export. Up to about 1.15 times over was measured.
899	- **`vp9_alpha_webm`.** It's the same soft cap on the picture's stream alone. The transparency's stream comes on top, at a constant quality.
900	
901	`audio_bitrate` is the AAC or Opus rate, 192 kbps when absent. Opus takes the nearest rate its encoder offers. ProRes, WAV and AIFF ignore it, because they write LPCM.
902	
903	## The loudness report
904	
905	Every export with sound measures its own mix and reports it as `loudness` in the `done` result, normalised or not. GIF and APNG have no sound, and a timeline with no sound has nothing to measure, so `loudness` is absent from both.
906	
907	`loudness_lufs` normalises the whole mix to an integrated loudness, from −70 to 0. The sheet's [Loudness](/export/loudness/) rows are −14 for streaming, −16 for podcasts and −23 for EBU R 128 broadcast, and an agent can ask for any value, such as −14.5. The export measures itself first, then applies one gain to everything, through the master limiter. The file lands on the target with its loudest peaks limited, rather than the whole mix held down. GIF and APNG ignore it.
908	
909	| Key | What it holds |
910	| --- | --- |
911	| `summary` | The same line the queue row and the progress sheet show, such as "Peak −1.0 dBTP · −16.0 LUFS", with " · peaks limited by 8.6 dB" when the limiter took 0.05 dB or more. |
912	| `integrated_lufs` | The file's integrated loudness. Absent when it has none, and `summary` then says "loudness not measurable". |
913	| `true_peak_dbtp` | The file's true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
914	| `sample_peak_dbfs` | The file's sample peak, never above the true peak. `null` when it's silent. |
915	| `gain_db` | The gain applied to reach the target. |
916	| `ceiling_dbtp` | The master limiter's ceiling. |
917	| `limited_db` | How far the limiter turned the loudest peak down. |
918	| `capped_by_gain` | `true` when the +40 dB limit on the gain decided it, so the file may be short of the target. |
919	| `target_lufs` | The `loudness_lufs` asked for. Absent when none was. |
920	
921	A programme shorter than one 400 ms measuring block, or one too quiet to pass the standard's gate, has a peak and no integrated loudness. Digital silence reads "Silent" in `summary`.
922	
923	## Peak dBTP
924	
925	Every export with sound goes through a master limiter, so the file's true peak stays at or under a ceiling. `peak_dbtp` sets that ceiling, from −20 to 0. It's −1 when absent, which is the sheet's fixed value. 0 is the loosest, and there's no way to turn the limiter off.
926	
927	You can pass it with or without `loudness_lufs`. `limited_db` in the [report](#the-loudness-report) says how far the limiter turned the loudest peak down.
928	
929	## Audio bits
930	
931	`audio_bits` is the sheet's [Bit depth](/export/bit-depth/) control: 16, the default, or 24. It's rounded once from the mix and never dithered, and the `done` result repeats it.
932	
933	It works on `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff` only. On any other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no bit depth; audio_bits applies to audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset. ProRes keeps 16-bit sound. Any other number is an error, whatever the preset.
934	
935	## Stems
936	
937	`stems` also writes [stems](/export/stems/) beside the mix, on `audio_m4a`, `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. It's the sheet's **Stems** control.
938	
939	| `stems` | What it writes |
940	| --- | --- |
941	| `tracks` | One file per heard track. |
942	| `names` | One file per track name. Heard tracks whose names match, ignoring case, share a file, and an unnamed track gets its own. |
943	
944	A track is heard when it has sound in it and isn't muted or silenced by another track's solo. Each stem is named `<file> - <track name>.<ext>`, beside the mix, so `mix.wav` and a track called Voice give `mix - Voice.wav`. An unnamed track is `Track N`, and [Stem file names](/export/stems/#stem-file-names) has the other cases.
945	
946	A stem holds its tracks' sound before the master, with no loudness gain and no limiter, so the stems add up to the mix wherever the master changed nothing. Any file already at a stem's name is replaced.
947	
948	The `done` result lists each one as `stems [{name, tracks, path}]`. `tracks` holds the ids of the timeline tracks in that stem.
949	
950	- On any other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no stems; stems applies to audio_m4a, audio_wav and audio_aiff", naming the preset.
951	- With no track heard, the error is "stems: no track is heard, so there is no stem to write".
952	- If a stem's file would be one of the project's media, the job fails before any stem is written, and `export_status` gives the reason.
953	- A failed or cancelled job leaves neither the mix nor any stem behind.
954	
955	## Dynamic range
956	
957	`dynamic_range` chooses the picture an [HLG project](/hdr/dynamic-range/) writes. It's the sheet's **Dynamic Range** control.
958	
959	| `dynamic_range` | What it writes |
960	| --- | --- |
961	| `hlg` | BT.2100 HLG, with no Dolby Vision. The default on the presets that carry HDR. |
962	| `pq` | HDR10: BT.2100 PQ at 1,000 cd/m², with a P3-D65 mastering display of 0.005–1,000 cd/m², MaxCLL 1,000 and MaxFALL 0. |
963	| `sdr` | The project's SDR version. |
964	
965	The presets that carry HDR are `hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422` and `prores_4444`. Every other video preset in an HLG project writes the SDR version, `vp9_alpha_webm` included, and audio presets ignore the argument.
966	
967	- `hlg` or `pq` on another video preset returns the error "h264 is 8-bit and writes the SDR version; export dynamic_range "pq" as hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 or prores_4444".
968	- `hlg` or `pq` in an SDR project returns the error "dynamic_range "pq" needs an HLG project; set_canvas output "hlg" first".
969	- `sdr` in an SDR project changes nothing.
970	
971	Once a job is `done`, `dynamic_range` in the result names the picture that was written. An SDR project's result has no such key.
972	
973	## Encoder speed
974	
975	`encoder_speed` trades export time for file size on `av1` and `av1_webm`. It's the sheet's [Speed](/export/encoder-speed/) control, and the `done` result names the one used.
976	
977	| `encoder_speed` | SVT-AV1 preset | What it does |
978	| --- | --- | --- |
979	| `faster` | 8 | The quickest. |
980	| `balanced` | 6 | The default. |
981	| `smaller` | 4 | The smallest file for the picture, and the slowest. |
982	
983	On every other preset `export` returns the error "h264 has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm", naming the preset. That includes `vp9_webm` and `vp9_alpha_webm`, which have one speed.
984	
985	## Transparent presets
986	
987	Four presets keep a transparent canvas transparent: `prores_4444`, `hevc_alpha`, `vp9_alpha_webm` and `apng`. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). A GIF can show a fully transparent pixel, but it has no alpha channel, so nothing partial survives.
988	
989	On the three movie presets, a `[width, height]` of a different shape from the canvas can't be written, because the padding would destroy the alpha channel. `export` queues the job, and `export_status` then reads `failed` with a reason that names both sizes. The shape is judged after an odd edge is evened, and within a pixel the picture fills the frame, so a size in the canvas's own proportions always works, at any scale. Every named size already has the canvas's shape.
990	
991	`apng` fits its picture inside the size instead, so this doesn't apply to it.
992

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

`set_video` is the one tool behind everything a clip's picture does: where it sits, how it's cropped, its effects, its motion and its grade. It takes a list of clips and a patch, an object holding only the properties you want to change. This page lists every key a patch can hold.

<AtAGlance
  tools="set_video"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Picture sub-tab', 'Clip tab ▸ Color sub-tab', 'Dragging on the canvas']}
/>

## `set_video`

Merges a patch into each clip's own video properties, as one undo step however many clips it names. It mirrors the Clip tab's [Picture sub-tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) and [Color sub-tab](/color/color-tab/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change, at least one. `get_project` lists their ids. |
| `patch` | object | Yes | The properties to change. The rest of this page lists its keys. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

```json
{ "clips": [12, 14], "patch": { "opacity": 0.8, "shadow": { "blur": 20 } } }
```

**How a patch merges.** A key you leave out keeps its value, inside a nested object too, so `{shadow: {blur: 20}}` keeps the shadow's colour, angle and distance. On a clip that has no shadow yet, the keys you left out take the defaults listed below. `shadow`, `chroma`, `reflection`, `spotlight`, `motion`, `look`, `cursor`, `cutout` and `hide_silent` set to `null` clear that property. `filters` and `obscure` are lists, so each replaces whole: send the full list, or `[]` to clear it. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

`record_screen` is **File ▸ New Recording…** without the panel. An agent says how many seconds to record, the call runs for that long, and the recording lands in the project the way one made with the panel does. There's no countdown, and the tool never asks for a permission.

<AtAGlance

  tools="record_screen"
  needs={[
