  ]}
/>

## Record the screen

The smallest call names only `seconds`:

```json
{ "seconds": 30 }
```

That records the main display for 30 seconds with its system sound, leaves Frame Job's own windows out of the picture, and lands the movie at the playhead of the front project. A recording then goes through these stages:

- **It starts at once.** There's no countdown and no panel.
- **It writes to disk.** The file goes to `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`, named for example `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov`, and it's never stored inside the project. A name that's already taken gets ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.
- **It lands.** The movie becomes ordinary media, and a clip goes at the playhead on the front track of whatever is open, a [nest](/mcp/nests/) included. When that track has no room there, Frame Job adds a new track in front of everything. This is one undo step, **Add Recording**.
- **It returns.** The call comes back once the recording is finished, imported and placed. See [What it answers](#what-it-answers).

47	## Choose a source
48	
49	`source` says what's recorded.
50	
51	| `source` | What it records | Files |
52	| --- | --- | --- |
53	| `screen` | A display or a window. The default. | `Screen Recording <date> at <time>.mov` |
54	| `voice_over` | The default microphone alone, with no picture. | `Voice-over <date> at <time>.m4a` |
55	| `camera` | A camera alone, with no screen. | `Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov` |
56	
57	An argument the source can't use isn't ignored. The call stops with a message naming it, and nothing is recorded. A JSON null counts as not given. This is what each source takes:
58	
59	| Argument | `screen` | `voice_over` | `camera` |
60	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
61	| `seconds`, `project`, `path`, `place`, `enhance` | Yes | Yes | Yes |
62	| `microphone` | Yes | Implied, and `false` stops the call | Yes |
63	| `rate` | Yes | Yes, for a new project's canvas | No |
64	| `camera`, `camera_format` | Yes, [beside the screen](#record-a-camera-beside-the-screen) | No | Yes |
65	| `camera_layout`, `camera_cutout` | Yes, with `camera` | No | No |
66	| `display`, `window`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows` | Yes | No | No |
67	| `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `cursor`, `keys` | Yes | No | No |
68	| `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing` | Yes | No | No |

70	## The arguments
71	
72	Only `seconds` is required. The sections further down cover the arguments for [voice-overs](#record-a-voice-over), [cameras](#record-a-camera-alone) and the [steps after landing](#run-steps-after-it-lands).
73	
74	### Length and source
75	
76	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
77	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
78	| `seconds` | number | Required | How long to record, from 1 to 600 seconds. It's wall-clock time, so a [pause](#a-person-can-pause-or-stop-it) shortens what's recorded. |
79	| `source` | `screen`, `voice_over` or `camera` | `screen` | What's recorded. See [Choose a source](#choose-a-source). |
80	
81	### Display or window
82	
83	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
84	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
85	| `display` | whole number, 0 or more | `0` | Which display, as an index into the displays that can be shared, 0 being the main one. Can't be used with `window`. |
86	| `window` | whole number | None | The system window id (`CGWindowID`) of one window to record on its own, at that window's own size, instead of a display. Can't be used with `display`. |
87	| `include_framejob_windows` | boolean | `false` | Puts Frame Job's own windows, the editor and the preview, in a display recording. By default they're left out. With `window` it changes nothing. Frame Job's own sound stays out either way. |
88	| `size` | `nominal` or `best`, in any case | `nominal` | `nominal` records a display's point size, and `best` its pixel size, twice the points on a Retina display. An odd dimension is rounded up to even. |
89	| `rate` | `30` or `60` | `60` | The most frames a second the file may hold, and the canvas rate of a new project the recording opens as. A camera alone records at its format's rate instead. |
90	
91	A screen recording's frame rate is whatever the screen did, because a frame arrives only when something changes. A mostly still screen reports a low, fractional rate. That's the file and not a fault, and the picture holds its last frame to the end of the sound.
92	
93	### Sound
94	
95	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
96	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
97	| `system_audio` | boolean | `true` | Records what the Mac plays as the movie's one stereo 48 kHz track. It takes in every app but Frame Job, so the timeline can play meanwhile and stay out of it. `false` writes a movie with no audio track, and `has_audio` reads false. |
98	| `microphone` | boolean | `false` | Also records the default microphone, to a second file beside the movie named `<movie name> (Microphone).m4a`. |
99	
100	The microphone's file lands as its own clip on a new track at the back named **Microphone**, lined up with the picture by the measured `mic_offset`. When the microphone began first and there's no room for it there, the clip's head is trimmed rather than the clip landing late.
101	
102	A microphone that fails doesn't fail the recording. The picture lands, the stretch it failed in has no `mic_path`, and `mic_problem` and the `note` say why. See [System audio and the microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/).
103	
104	### Pointer and keys
105	
106	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
107	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
108	| `cursor` | `separate` or `in_picture` | `separate` | `separate` keeps the pointer out of the movie, and Frame Job draws it on the clip from the cursor file, where you can restyle it. `in_picture` has macOS draw the pointer into the movie. |
109	| `show_clicks` | boolean | `false` | Shows each mouse click. With `in_picture`, a ring is drawn around each click into the movie. With `separate`, the clips land with click ripples on, drawn by Frame Job. |
110	| `keys` | `off` or `shortcuts` | `off` | `shortcuts` writes keyboard shortcuts into the cursor files, and needs the Input Monitoring permission. |
111	
112	Every display or window recording writes a cursor file beside each movie, named `<movie name>.fjcursor`, holding the pointer's path, its clicks and scrolls. A problem with it never fails the recording. `segments` reports it as `cursor_problem`, and the note repeats it. A `separate` stretch with no cursor file has no pointer at all, and the note ends "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."
113	
114	With `keys: "shortcuts"`, the file records each shortcut pressed with ⌘ or ⌃, or with ⌥ and an arrow, Delete, Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc, spelled like `cmd+shift+4`. Every other key is a mark of the time alone, never which key was typed. Nothing is written while an app holds secure input. See [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) and [The cursor in a recording](/recording/cursor/).
115	
116	### Where it goes
117	
118	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
119	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
120	| `path` | string | `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings` | A folder to record into, created if it doesn't exist. It names the folder and never the file, and the answer's `path` is the file that was written. A leading `~` means your home folder, and a blank string means the default folder. |
121	| `project` | string | The front project | The open project to land in, as `get_project` reports its path. One that names nothing open stops the call. It never turns into a new project. |
122	| `place` | boolean | `true` | Puts clips on the timeline, in one undo step with the media. `false` adds the recording to the media list only, and the note says to place it with `add_clip`. |
123	
124	In a new project `place: false` has no effect, because the project is made from the recording's picture. Its clips are on the timeline, one for each stretch and the first at 0, and the `note` says so.
125	
126	## Record a voice-over
127	
128	`source: "voice_over"` records the default microphone alone, as the panel's **Microphone Only** does. `microphone: true` is implied. The only permission it reads is the Microphone one, and it looks nothing up.
129	
130	Each stretch between pauses is its own `.m4a` file. The files land touching, from the playhead, on one new track at the back named **Microphone**, in one undo step, **Add Recording**. In a new project the first file starts the project, on a 1920 × 1080 canvas at `rate`, and later files touch it on its one track.
131	
132	The answer's `path` is the first `.m4a`, its `width` and `height` are 0, and it has no `mic_path`. A microphone that stops on its own ends the voice-over, what it wrote lands, and `mic_problem` and the `note` say so.
133	
134	See [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/).
135	
136	## Record a camera alone
137	
138	`source: "camera"` records one camera, with no screen, and lands it as a screen recording's picture lands. It reads the Camera permission and never the Screen Recording one. `microphone: true` adds the default microphone as a second file, as for a screen.
139	
140	Recording starts once the camera has settled at its frame rate, which takes up to a second, and `seconds` counts from its first frame. While it runs, a recorder panel left open with a camera chosen reads "The camera is recording." in its preview. The movie holds no sound, so `has_audio` is false. In a new project the canvas is the file's size at the format's frame rate, rounded.
141	
142	### Choose the camera and its format
143	
144	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
145	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
146	| `camera` | string | The default camera with `source: "camera"`, none with `source: "screen"` | A camera's unique id, or its name in any case. Blank counts as not given. |
147	| `camera_format` | string | `best` | The format to record at, in any case: `1920x1080@30`, or `1920x1080` for that size's highest frame rate, or `best`. Blank or null means `best`. |
148	
149	The default camera is the Mac's preferred camera, then the first built-in one, then the first connected. `best` is the largest size wider than tall that runs at 30 fps or more, at its highest frame rate.
150	
151	An unknown camera stops the call with a list of every camera connected, by name and id. With none connected the message is "No camera is connected." A format the camera doesn't have stops the call with a list of its formats. With `source: "screen"`, `camera_format` needs `camera`: "With source screen, camera_format needs camera — name the camera to record beside the screen."
152	
153	The answer carries `camera`, with the camera's `name`, `id` and `format`, spelled like `1920x1080@30`. It adds `problem` when the camera stopped on its own, which ends the recording with `stopped_by: "system_stopped"` and lands what it wrote, and `note` when the camera hadn't settled by the time recording began. The top-level `note` repeats both.
154	
155	See [Record a camera](/recording/record-a-camera/).
156	
157	## Record a camera beside the screen
158	
159	`source: "screen"` with `camera` records that camera at the same time as the screen, for a talking head over a screencast. It's the panel's **Record the camera too** box, and `camera_format` works as it does for a camera alone.
160	
161	Each stretch gets a camera movie named after its screen movie, like `Screen Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33 (Camera).mov`. The camera files land in the same undo step as the screen, on one new track named **Camera** in front of the screen's. Each camera clip starts where its screen clip starts, moved by that stretch's measured `camera_offset`. A camera usually starts a little before the screen, and then the clip's first frames are trimmed rather than the clip starting early. A camera clip never starts before its screen clip, and never overlaps the camera clip before it.
162	
163	With `place: false` the camera files are added to the media list only, with no clip and no **Camera** track. In a new project the first movie starts the project, and its camera is one undo step: **Add Camera**, or **Add Camera and Microphone** with a microphone, for a recording that wasn't paused.
164	
165	The Camera permission is checked before the Screen Recording one. See [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/).
166	
167	### Lay the camera out
168	
169	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
170	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
171	| `camera_layout` | see below | `corner_square` | How each camera clip lands, laid out from its first frame with its stretch's screen clip, as the panel's **Layout** does. |
172	| `camera_cutout` | boolean | `false` | Runs [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) on the camera clips right after the landing, as the panel's **Remove the camera's background when it lands** box does. |
173	
174	| `camera_layout` | Panel's name | What you get |
175	| --- | --- | --- |
176	| `corner_square` | Corner | The bottom-right corner, scaled to fit a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % safe area. |
177	| `corner_rounded` | Rounded Corner | The same corner with rounded edges. |
178	| `corner_circle` | Circle | The same corner as a circle. |
179	| `side_by_side` | Side by Side | The screen and the camera next to each other. |
180	| `camera_full` | Camera Full | The camera fills the canvas. |
181	
182	The layout reaches no further than the later end of the two clips. When a stretch's screen clip is missing, or isn't playing where its camera starts, that camera goes in the bottom-right corner instead. Either way it stays an ordinary clip you can move. [Camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/) has the rest.
183	
184	Both arguments need `camera`, and neither works with `source: "voice_over"` or `"camera"`. `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout: true` also need `place: true`. Frame Job checks all of this before it reads any permission, and the message says what's missing. For example: "With source screen, camera_layout needs camera — name the camera to record beside the screen."
185	
186	## Run steps after it lands
187	
188	These arguments run a command over the recording once it has landed. Each is its own undo step, so undoing one keeps the recording, and they run in the order of this table. The landing itself is the same with or without them.
189	
190	| Argument | What it runs | On which clips | Undo step | Needs |
191	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
192	| `camera_cutout` | Remove Background | The camera clips | **Remove Background** | `camera`, `place: true` |
193	| `enhance` | `enhance_voice` at −16 LUFS | The microphone's clips, or a voice-over's | **Enhance Voice** | `microphone: true` or `source: "voice_over"`, `place: true` |
194	| `auto_zoom` | `auto_zoom` | The screen clips | **Auto Zoom** | `place: true` |
195	| `shortcut_overlays` | `add_shortcut_overlays` | The screen clips | **Add Shortcut Overlays** | `place: true`, `keys: "shortcuts"` |
196	| `speed_up_typing` | `speed_up_typing` | The screen clips | **Speed Up Typing** | `place: true`, `keys: "shortcuts"` |
197	
198	All default to `false`. The last three are the panel's **When it lands:** boxes, **Zoom in on clicks**, **Show shortcuts** and **Speed up typing**. `enhance` is its **Enhance the microphone when it lands** box. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).
199	
200	The screen clips are the clips of the recording's movies that have a cursor file. `enhance` never touches the picture, a camera or the system audio.
201	
202	### What they wait for
203	
204	The call stays open while these run, and `project` in the answer is read after them.
205	
206	- `enhance` waits for the microphone's loudness and speech to be analysed, up to 5 minutes.
207	- `speed_up_typing` waits for the clips' speech to be detected, up to 5 minutes.
208	- `enhance`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` also wait while the project is busy, up to 5 minutes: a drag is under way, or a different nest is open from the one the recording landed in.
209	- `camera_cutout` waits for nothing, and runs straight after the landing.
210	
211	### The values they use
212	
213	They run at the tools' own defaults, never at what the sheets last remembered.
214	
215	| Step | Values |
216	| --- | --- |
217	| `enhance` | −16 LUFS. Call [`enhance_voice`](/mcp/tools-audio/#enhance_voice) afterwards for another target. |
218	| `auto_zoom` | Zoom 2×, Arrive 0.6 s, Stay 2.5 s, Follow the cursor while zoomed on, Zoom on typing on, Replace existing zooms off, Motion blur 50 %. |
219	| `shortcut_overlays` | Bottom, dark, 1.5 s. |
220	| `speed_up_typing` | ×4 for stretches of 3 s or more, Keep pitch on. A speed-up that leaves a clip silent above ×12 is applied, and says so in `audio_note`. |
221	
222	### What each one answers
223	
224	Each step adds its own answer to the call's answer, under its name, or a sentence under `<name>_error` saying why it didn't run. The recording stays either way.
225	
226	| Key | Holds |
227	| --- | --- |
228	| `camera_cutout` | `clips`, the clips that were cut out. |
229	| `camera_cutout_error` | "No camera clip landed on the timeline, so Remove Background did not run." |
230	| `enhance` | What `enhance_voice` answers. |
231	| `enhance_error` | That no microphone clip landed, that it wasn't ready to measure within 5 minutes, that the call was stopped first, or `enhance_voice`'s own reason. |
232	| `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing` | What each tool answers. |
233	| `auto_zoom_error`, `shortcut_overlays_error`, `speed_up_typing_error` | That no screen clip with a cursor file landed, that the project was busy or the speech wasn't detected within 5 minutes, that the call was stopped first, or the tool's own reason. |
234	
235	If `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` or `speed_up_typing` fails for a reason of its own, the next one still runs. When no screen clip landed, a wait runs out or the call is stopped, none of the remaining ones run, and each gets its own sentence.
236	
237	## It never asks for a permission
238	
239	`record_screen` reads each permission and never requests one. It never shows a system prompt, never opens the window picker and never opens System Settings. A person grants them in the panel, usually by pressing **Record** in **File ▸ New Recording…** once. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
240	
241	| Permission | When it's read | What the call says when it's missing |
242	| --- | --- | --- |
243	| Screen Recording | Any `screen` recording | "Screen Recording is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, then relaunch." |
244	| Microphone | `microphone: true` or `source: "voice_over"` | "The microphone is not granted to Frame Job (status: denied)." and the Microphone pane. With status `notDetermined`, it says to press Record in **File ▸ New Recording…** once. The status may also read `restricted`. |
245	| Camera | `source: "camera"` or `camera` | "The camera is not granted to Frame Job (status: denied)." and the Camera pane. With status `notDetermined`, it says to press Record with the Camera source once. |
246	| Input Monitoring | `keys: "shortcuts"` | "Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring." |
247	
248	A Frame Job launched from a shell runs under the terminal's permissions, not its own. Each of these messages then also names the launching process by its pid, and says the permission that counts is that application's, or to relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"`.
249	
250	:::caution
251	macOS periodically asks whether to keep letting Frame Job record, and neither Frame Job nor the tool can see that alert. A capture waiting behind it looks like a hang. When a start or a finish times out, the answer says an alert may be waiting on the screen. Answer it and call again.
252	:::
253	
254	## What's checked first
255	
256	Frame Job checks a call in a fixed order and stops at the first problem. The caller's own mistakes come first, so an agent hears about a mistake even when no permission has been given.
257	
258	1. `seconds` missing or outside 1 to 600.
259	2. `source` unknown, then the arguments that source can't take, including `camera_format`, `camera_layout` or `camera_cutout` on a screen recording without `camera`, then `microphone: false` with a voice-over.
260	3. `display` with `window`, or a `display` or `window` that isn't a valid number.
261	4. `rate` or `size` outside its values.
262	5. `keys` or `cursor` outside its values.
263	6. `enhance` without a microphone, then with `place: false`.
264	7. `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing`, in that order, each with `place: false`, and the last two without `keys: "shortcuts"`.
265	8. `camera_layout` outside its values, then `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout: true` with `place: false`.
266	9. The Microphone permission.
267	10. The Input Monitoring permission.
268	11. A `project` that names nothing open.
269	12. For a camera, the camera lookup, then `camera_format`, then the Camera permission.
270	13. For a screen, the Screen Recording permission.
271	14. The display or window lookup. A window that can't be shared gets "No window with id 123 is shareable." An index past the last display gets "display must be 0…1 (got 3); 2 displays are shareable."
272	
273	When the console is locked or every display is asleep, step 14 says "No display is shareable right now — the console is locked or every display is asleep; nothing can be recorded until one is."
274	
275	After those, a call with a microphone needs a default microphone, or it stops with "No microphone is available." Then the recording starts.
276	
277	## How long the call takes
278	
279	| Stage | How long |
280	| --- | --- |
281	| Starting | Up to 20 seconds, then "The recording did not start within 20 s." |
282	| Recording | `seconds`, plus about a second to start and finish. |
283	| Finishing | Up to about 75 s more if the files are slow to close, and 60 s more for each further stretch of a paused recording. |
284	| Finishing, with a camera beside the screen | Up to about 105 s more, and 90 s more for each further stretch, because each camera file is read too. |
285	| Landing | Up to 20 seconds, while a drag in the target project ends. |
286	| [Steps after landing](#what-they-wait-for) | Up to 5 minutes for each wait. |
287	
288	A finish that times out lists every movie it still holds, then the camera files, because they may yet finish on their own. If a drag outlasts its wait, the message names the files too, which are on disk either way:
289	
290	"The recording was saved at `<path>` but could not be added: …"
291	
292	Calls run one at a time, so a recording holds up the next call until it returns. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).
293	
294	## A person can pause or stop it
295	
296	While an agent records, the same [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) appears as for the panel, so a person at the Mac can pause, resume or stop it. **File ▸ Pause Recording** and **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) work too. An agent has no tool to pause or resume.
297	
298	- **Stop** ends the call early and the recording still lands, with `stopped_by: "stopped"` and a `duration` shorter than `seconds`. That's the same value the tool's own stop gives, so the short `duration` is what tells the two apart.
299	- **Pause** shortens what the call records, because `seconds` keeps running. The paused time is in no file, and `pauses` counts the presses, including a pause with no resume before the stop.
300	
301	A paused recording is a sequence of files, one for each stretch between a start or a resume and a pause or the stop. Each is named by its own start time and, with a microphone, carries its own microphone file. Every stretch lands as its own clip on one track, touching the one before, and each microphone file as its own clip on the **Microphone** track at its own offset.
302	
303	## What it answers
304	
305	Times are ticks, 600,000 to the second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). Most top-level keys describe the first stretch, the recording's own file.
306	
307	| Key | What it holds |
308	| --- | --- |
309	| `path` | The first stretch's file, the one a new project is addressed by. |
310	| `duration` | The total recorded across every stretch. |
311	| `width`, `height`, `fps` | The first stretch's picture size and frame rate, with `fps` as `[num, den]`. |
312	| `has_audio`, `audio_tracks` | What that movie holds. `audio_tracks` is 1 with system audio, else 0. The microphone is never a track of the movie. |
313	| `mic_offset` | Always present, and 0 with no microphone. The measured lead in ticks, positive when the picture began after the microphone. |
314	| `mic_path`, `mic_duration` | The first stretch's microphone file, when it landed. |
315	| `mic_problem` | Every stretch's microphone sentence, joined. It can stand beside a `mic_path` when a later stretch failed. |
316	| `media`, `clip`, `mic_media`, `mic_clip` | The first stretch's ids. There's no `clip` or `mic_clip` with `place: false`. |
317	| `camera` | The camera used, as in [Choose the camera and its format](#choose-the-camera-and-its-format). |
318	| `pauses` | How many times Pause was pressed, 0 when never. |
319	| `segments` | Always present, one entry for each file, in order. Exactly one for a recording never paused. |
320	| `stopped_by` | `stopped` for the tool's own stop and a person's Stop from Frame Job. `user_stopped` for macOS's own screen-recording indicator. `system_stopped` for a display that slept or a camera that stopped on its own. |
321	| `landed` | `document` or `new_project`. |
322	| `unreadable` | Any stretches left out. See below. |
323	| `note` | Present when there's something to say. |
324	| `project` | The usual project summary. |
325	| `new_media`, `new_clips`, `new_tracks` | The ids made, as every edit reports them, when it landed in an open project. `new_tracks` appears when a track was added. `scope` and `document_ops` appear when it landed inside a nest. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/). |
326	
327	Each entry of `segments` carries these keys. A screen recording's frame rate differs between stretches, so each has its own.
328	
329	| Key | What it holds |
330	| --- | --- |
331	| `path`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps` | This stretch's file. |
332	| `started_at` | When this stretch began, in UTC to the millisecond, like `2026-09-12T13:04:22.417Z`. |
333	| `mic_offset`, `mic_path`, `mic_duration`, `mic_problem` | As at the top level, for this stretch. |
334	| `media`, `clip`, `mic_media`, `mic_clip` | This stretch's ids, when known. |
335	| `camera_path`, `camera_duration`, `camera_offset` | This stretch's camera file, when it landed. `camera_offset` is in ticks, positive when the camera began after the screen. |
336	| `camera_problem`, `camera_note` | What went wrong with this stretch's camera, when anything did. The note repeats them. |
337	| `camera_media`, `camera_clip` | The camera's ids, when known. |
338	| `cursor_path`, `cursor_image` | This stretch's cursor file, when one was written. `cursor_image` reads `none` because no cursor image is recorded. |
339	| `cursor_problem` | Why the file wasn't written, or holds only the geometry the screen had when the stretch began. |
340	
341	### When a stretch won't read
342	
343	A stretch whose movie won't read, such as an empty file from a pause straight after a resume, is left out rather than failing the recording. The readable stretches land, and `unreadable` lists each one left out, with its `path`, its `kept_files` still on disk and the `reason`. When its microphone file reads, the entry adds `mic_path` and `mic_duration`, and `mic_media` and `mic_clip` when known, and that microphone lands in the slot the picture would have had. A camera file from such a stretch stays on disk, named in `kept_files`, and doesn't land.
344	
345	Only a recording with no readable movie at all fails, and it names every file.
346	
347	## Undo a recording
348	
349	In an open project, one undo removes every stretch's media and clips and leaves the files on disk, as undoing Add Media… does.
350	
351	A recording that opened as a new project has no undo step for its first picture, because the project is made from it. Whatever came with it is one undo step, and undoing it leaves that first picture alone in the project:
352	
353	| What came with it | Undo step |
354	| --- | --- |
355	| A microphone, on a recording never paused | **Add Microphone** |
356	| A camera, on a recording never paused | **Add Camera** |
357	| A camera and a microphone, on a recording never paused | **Add Camera and Microphone** |
358	| Only click ripples, on a recording never paused | **Cursor Clicks** |
359	| Later stretches of a paused recording, with all their files | **Add Recording Segments** |
360	
361	[Steps after landing](#run-steps-after-it-lands) undo first, one at a time, last first.

376	
377	Frame Job gives an agent 125 tools. This page names every one and links to its full reference, and says how a client can read what each one takes.
378	
379	## The tool catalog
380	
381	The 125 tools come in two kinds.
382	
383	- **69 edit tools.** Each makes one kind of edit to the project, as one undo step. These also take `scope`, which aims the edit inside a [nest](/mcp/nests/) by the nest's id.
384	- **56 app tools.** These work with files, read things, change what the app is showing, or run a whole command such as `record_screen` or `make_vertical_version`.
385	
386	Every tool takes `project`, which says which open project it acts on. Leave it out for the front project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).
387	
388	## How arguments are published
389	
390	Each tool publishes its arguments as JSON Schema, in the `inputSchema` of `tools/list`. That's where a client reads every argument's name, its kind, its closed list of values, its bounds and which arguments are required. The helper answers `tools/list` even when Frame Job isn't running. See [The helper and the socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/).
391	
392	Each tool's description says what it's for and what it returns. An argument that isn't in the schema stops the call before the tool runs, with a message listing what the tool does take: "trim_start does not take at. It takes alone, clip, to, project and scope."
393	
394	A few arguments read differently from what their kind suggests:
395	
396	| Argument | What's different |
397	| --- | --- |
398	| Every boolean | May also be sent as the string `"true"`, `"1"`, `"false"` or `"0"`. |
399	| `text` on `add_text_clip`, `shape` on `add_shape_clip` | May be a plain string: the words, or the kind of shape. |
400	| `kind` on `set_transition`, `region` on `add_zoom_action` | Must be sent even when null, because null means something: no transition, or zoom back out. |
401	| `rate` on `set_speed` and `add_speed_ramp` | Published as ×0.1 to ×1000. A rate outside that is brought into range, with no error. Zero or less stops the call. |
402	| `fps` on `set_canvas` | Each of its two numbers must be at least 1. |
403	| `clips` on every tool but `set_selection`, `groups` on `paste_attributes`, `ranges` on `ripple_delete_ranges` and `copy_pieces` | Can't be empty: the call stops and names the argument. On `set_selection`, an empty `clips` selects nothing. |
404	| `at` on `split`, `paste`, `freeze_frame` and `add_marker` | Optional. It takes the playhead when left out. |
405	| `focus` on `switch_layout` | May be null or left out, and the tool then fills it from the camera's cached person masks. |
406	
407	Four tools need at least one of their optional arguments, because a call that names nothing to change stops with an error: `set_track`, `set_marker`, `set_canvas` and `set_transition_style`.
408	
409	Frame Job fills a few values itself, from what only it can read, so the tools don't publish them and sending one stops the call: a graphic's `schema`, a relinked file's details, and the faces and turns `reframe_clip` follows.

6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	`set_video` is the one tool behind everything a clip's picture does: where it sits, how it's cropped, its effects, its motion and its grade. It takes a list of clips and a patch, an object holding only the properties you want to change. This page lists every key a patch can hold.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  tools="set_video"
12	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Picture sub-tab', 'Clip tab ▸ Color sub-tab', 'Dragging on the canvas']}
13	/>
14	
15	## `set_video`
16	
17	Merges a patch into each clip's own video properties, as one undo step however many clips it names. It mirrors the Clip tab's [Picture sub-tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) and [Color sub-tab](/color/color-tab/).
18	
19	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
20	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
21	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change, at least one. `get_project` lists their ids. |
22	| `patch` | object | Yes | The properties to change. The rest of this page lists its keys. |
23	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
24	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
25	
26	```json
27	{ "clips": [12, 14], "patch": { "opacity": 0.8, "shadow": { "blur": 20 } } }
28	```
29	
30	**How a patch merges.** A key you leave out keeps its value, inside a nested object too, so `{shadow: {blur: 20}}` keeps the shadow's colour, angle and distance. On a clip that has no shadow yet, the keys you left out take the defaults listed below. `shadow`, `chroma`, `reflection`, `spotlight`, `motion`, `look`, `cursor`, `cutout` and `hide_silent` set to `null` clear that property. `filters` and `obscure` are lists, so each replaces whole: send the full list, or `[]` to clear it. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).
31	
32	**Colours.** A colour is four numbers, `[r, g, b, a]`, each 0 to 1. Three numbers are refused, and so is a value outside the range. Two keys differ: the chroma key's colour is three numbers with no alpha, and the cursor's `click_color` is a CSS colour.
33	
34	**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. If the patch changes nothing, the call says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
35	
36	**When it refuses.**
37	
38	- A key or value the patch doesn't know is an error naming its dotted path, array indices included, and the value you sent, such as `filters[1].kind`. Nothing is dropped, corrected or clamped.
39	- A number outside its range is an error naming the key, the range and the number.
40	- A clip with no video properties is an error: "clip 7 has no video properties".
41	- The sections below list what a particular kind of clip can't take.
42	
43	### Which key does what
44	
45	| Keys | Section |
46	| --- | --- |
47	| `x`, `y`, `scale`, `rotation`, `opacity`, `blend` | [Transform](#transform-position-scale-rotation-opacity-and-blend) |
48	| `crop`, `corner_radius` | [Crop and corners](#crop-and-corners) |
49	| `shadow`, `chroma`, `filters`, `reflection`, `spotlight`, `obscure` | [Effects](#effects-shadow-chroma-key-filters-reflection-spotlight-and-obscure) |
50	| `cutout` | [Remove Background](#cutout) |
51	| `behind_subject` | [Text Behind Subject](#behind_subject) |
52	| `cursor` | [The recorded cursor](#cursor) |
53	| `motion` | [Motion presets](#motion) |
54	| `motion_blur` | [Motion blur](#motion_blur) |
55	| `hide_silent` | [Hide While Silent](#hide_silent) |
56	| `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, `qualifier` | [Light and colour](#color), [wheels](#wheels), [curves](#curves), [looks and LUTs](#look), [the qualifier](#qualifier) |
57	
58	### On an adjustment clip
59	
60	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) has no picture of its own. Only `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, the sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters, and `opacity` (the grade's strength) do anything there, and `qualifier` narrows which pixels they reach. The blur, sharpen and pixelate filters and any blend mode but `normal` are errors, such as "clip 7 is an adjustment clip and cannot take the blur filter".
61	
62	### Animate a property
63	
64	`set_video` changes the clip's base value, which holds for the clip's whole length. To change a value over time, use `add_action` then `set_action_end`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action_end). `motion` and `hide_silent` can't be animated.
65	
66	## Transform: position, scale, rotation, opacity and blend
67	
68	The clip's picture is centred on the canvas centre plus `x` and `y`, scaled, then rotated about that same centre. The [Transform section](/canvas/transform/) and dragging on the canvas change the same values.
69	
70	| Key | What it does | Range |
71	| --- | --- | --- |
72	| `x`, `y` | The clip's centre, in canvas pixels from the canvas centre. `y` runs down. | Any number |
73	| `scale` | The size. 1 is native pixels. | 0.01 to 10 |
74	| `rotation` | Degrees about the clip's centre. Positive turns clockwise on screen. | Any number |
75	| `opacity` | How solid the clip is. | 0 to 1 |
76	| `blend` | How the clip combines with what's already on the canvas. | `normal`, `multiply`, `screen`, `add`, `overlay`, `darken`, `lighten`, `difference` |
77	
78	`normal` is the default. A blend mode needs something under it. Over an empty black canvas, `multiply`, `darken` and `overlay` read black, while `screen`, `add`, `lighten` and `difference` change nothing, so `add_background` is usually the call to make first.
79	
80	A blend is forced to `normal` for the length of any transition, and on a clip on a matte track, so the frame there can differ from the value `get_project` reports. A nest clip can't take a blend mode other than `normal`. See [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/).
81	
82	## Crop and corners
83	
84	| Key | What it does | Range |
85	| --- | --- | --- |
86	| `crop` | `{l, t, r, b}`, the pixels to remove from each edge of the source. Cropping never shifts what's left. | Each 0 or more |
87	| `corner_radius` | Rounds the corners of the cropped picture, in source pixels, before it's rotated. | 0 or more |
88	
89	The opposite edges have to leave something behind: `l` plus `r` must be less than the source's width, and `t` plus `b` less than its height. See [Crop](/canvas/crop/) and [Corner radius](/canvas/corner-radius/).
90	
91	## Effects: shadow, chroma key, filters, reflection, spotlight and obscure
92	
93	Each of these is off until you set it. `shadow`, `chroma`, `reflection` and `spotlight` are objects that merge, and `null` clears one. `filters` and `obscure` are lists that replace whole.
94	
95	### Shadow
96	
97	`shadow` is `null` or an object. See [Shadow](/effects/shadow/).
98	
99	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
100	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
101	| `color` | The shadow's colour. | Four numbers | Black |
102	| `opacity` | How strong it is. | 0 to 1 | 0.5 |
103	| `blur` | How soft it is, in source pixels. | 0 or more | 12 |
104	| `angle` | The direction, in degrees. 0 is to the right, turning anticlockwise. | Any number | 315 |
105	| `distance` | How far it falls, in source pixels. | 0 or more | 8 |
106	
107	### Chroma key
108	
109	`chroma` is `null` or an object. See [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/).
110	
111	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
112	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
113	| `key` | The colour to remove, as three numbers with no alpha. | Each 0 to 1 | Green, `[0, 1, 0]` |
114	| `tolerance` | How far from the key a colour can be and still go. | 0 to 1 | 0.2 |
115	| `softness` | How gradually the edge falls off. | 0 to 1 | 0.1 |
116	| `spill` | How much of the key's colour to take off what's left. | 0 to 1 | 0.5 |
117	
118	### Filters
119	
120	`filters` is a list of up to four `{kind, amount}` objects. `kind` is `blur`, `sharpen`, `pixelate`, `sepia`, `noir`, `vignette` or `invert`. `amount` is 0 to 1, where 0 does nothing. Each entry must name both keys: leaving one out is an error. A fifth filter is an error, never dropped. Sepia, noir, vignette and invert run in list order. Blur, sharpen and pixelate always run before them, wherever they sit in the list. See [Filters](/effects/filters/).
121	
122	```json
123	{ "filters": [{ "kind": "noir", "amount": 1 }, { "kind": "vignette", "amount": 0.4 }] }
124	```
125	
126	### Reflection
127	
128	`reflection` is `null` or an object. See [Reflection](/effects/reflection/).
129	
130	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
131	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
132	| `opacity` | How strong the reflection is where it touches the clip. | 0 to 1 | 0.35 |
133	| `height` | How much of the clip is mirrored, as a fraction of its cropped height. | 0 to 1 | 0.5 |
134	| `gap` | The space between the clip and the reflection, in source pixels. | 0 or more | 0 |
135	| `falloff` | How far it fades across `height`. 0 doesn't fade, 0.5 ends at half `opacity`, and 1 reaches transparent exactly at `height`. | 0 to 1 | 1 |
136	
137	### Spotlight
138	
139	`spotlight` is `null` or an object. It dims the clip outside a shape and can magnify what's inside it. See [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/).
140	
141	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
142	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
143	| `shape` | The shape. | `rect`, `ellipse` | `rect` |
144	| `x`, `y` | The shape's centre, in source pixels from the centre of the cropped picture, `y` down. It can sit outside the picture. | Any number | 0 |
145	| `width`, `height` | The shape's size, in source pixels. | Above 0 | 480, 270 |
146	| `feather` | How many source pixels the edge blurs over. | 0 or more | 40 |
147	| `dim` | How much darker it is outside. 0 changes nothing, and 1 is black. | 0 to 1 | 0.6 |
148	| `zoom` | How much to magnify what's inside. 1 is no zoom. | 1 to 2 | 1 |
149	
150	Because the box is in source pixels, it stays on the picture when the clip is moved, scaled or rotated.
151	
152	### Obscure
153	
154	`obscure` is a list of up to four regions, each hiding what's under it. It uses the spotlight's frame for its centre and box. See [Obscure](/effects/obscure/).
155	
156	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
157	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
158	| `shape` | The shape. | `rect`, `ellipse` | `rect` |
159	| `x`, `y` | The region's centre, in source pixels from the centre of the cropped picture. | Any number | 0 |
160	| `width`, `height` | The region's size, in source pixels. | Above 0 | 480, 270 |
161	| `feather` | How many source pixels the effect ramps in over. | 0 or more | 20 |
162	| `kind` | How it hides. | `blur`, `pixelate` | `pixelate` |
163	| `amount` | How strongly it hides. | 0 to 1 | 1 |
164	
165	## `cutout`
166	
167	Remove Background: draws the clip as its subject alone, from masks made on your Mac. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Remove Background** and the Picture sub-tab's **Background** section. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).
168	
169	`cutout` is `null` or an object. `{cutout: {}}` turns it on with all five defaults, an object merges, and `null` removes it.
170	
171	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
172	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
173	| `subject` | What to keep. `foreground` keeps every foreground subject in the picture, and only an image clip can take it. | `person`, `foreground` | `person` |
174	| `quality` | The mask quality. Only `standard` works, and `best` is refused. | `standard` | `standard` |
175	| `background` | `remove` draws only the subject. `keep` draws the clip whole, which [Text Behind Subject](#behind_subject) uses. | `remove`, `keep` | `remove` |
176	| `edge` | Shrinks or grows the outline. | −1 to 1 | 0 |
177	| `feather` | Softens the outline. | 0 to 1 | 0 |
178	
179	A media, still or image clip can take a cutout. A text, shape, graphic, adjustment or nest clip is refused, and so is `foreground` on a media or still clip.
180	
181	**When the masks are made.** They're made as soon as the cutout is set, and `analyze_cutout` says where they stand. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/#analyze_cutout). The cutout draws in the preview, `render_frame` and every export:
182	
183	- The preview draws a frame whole while its mask isn't made yet.
184	- `render_frame` waits up to 30 s for its masks, then draws the clip uncut and says so.
185	- An export waits for every mask it draws.
186	- A clip with no person in any frame it plays draws uncut. Once a person is found anywhere in it, a frame with no person keeps little or nothing, so what's behind shows through.
187	
188	**In an action.** `edge` and `feather` animate, and `background` switches when the action ends. `subject` and `quality` are refused there, and an action can't switch the cutout off. On a clip with no cutout, an action's cutout keys do nothing.
189	
190	## `behind_subject`
191	
192	Text Behind Subject: `true` makes the person in a cutout clip stand in front of this clip, by cutting this clip away wherever that person is at each moment. It looks at every cutout clip on a track behind it, on the same timeline or in the same nest, and inside any nest on such a track. A cutout clip in front of it doesn't cut it. Any clip with a `cutout` counts, with `background` set to `remove` or `keep`. The default is `false`. It mirrors the Picture sub-tab's **Behind Subject** section. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/).
193	
194	Any clip that draws a picture can take it, except an adjustment clip or a nest clip, which are refused. In an action it switches when the action ends. [`text_behind_subject`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#text_behind_subject) places a title this way in one step.
195	
196	## `cursor`
197	
198	Styles the pointer Frame Job recorded beside a screen recording, in the movie's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), as it's drawn on this clip. It mirrors the Picture sub-tab's **Cursor** section. See [Style the recorded cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/).
199	
200	`cursor` is `null` or an object. `{cursor: {}}` stores all eight defaults, and an object merges. A value out of range is refused, never clamped.
201	
202	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
203	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
204	| `show` | Whether the cursor is drawn. | `true`, `false` | `true` |
205	| `scale` | Its size. | 0.25 to 8 | 1 |
206	| `style` | `recorded` draws the recorded image, and `arrow` draws Frame Job's own arrow. `recorded` also draws the arrow at a moment the file holds no cursor image. | `recorded`, `arrow` | `recorded` |
207	| `smoothing` | How much the path is smoothed. | 0 to 1 | 0 |
208	| `hide_idle` | Seconds of no activity before it hides. `null` never hides it. | `null`, 0.5 to 30 | `null` |
209	| `clicks` | What a click draws. | `none`, `ripple` | `none` |
210	| `click_color` | The ripple's colour, as a CSS colour. | Any CSS colour | `#ffffffcc` |
211	| `click_size` | The ripple's size. | 0.25 to 4 | 1 |
212	
213	**In an action.** `scale` and `click_size` animate. `show`, `style`, `clicks` and `click_color` switch when the action ends. `smoothing` and `hide_idle` have no effect in an action, so write them here. On a clip with no cursor, every cursor key in an action switches at the end, so give the clip one first with `{cursor: {}}` if you want them to animate.
214	
215	## `motion`
216	
217	What the clip does on its way in, on its way out and all the way through. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Motion ▸**. See [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).
218	
219	`motion` is `null` or `{in, out, during}`. The three slots merge: a slot you leave out keeps what's stored, a slot set to `null` clears that slot, and `{motion: null}` clears all three.
220	
221	| Slot | Keys | Values |
222	| --- | --- | --- |
223	| `in`, `out` | `kind`, `duration` | `kind` is `fade`, `zoom_in`, `zoom_out`, `slide_left`, `slide_right`, `slide_up`, `slide_down`, `spin` or `pop`. `duration` is in ticks, measured from the clip's first or last frame. |
224	| `during` | `kind`, `amount`, `period` | `kind` is `pulse`, `shake`, `spin`, `bounce` or `drift`. `amount` is 0 to 1. `period` is in ticks, and `drift` ignores it. |
225	
226	```json
227	{ "motion": { "in": { "kind": "fade", "duration": 300000 }, "during": null } }
228	```
229	
230	A slot you name without its keys starts from a half-second `fade`, or for `during` a `pulse` of amount 0.5 and period 1 s.
231	
232	The durations snap to the frame grid, and the period snaps with a floor of one frame, so `get_project` can answer with a number near the one you sent. `in` plus `out` longer than the clip scales both down to meet, rather than being refused. A negative duration, or a period under one tick, is an error.
233	
234	`motion` can't be animated: `set_action_end` refuses it. `get_project` reports the clip as if it weren't moving, because the preset only becomes placement when a frame is drawn.
235	
236	## `motion_blur`
237	
238	Blurs the clip, and its moving cursor, along their motion. It mirrors the **Motion Blur** row in the Picture sub-tab's **Transform** section. See [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/).
239	
240	`motion_blur` is 0 to 1, the shutter as a fraction of one canvas frame. 0 is off and the default, and 0.5 is a 180° shutter. It animates in an action, and draws in the preview, `render_frame` and every export.
241	
242	Anything above 0 is refused on a nest clip, so set it on the clips inside, and on an adjustment clip. The clip draws sharp during a transition, including inside a nest clip that's in one, on a matte track or cut by a matte, when Behind Subject cuts it, and with a drop shadow. The value stays stored. See [Where it stays sharp](/motion/motion-blur/#where-it-stays-sharp).
243	
244	## `hide_silent`
245	
246	Fades a clip, usually a camera, out while a media's speech is silent, and back in ahead of the next words. It mirrors the Picture sub-tab's **Hide While Silent** section. See [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/).
247	
248	`hide_silent` is `null` or an object.
249	
250	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
251	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
252	| `media` | Required. The id of the media, with sound, whose speech the clip follows. | A media id | |
253	| `pre_roll` | How long before speech the clip is fully in, in ticks. | 0 to 3,000,000 (5 s) | 120,000 (0.2 s) |
254	| `hold` | How long after speech it stays, in ticks. | 0 to 3,000,000 (5 s) | 900,000 (1.5 s) |
255	| `fade` | How long the fade takes, in ticks. | 0 to 3,000,000 (5 s) | 180,000 (0.3 s) |
256	
257	```json
258	{ "hide_silent": { "media": 3, "hold": 600000 } }
259	```
260	
261	The fade follows the clips of that media on the clip's own timeline or nest, then in each nest around it, working outwards until it finds one playing. Where none plays, the clip stays visible. These three times don't snap to the frame grid.
262	
263	If the media has no saved speech, this call saves it from the on-device voice detection first, in the same undo step. It's refused when the media has no sound, when its speech hasn't been detected yet ("Try again in a moment."), and on a nest clip, so set it on the clips inside.
264	
265	Only the drawn frame sees the fade: `get_project` reads the clip's opacity without it. `hide_silent` can't be animated.
266	
267	## `color`
268	
269	The thirteen values of the Color sub-tab's **Light** and **Color** sections, in one object. Each is 0 for unchanged, and any subset merges. See [Light](/color/light/) and [Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue](/color/color-section/).
270	
271	| Key | What it does | Range |
272	| --- | --- | --- |
273	| `exposure` | Exposure, in stops. | −3 to 3 |
274	| `temperature` | Positive is warmer. | −1 to 1 |
275	| `tint` | Positive is more magenta. | −1 to 1 |
276	| `highlights` | The upper half of the brightness range. | −1 to 1 |
277	| `shadows` | The lower half of the brightness range. | −1 to 1 |
278	| `whites` | Stretches the picture, held at black. | −1 to 1 |
279	| `blacks` | Stretches the picture, held at white. | −1 to 1 |
280	| `vibrance` | Saturation on the colours that have little. | −1 to 1 |
281	| `fade` | Lifts black towards 10 % and lowers white towards 95 %. | 0 to 1 |
282	| `brightness` | Brightness. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −1 to 1. |
283	| `contrast` | Contrast. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −1 to 1. |
284	| `saturation` | Saturation. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −1 to 1. |
285	| `hue` | Turns every colour's hue this many degrees, red towards yellow towards green, keeping its brightness. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −180 to 180. |
286	
287	A value outside a stated range is refused.
288	
289	The grade runs in this order: `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, then the sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters.
290	
291	## `wheels`
292	
293	Lift, gamma and gain: three colour pushes, each with its own brightness. An agent can set a push as exact numbers, which the [Wheels section](/color/wheels/) has no field for.
294	
295	`wheels` is `{lift, gamma, gain}`, each `{x, y, master}`, each −1 to 1, with 0 unchanged. Any subset merges, so `{wheels: {lift: {x: 0.2, y: -0.1}}}` keeps lift's `master` and the other two wheels.
296	
297	| Key | What it does |
298	| --- | --- |
299	| `x`, `y` | The colour push. Its angle is the hue (0° red, 120° green, 240° blue), and its length is the strength. It must lie inside the unit circle, so `x²` plus `y²` is at most 1. |
300	| `master` | The brightness. |
301	
302	`lift` moves black and holds white, `gain` moves white and holds black, and `gamma` moves the middle and holds both ends. A value outside these limits is refused, never clamped.
303	
304	## `curves`
305	
306	Writes the curves of the Color sub-tab's **Curves** section, one list of points per channel. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/) and [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/).
307	
308	`curves` is an object with up to six channels. A list replaces that channel whole, and `null` removes it. Each list is 2 to 16 `[x, y]` points with `x` strictly rising.
309	
310	| Channel | `x` | `y` | No change |
311	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
312	| `master`, `red`, `green`, `blue` | 0 to 1 | 0 to 1 | `y` equals `x` from 0 to 1 |
313	| `hue_hue` | Hue in degrees, 0 up to but not including 360 | A shift in degrees, −180 to 180 | Every `y` is 0 |
314	| `hue_sat` | Hue in degrees, 0 up to but not including 360 | A saturation gain, 0 to 2 | Every `y` is 1 |
315	
316	```json
317	{ "curves": { "master": [[0, 0.05], [0.5, 0.55], [1, 1]], "hue_sat": null } }
318	```
319	
320	A curve that changes nothing is stored as no curve. A point outside these limits is refused, never clamped.
321	
322	The tone channels are smooth monotone curves through their points, flat outside the first and last `x`, and a colour goes through `master` first, then its own channel. The two hue curves are smooth curves that wrap at 0 and 360. They run after the tone channels, and both look up the colour's original hue, so `hue_sat` doesn't see the shift `hue_hue` made. A positive shift turns red towards yellow towards green, keeping brightness, and the gain scales saturation. Greys are left alone: a colour whose strongest and weakest channels are within 0.02 of each other doesn't change, and the effect reaches full strength at 0.06.
323	
324	In an action, a curve that changes nothing animates to neutral, and two curves with different point counts blend their values across the action.
325	
326	## `look`
327	
328	Applies one of the eight built-in looks, or an imported `.cube` LUT, at an amount. It mirrors the Color sub-tab's **Look** section and **Clip ▸ Look ▸**. See [Looks](/color/looks/) and [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).
329	
330	`look` is `null` or an object. `{look: null}` removes it.
331	
332	| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
333	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
334	| `kind` | Which look. | `warm`, `cool`, `teal_orange`, `vivid`, `faded`, `vintage`, `dramatic`, `black_white`, `lut` | |
335	| `media` | The media id of the `.cube` file. Required with `lut`, and refused with any other kind. | A LUT's media id | |
336	| `amount` | How much of it. | 0 to 1 | 1 |
337	
338	```json
339	{ "look": { "kind": "teal_orange", "amount": 0.6 } }
340	```
341	
342	For a LUT, bring the file in with `import_media`, then send `{look: {kind: "lut", media: 9}}` with the id it answers.
343	
344	A new kind keeps the clip's amount, and a built-in kind replaces a LUT. An amount alone needs a clip that already has a look. In an action the amount ramps while the kind and the LUT stay the same. A change of kind or of LUT switches when the action ends, amount included.
345	
346	## `qualifier`
347	
348	Narrows which pixels an adjustment clip's grade reaches, by hue, saturation and luma. It mirrors the Color sub-tab's **Qualifier** section. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).
349	
350	The qualifier is for adjustment clips only. On any other clip it's an error naming the clip. It reads the picture behind the clip, before the grade.
351	
352	`qualifier` is `{hue, saturation, luma, invert, blur}`.
353	
354	| Key | Keys inside it | What it does |
355	| --- | --- | --- |
356	| `hue` | `center`, `width`, `softness` | In degrees. `center` is 0 to 360 and wraps. `width` is 0 to 360, fully selected about the centre. `softness` is 0 to 180, the fall-off outside each edge. A colour's selection fades out as its chroma falls from 0.06 to 0.02, and at 0.02 or under it's never selected. |
357	| `saturation` | `low`, `high`, `softness` | Each 0 to 1, with `low` no more than `high`. Near-black reads as 0. |
358	| `luma` | `low`, `high`, `softness` | Each 0 to 1, with `low` no more than `high`. Rec. 709 luma, or BT.2020 luma in an HDR (HLG) project. |
359	| `invert` | | `true` selects everything else. |
360	| `blur` | | 0 to 1, 0 being off. Softens the selection by a Gaussian of 24 × `blur` canvas pixels. It never softens a matte cutting the clip, and does nothing while no range is on. |
361	
362	A range merges: `{hue: {}}` turns hue on at centre 30, width 50, softness 25, and saturation and luma turn on at low 0, high 1, softness 0.1. A partial range keeps the rest, and `null` turns a range off. The selection is the product of the ranges that are on. A value outside its bounds is refused, never clamped.
363	
364	In an action the numbers animate, the hue centre taking the short way round, so 350 to 10 passes 0. A range turned on, and `invert`, switch when the action ends. An action can't turn off a range the clip already has on: `null` there only takes the range out of the action's end.
365	
366	`render_frame` with `selection` set to the adjustment clip's id draws what the qualifier selects, as [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) does. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/#selection).
367

378	title: "Tools: clip sound (set_audio)"
379	description: "The Sound tab's settings through one agent tool: volume, fades, ducking, pan, EQ, dynamics, voice isolation and voice effects."
380	---
381	
382	`set_audio` is how an agent changes a clip's sound: its volume, fades, ducking, pan, EQ and every other setting in the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). You name the clips and send only what should change, and the rest of each clip's sound stays as it is.
383	
384	## `set_audio`
385	
386	Changes the base sound settings of one or more clips, as one undo step. Read them back with [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/), where they're under each clip's `audio`.
387	
388	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
389	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
390	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids. At least one. |
391	| `patch` | object | Yes | The settings to merge. Each key is described below. |
392	| `scope` | integer | No | Look the clips up inside this nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
393	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
394	
395	```json
396	{
397	  "clips": [12, 15],
398	  "patch": {
399	    "volume": 0.8,
400	    "eq": { "high_pass": { "frequency": 100 } },
401	    "gate": {}
402	  }
403	}
404	```
405	
406	The patch follows the rules of [Patches](/mcp/patches/):
407	
408	- A key you leave out keeps what's stored.
409	- `duck`, `compressor`, `limiter`, `eq` and each of its slots, `hum`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser` and `voice` are objects, and they merge key by key.
410	- `null` on one of those clears it, so `{"duck": null}` turns ducking off.
411	- An empty object turns `duck`, `compressor`, `limiter`, `hum`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser` or an EQ slot on at its defaults, so `{"limiter": {}}` adds the limiter.
412	
413	**Answers** with the [project summary](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/). A patch that changes nothing answers "made no change".
414	
415	**Refuses** a key it doesn't know, naming its path, and a value out of range, naming the key and the value you sent. Nothing is clamped. A clip with no sound settings, such as a text clip, is refused by id.
416	
417	All times in the patch are ticks, 600,000 to the second.
418	
419	### Volume and mute
420	
421	| Key | Type | What it does |
422	| --- | --- | --- |
423	| `volume` | number | The clip's gain, from 0 to 32. 1 is unity. |
424	| `muted` | boolean | Mutes the clip. |
425	
426	See [Clip volume](/audio/volume/).
427	
428	### Fades and fade shapes
429	
430	| Key | Type | What it does |
431	| --- | --- | --- |
432	| `fade_in`, `fade_out` | integer | The fade's length in ticks, 0 or more. |
433	| `fade_in_shape`, `fade_out_shape` | string | The fade's curve: `linear` (the default), `s_curve`, `plus_3db`, which moves fastest near silence, or `minus_3db`, which moves fastest near full level. |
434	
435	The shapes are the **Fades** section's **In shape** and **Out shape**. See [Audio fades](/audio/fades/).
436	
437	### Ducking
438	
439	`duck` lowers other sound while this clip plays, or only while its speech plays.
440	
441	| `duck` key | Range | Default | What it does |
442	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
443	| `level` | 0 to 1 | 0.2 | What the other sound is multiplied by. |
444	| `attack` | 0 or more ticks | 300,000 (0.5 s) | How long the sound takes to go down. |
445	| `release` | 0 or more ticks | 600,000 (1 s) | How long it takes to come back. |
446	| `mode` | `extent` or `speech` | `extent` | `extent` ducks for the clip's whole length. `speech` ducks only while its speech plays. |
447	| `pre_roll` | 0 or more ticks | 300,000 (0.5 s) | With `speech`, how far before each stretch of speech to start. |
448	| `hold` | 0 or more ticks | 300,000 (0.5 s) | With `speech`, how far after it to hold. |
449	
450	`mode: "speech"` is **Speech** in the **Ducking** section's **Duck by** pop-up. It saves the media's detected speech in the same undo step, so it needs on-device speech detection to have finished. It's an error for a clip that isn't a media clip with sound, and for one whose speech hasn't been detected yet, which says to try again in a moment. To write the speech spans yourself, use [`set_media_speech`](/mcp/tools-media/#set_media_speech).
451	
452	See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/) and [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/).
453	
454	### Mono, keep pitch, pan and channels
455	
456	| Key | Type | What it does |
457	| --- | --- | --- |
458	| `mono` | boolean | Plays the clip in mono. |
459	| `keep_pitch` | boolean | Keeps the sound's pitch at a new speed. A clip starts with this on. |
460	| `pan` | number | From −1 hard left to 1 hard right. |
461	| `channels` | string | `both` (the default), `left`, `right` or `swapped`. `left` and `right` play that channel of a stereo source from both sides, and `swapped` exchanges them. It comes after isolation and any voice effect, and a mono source ignores it. |
462	
463	See [Pan and Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/), [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/) and [Channels](/audio/channels/).
464	
465	### Compressor and limiter
466	
467	| `compressor` key | Range | Default |
468	| --- | --- | --- |
469	| `threshold_db` | −60 to 0 dB | −18 |
470	| `ratio` | 1 to 20 | 3 |
471	| `attack` | 0 or more ticks | 6,000 (10 ms) |
472	| `release` | 0 or more ticks | 120,000 (200 ms) |
473	| `makeup_db` | 0 to 24 dB | 0 |
474	
475	`limiter` is a true-peak limiter, last in the clip's chain. Its ceiling holds after the clip's base volume.
476	
477	| `limiter` key | Range | Default |
478	| --- | --- | --- |
479	| `ceiling_db` | −24 to 0 dBTP | −1 |
480	| `release` | 600 to 600,000 ticks | 60,000 (100 ms) |
481	
482	See [Compressor](/audio/compressor/) and [Limiter](/audio/limiter/). A track has its own pair, set with [`set_track`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#a-tracks-compressor-and-limiter).
483	
484	### Noise reduction and voice isolation
485	
486	| Key | Range | What it does |
487	| --- | --- | --- |
488	| `noise_reduction` | 0 to 1 | Reduces noise in the clip's sound. |
489	| `isolation` | 0 to 1 | Isolates a voice with Apple's on-device model, which also reduces room echo. 0 is off, 0.8 is the app's default and 1 leaves silence between words. |
490	
491	Isolation is rendered offline. The clip plays without it until the render finishes, and an export waits for it. A clip not at ×1 plays without it.
492	
493	See [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) and [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/).
494	
495	### EQ
496	
497	`eq` has seven slots, after the channel pick. Each slot is `null` for off, or an object.
498	
499	| Slot | Keys | Default |
500	| --- | --- | --- |
501	| `high_pass` | `frequency` 20 to 20,000 Hz, `slope` 12 or 24 dB/octave | 80 Hz, 12 |
502	| `low_shelf` | `frequency`, `gain_db` −24 to 24 dB | 100 Hz, 0 dB |
503	| `band_1`, `band_2`, `band_3` | `frequency`, `gain_db`, `q` 0.1 to 10 | 1,000 Hz, 0 dB, 1 |
504	| `high_shelf` | `frequency`, `gain_db` | 8,000 Hz, 0 dB |
505	| `low_pass` | `frequency`, `slope` | 12,000 Hz, 12 |
506	
507	`bypass: true` keeps the settings and silences them. `{"eq": {"high_pass": {}}}` turns one slot on at its defaults.
508	
509	The inspector's buttons are these moves:
510	
511	| Button | Patch |
512	| --- | --- |
513	| **Rumble Cut** | `high_pass` at 80 Hz, slope 24 |
514	| **De-mud** | `band_1` at 300 Hz, −3 dB, Q 1 |
515	| **Presence** | `band_3` at 4,000 Hz, +3 dB, Q 1 |
516	
517	See [EQ](/audio/eq/).
518	
519	### Hum removal
520	
521	`hum` notches out mains hum and its harmonics, after the EQ.
522	
523	| `hum` key | Range | Default |
524	| --- | --- | --- |
525	| `frequency` | 50 or 60 Hz | 60 |
526	| `depth_db` | 6 to 60 dB | 30 |
527	| `harmonics` | 1 to 8 | 4 |
528	
529	See [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/).
530	
531	### Gate
532	
533	`gate` turns the pauses down. It's a downward expander, after noise reduction. For each dB the sound falls below the threshold, the level drops by a further `ratio` − 1 dB, and never by more than `range_db` in all.
534	
535	| `gate` key | Range | Default |
536	| --- | --- | --- |
537	| `threshold_db` | −40 to 0 dB, relative to the clip's measured loudness | −10 |
538	| `ratio` | 1 to 20 | 4 |
539	| `range_db` | 1 to 80 dB | 20 |
540	| `attack` | 0 to 60,000 ticks | 600 (1 ms) |
541	| `hold` | 0 to 300,000 ticks | 30,000 (50 ms) |
542	| `release` | 600 to 1,200,000 ticks | 60,000 (100 ms) |
543	
544	The loudness it's relative to is what [`normalize_clip`](/mcp/tools-audio/#normalize_clip) reports, before the clip's volume. See [Gate](/audio/gate/).
545	
546	### Leveller
547	
548	`leveller` evens out a speaker who moves on and off the microphone, after the gate. It's a gain curve made ahead of time from the clip's measured loudness and its speech, so it sounds the same in the preview and an export.
549	
550	| `leveller` key | Range | Default |
551	| --- | --- | --- |
552	| `target_db` | −20 to 10 dB, relative to the clip's loudness | 0 |
553	| `max_up_db` | 0 to 24 dB | 12 |
554	| `max_down_db` | 0 to 24 dB | 12 |
555	| `response` | 300,000 to 6,000,000 ticks | 1,200,000 (2 s) |
556	
557	Each phrase's level is brought to `target_db`, never more than the two limits. A pause holds the gain and glides to the next phrase over its last 0.25 s, and a phrase under 1 s takes its neighbour's gain.
558	
559	It waits for the clip's speech as well as its loudness. It does nothing where speech detection isn't available or no phrase has 1 s of speech. See [Leveller](/audio/leveller/).
560	
561	### De-esser
562	
563	`de_esser` comes after the leveller. It turns the band above `frequency` down on sibilance and never boosts it.
564	
565	| `de_esser` key | Range | Default |
566	| --- | --- | --- |
567	| `frequency` | 2,000 to 12,000 Hz | 6,000 |
568	| `threshold_db` | −30 to 20 dB, relative to the clip's loudness | 0 |
569	| `range_db` | 1 to 24 dB | 6 |
570	
571	The gate, leveller and de-esser act only once the clip's loudness is measured. Until then the clip plays without them, and an export waits. A clip too short or too quiet to measure plays without them, and on a nest clip they do nothing. See [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/).
572	
573	### Voice effects
574	
575	`voice` replaces the clip's sound with a rendered effect, after isolation and before the channel pick.
576	
577	| `voice` key | Range | Default | What it does |
578	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
579	| `kind` | See below | None | Which effect. Needed when the clip has no voice effect yet. |
580	| `amount` | 0 to 1 | 1 | How much of the effect. 0 plays the clip dry. |
581	| `pitch` | −12 to 12 semitones | The kind's own: 0 for `pitch`, +5 for `high`, −5 for `deep` | Read only by `pitch`, `high` and `deep`. |
582	
583	| Group | Kinds |
584	| --- | --- |
585	| Voice | `pitch`, `high`, `deep`, `robot` |
586	| Tone | `bass`, `treble`, `bright`, `telephone`, `radio` |
587	| Character | `lofi`, `distorted` |
588	| Space | `echo`, `room`, `hall`, `plate`, `cathedral` |
589	
590	A new `kind` keeps a stored `pitch` unless you send `pitch: null` with it. `{"voice": null}` clears the effect.
591	
592	The clip plays without the effect until its render finishes, and an export waits for it. A clip not at ×1 plays without it, and reverb and echo tails end with the clip. See [Voice effects](/audio/voice-effects/).
593	
594	## Animate sound
595	
596	`set_audio` sets the clip's base values. To change one over time, use an action's `set_action_end`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/) and [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
597	
598	Volume, mute, the fades, `pan`, `mono`, `channels`, `eq`, `hum`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and `isolation` can all animate. `duck`, `keep_pitch`, the fade shapes and `voice` can't, and only `set_audio` sets them.
599
