content.content:
1	---
2	title: "Tools: framing and vertical"
3	description: The agent tools that frame one clip on the canvas, switch camera layouts and make a tall or square version of a project, with every argument, answer and refusal.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	These three tools fit pictures to a canvas: `reframe_clip` frames one clip, `switch_layout` arranges a camera and a screen, and `make_vertical_version` makes a 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1 version of the whole timeline.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…']}
12	  tools={['reframe_clip', 'switch_layout', 'make_vertical_version']}
13	  needs="Nothing to set up. Faces, people and salient regions are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
14	/>
15	
16	Times are in ticks, 600,000 a second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/) covers the `project` summary, the `new_clips` and `new_tracks` lists, and the message you get when a call changes nothing.
17	
18	## `reframe_clip`
19	
20	Frames one clip on the current canvas: following a subject, a recorded pointer or whoever is talking, or centring, fitting or rescaling it. **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…** is this tool with `replace: true` on each selected clip and a **Backgrounds** track as `backdrop`, and **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** calls it for each clip. [Reframe a clip](/framing/reframe-clip/) explains the framing itself.
21	
22	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
23	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
24	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to frame. |
25	| `follow` | string | Yes | What to do: `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `cursor`, `layout`, `speaker`, `center`, `fit` or `keep`. Each has a section below. |
26	| `zoom` | number | No | How tight the frame is, 1 to 4 times the scale that fills the canvas. Default 1. |
27	| `where_empty` | string | No | What shows where there's nothing to follow: `fit`, the whole picture, or `center`. Default `fit`. |
28	| `backdrop` | integer | No | A track behind the clip's for a blurred copy of it. Left out, no copy is made. |
29	| `replace` | boolean | No | `true` removes the clip's own moves before framing. Default `false`, which builds the framing into them. |
30	| `from_width` | integer | No | `keep` and `layout` only: the width of the canvas the clip was placed on. Default the current canvas's. |
31	| `from_height` | integer | No | `keep` and `layout` only: the height of that canvas. Default the current canvas's. |
32	| `mics` | array of integers | With `speaker` | `speaker` only: two to four clip ids, the microphones of the people in the shot. |
33	| `mic_faces` | array of integers | No | `speaker` only: each microphone's face number, in `mics`' order. Left out, Frame Job matches them. |
34	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside that nest. Inside a nest the nest's canvas is the canvas. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
35	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
36	
37	Which kind reads which argument is in [Which options each kind reads](/framing/reframe-clip/#which-options-each-kind-reads). An argument a kind doesn't read is ignored, but `zoom` outside 1 to 4, a `from_width` or `from_height` of 0 and an unknown `backdrop` track stop the call whatever the kind.
38	
39	To frame for a new canvas, call [`set_canvas`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_canvas) first and leave `rescale_clips` off, which is its default. `keep` and `layout` then take the old size in `from_width` and `from_height`.
40	
41	This call follows whatever Frame Job finds in clip 12, one and a half times tighter than the scale that fills the canvas:
42	
43	```json
44	{ "clip": 12, "follow": "subject", "zoom": 1.5 }
45	```
46	
47	It answers `ok: true`, `cached` and the `project` summary. `cached` is false when an analysis ran first. A blurred copy adds its id to `new_clips`, and `new_tracks` when it needed a new track.
48	
49	The framing is written as the clip's position and scale and one action per move, as one undo step, **Reframe Clip**. A framing that would leave the clip exactly as it is changes nothing and makes no undo step.
50	
51	### `follow: subject`, `face`, `person` and `salient`
52	
53	These follow [what Frame Job finds](/framing/what-is-found/) in the clip on your Mac. `subject` follows a face, else a person, else a salient region, the part of the picture the eye goes to first. `face`, `person` and `salient` follow only that kind.
54	
55	- The frame eases onto the subject and moves only when the subject leaves a dead zone, the area around its aim where small movements are ignored.
56	- It cuts hard at each shot change.
57	- It holds a lost subject for 1 s, then follows another, or eases over 0.8 s to what `where_empty` says.
58	- It returns once a subject has been seen for 0.6 s.
59	- It frames two people together when both fit.
60	
61	The tool analyses the clip first. See [The analysis wait](#the-analysis-wait). A clip whose media has a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) can't use these four, because a recording with a cursor file follows its cursor, never faces. See [How a followed frame moves](/framing/reframe-clip/#how-a-followed-frame-moves).
62	
63	### `follow: cursor`
64	
65	Follows a screen recording's recorded pointer, read from its media's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). It reads the file at once, with no analysis and no wait.
66	
67	- The frame sits on the pointer and moves only when the pointer leaves a dead zone reaching 20 % of the frame's width and 12 % of its height either side of where the frame is aimed.
68	- It arrives on each click outside that zone, in a move that ends on the click's frame.
69	- It holds still while the person types, though a click still arrives.
70	
71	The frame never shows the whole picture, so `where_empty` and `backdrop` do nothing here. A clip whose media has no cursor file can't use it. A cursor file that's missing or won't read stops the call, in a sentence naming it.
72	
73	### `follow: layout`
74	
75	Re-lays a camera clip's [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/), and its screen's, on the current canvas. You can name the camera or the screen, and both are re-laid.
76	
77	Each switch made on `from_width` × `from_height` is recognised and switched again here at the same time, length and curve. To be recognised, its position, crop and corner radius must match what Frame Job would have made to within 1 px, and its scale and opacity to within 0.001.
78	
79	- **Side by Side** becomes **Stacked** on a canvas taller than wide.
80	- The cut pieces of the recording take the new layout.
81	- Any zoom on them is adjusted so it still shows the same part of the picture.
82	
83	It reads no `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` or `replace`, and it runs no analysis. A switch edited by hand can't be recognised, and the call stops, naming the clip and the action.
84	
85	### `follow: speaker`
86	
87	Frames a wide shot of two to four people on whoever is talking. Each person needs a microphone of their own, named in `mics`: a clip of a sound file or a camera's detached sound, each on its own track, and not the clip being framed. **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** offers this as Follow **Speaker**. See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/).
88	
89	- Who talks when is read from the microphones as [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) reads it at its default settings.
90	- Each microphone is matched to the face whose mouth moves with it, analysed on your Mac. Faces are numbered 1, 2 and so on from left to right.
91	- Each change of speaker is a hard cut, held at least 2 s.
92	- Two people talking at once are framed together when they fit. Otherwise the frame stays on one of them, the one already framed if that person is talking.
93	- While nobody talks, the last speaker stays.
94	
95	When the match is weak, because a microphone and its face agree by less than 0.2 (1 is perfect agreement), the call stops and says where each face is, for example "face 1 at 28 % across the picture, face 2 at 71 %". Name each microphone's face in `mic_faces` and call again. Here microphone clip 31 is the right-hand of two faces and clip 32 the left-hand one:
96	
97	```json
98	{ "clip": 12, "follow": "speaker", "mics": [31, 32], "mic_faces": [2, 1] }
99	```
100	
101	A clip that changes shot can't be framed this way. Split it first with [`split_at_shots`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#split_at_shots). `speaker` reads its microphones in the timeline or nest open in the window, so a call addressed to a nest that isn't open stops and says to open it with [`set_scope`](/mcp/nests/).
102	
103	### `follow: center`
104	
105	Holds the frame on the middle of the picture for the whole clip, at `zoom`. It needs no analysis.
106	
107	### `follow: fit`
108	
109	Shows the whole picture for the whole clip, scaled to fit the canvas. It needs no analysis and doesn't read `zoom`. With `backdrop`, the blurred copy fills the canvas around it.
110	
111	### `follow: keep`
112	
113	Rescales the clip from the canvas it was made for, `from_width` × `from_height`, to the current one, as `set_canvas` does with `rescale_clips`. Every position and scale its actions set moves with it. With neither argument there's nothing to rescale.
114	
115	`keep` frames clips the other kinds won't, such as a title, a shape, a rotated clip or a clip on a matte track, as long as it has a picture. It reads no `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` or `replace`.
116	
117	### `zoom`, `where_empty`, `backdrop` and `replace`
118	
119	**`zoom`** sets how tight the frame is, from 1 to 4. At 1, the default, the picture covers the canvas with nothing to spare. `center`, the four following kinds, `cursor` and `speaker` read it, and `fit`, `keep` and `layout` don't.
120	
121	**`where_empty`** is what the four following kinds and `speaker` show where there's nothing to follow: `fit`, the whole picture, or `center`, the middle of the picture.
122	
123	**`backdrop`** names a track for one blurred copy of the clip, for its whole length, made only when the framing shows the whole picture somewhere. That means `fit`, or a followed clip that falls back to `fit`.
124	
125	- The copy goes on the named track when that track is unlocked, isn't a matte and is free over the clip. Otherwise it goes on a new track at the back.
126	- It's the copy **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** makes.
127	- It keeps the clip's speed actions, so a ramped clip's copy shows the same frames.
128	
129	**`replace`** decides what happens to the actions the clip already has. By default they stay, and the framing is built into the clip's position and scale and into every action end that moves or scales it, so a zoom or pan still happens inside the new framing.
130	
131	- The framing's own moves go in the gaps between the clip's actions. A move that would overlap one is shifted up to 0.5 s earlier, or else made part of that action, following its curve.
132	- A cut splits the action it lands in. A linear action plays as before and an eased one eases again on each side. A speed action, or one running past the clip's end, isn't split, and the cut becomes part of it instead.
133	- With `replace: true`, every `x`, `y` and `scale` is removed from the clip's action ends and the picture is fitted first. Volume and every other key stay, and an action left with nothing is removed.
134	
135	`keep` and `layout` don't read `replace`.
136	
137	### The analysis wait
138	
139	The four following kinds and `speaker` need the part of the file the clip plays analysed for shots, faces and subjects, with 1 s either side. The tool asks for what's missing and waits up to 60 s.
140	
141	Past that nothing changes. The answer is `ok: true` with `analyzing` and a `note`, so check for it rather than reading `ok` alone:
142	
143	| Key | What it holds |
144	| --- | --- |
145	| `analyzing.media` | The ids of the media still being analysed. |
146	| `analyzing.covered` | How much is done, from 0 to 1. |
147	| `note` | How far it got, and to call `reframe_clip` again. |
148	
149	The analysis carries on after the answer, so call again to apply the framing.
150	
151	- `center`, `fit`, `keep`, `layout` and `cursor` need no analysis.
152	- `speaker` also needs its microphones' loudness and speech, which Frame Job measures when a file is added. While that's still running the call stops and says to try again in a moment.
153	- If the analysis fails, the call stops, naming the analysis and the media.
154	- If the [Assistant](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) is stopped during the wait, nothing is framed.
155	- If the project or the open nest changes during the wait, nothing is framed. Call again.
156	
157	### Refusals
158	
159	A [refused call](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/#a-refusal) changes nothing and answers with one sentence saying why. Frame Job first checks the arguments, and stops on an unknown clip, a `zoom` outside 1 to 4, a `from_width` or `from_height` of 0, an unknown `backdrop` track or, with `speaker`, an unknown clip in `mics`. Then it checks these in order:
160	
161	1. Anything but `keep` on a text, shape, graphic or adjustment clip.
162	2. A clip with no picture, or a crop or scale that leaves none.
163	3. A nest clip, then a still or image clip, with a following kind, `cursor` or `speaker`.
164	4. `cursor` on a clip whose media has no cursor file, then a following kind or `speaker` on one whose media has a cursor file.
165	5. Unless `keep` or `layout`: a clip on a matte track or cut by a matte, then a turned clip (a rotation, an action turning it, or a spin in its motion).
166	6. For `speaker`, its microphones:
167	   - `mics` doesn't hold two to four clips, or names a clip twice.
168	   - A microphone is the clip being framed, or has no sound from a media file.
169	   - A microphone's sound is off.
170	   - Two microphones are on one track.
171	   - `mic_faces` doesn't have one number for each microphone, names face 0, or names a face twice.
172	7. For `layout`:
173	   - The clip holds no camera layout.
174	   - A clip is laid out both as a camera and as a screen.
175	   - A screen layout has no camera switch in front of it.
176	   - The first switch isn't a layout Frame Job made on `from_width` × `from_height`, which means it was edited by hand.
177	
178	These need the analysis, the cursor file or the microphones, so they come last, in this order:
179	
180	8. For `speaker`:
181	   - A microphone is still being measured, or never speaks over the clip.
182	   - The clip changes shot.
183	   - Fewer faces show than there are microphones. A face counts when it's in at least a quarter of the clip's samples.
184	   - `mic_faces` names a face past the ones found.
185	   - Nobody speaks inside the clip.
186	   - The faces don't show who is whose.
187	9. When a blurred copy would be made: a nest clip, or a `backdrop` track that isn't behind the clip's.
188	10. A following kind with no analysis for the part that plays, or `cursor` with no recorded point in it.
189	
190	## `switch_layout`
191	
192	Lays out a camera clip and the screen recording behind it at a time, as [**Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸**](/framing/camera-layouts/) and the Picture sub-tab's [Layout section](/framing/layout-section/) do at the playhead. Those pages describe each layout and how far it reaches.
193	
194	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
195	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
196	| `camera` | integer | Yes | The camera clip's id: a clip with a picture playing at `at`. |
197	| `layout` | string | Yes | `corner`, `side_by_side`, `stacked`, `camera_full` or `screen_only`. |
198	| `at` | integer | Yes | When the switch starts, in ticks. Inside a nest, this is the nest's own time. |
199	| `screen` | integer | No | The screen clip's id, on a track behind the camera's. Left out, it's the clip drawing behind the camera at `at`: the front-most one on a shown, non-matte track, passing over adjustment clips and clips with their picture off. With none there, the camera is laid out alone. |
200	| `shape` | string | No | `corner` only: `square`, `rounded` or `circle`. Default `square`. |
201	| `corner` | string | No | `corner` only: `bottom_right`, `bottom_left`, `top_right` or `top_left`. Default `bottom_right`. |
202	| `duration` | integer | No | How long the switch eases, in ticks. Default 0.5 s (300000). It's clamped to the clip and to its next layout action. |
203	| `curve` | string | No | How the switch eases: `linear`, `ease_in`, `ease_out` or `ease_in_out`. Default `ease_in_out`. |
204	| `through` | integer | No | Where the layout stops holding, in ticks, after `at`. |
205	| `focus` | array of 2 numbers, or null | No | `[x, y]`: the point of the camera's picture a crop is centred on, in the camera media's source pixels from the picture's centre, y down. It's clamped inside the picture. |
206	| `nest` | boolean | No | `true` nests the camera's clips, or the screen's, first when one of them zooms or moves after `at`, instead of stopping. Default `false`. |
207	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside that nest. Inside a nest the nest's canvas is the canvas. |
208	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
209	
210	| `layout` | The camera | The screen |
211	| --- | --- | --- |
212	| `corner` | In a corner box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third tall, 5 % in from the edges | At its full placement, where a newly added clip sits |
213	| `side_by_side` | Cropped to fill the right third | Fitted in the left two-thirds |
214	| `stacked` | Filling the rest below the screen | Across the top |
215	| `camera_full` | Fills the canvas | At its full placement |
216	| `screen_only` | Hidden where it is, at opacity 0 | At its full placement |
217	
218	The camera and the screen each get one layout action at `at`. At a clip's first frame the layout becomes its base, and a one-frame action marks the cut. A layout action already starting at `at` is replaced, and one still easing at `at` is shortened to end there.
219	
220	The layout holds. Every later clip on the camera's track, and on the screen's, that starts before the next switch on that track, `through` or the track's end takes it as its base and keeps its own actions.
221	
222	With `focus` left out or null, the tool fills it as the menu does, from the middle of the person in the camera clip, when [`analyze_cutout`](/mcp/tools-analysis/#analyze_cutout)'s person masks are cached for every frame it plays. Otherwise the crop is centred. A filled `focus` is dropped when `nest: true` nests the camera, but a `focus` you send goes as given.
223	
224	This call puts the camera in a round box at the top right, starting 2 s in:
225	
226	```json
227	{ "camera": 8, "layout": "corner", "at": 1200000, "shape": "circle", "corner": "top_right" }
228	```
229	
230	It answers `ok: true`, `focus` (the `[x, y]` the crop centres on, sent by you or filled from the masks, or null when there's none) and the `project` summary, with `new_clips` and `new_tracks` when `nest: true` made a nest. It's one undo step, **Camera Layout**.
231	
232	A negative `at`, a `duration` that isn't positive, a `through` not after `at`, or a `focus` that isn't two numbers stops the call before anything else. Then it's refused, with nothing changed and the clip named, when:
233	
234	- the camera has no picture, or doesn't play at `at`, and the same for a `screen` you name
235	- `screen` isn't on a track behind the camera's
236	- `side_by_side` or `stacked` has no screen
237	- the camera is a nest clip and the shape is `rounded` or `circle`
238	- a clip in the layout's reach holds a zoom or another action that moves it after `at`. A screen still at its full placement isn't asked in `corner`, `camera_full` and `screen_only`, since its zooms keep playing. Send `nest: true` to nest those clips first, in the same step, so the layout moves the nest and the zoom stays inside it.
239	- with `nest: true`, one of the clips to nest is already laid out, or nesting would make the camera a nest clip in a `rounded` or `circle` corner
240	- the project or the open nest changes while the tool reads the person masks. Call again.
241	
242	## `make_vertical_version`
243	
244	Makes a vertical (9:16), 4:5 or square (1:1) version of the top-level timeline, as [**File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**](/framing/make-vertical-version/) does. [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/) goes through what happens to each kind of clip. The tool has no `scope`, because it only works on the top-level timeline.
245	
246	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
247	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
248	| `shape` | string | Yes | The new shape: `9:16`, `4:5` or `1:1`. |
249	| `follow` | string | No | What a movie clip follows: `subject`, `face`, `person`, `salient`, `speaker` or `center`. Default `subject`. |
250	| `zoom` | number | No | How tight, 1 to 4 times the scale that fills the new canvas. Default 1. |
251	| `where_empty` | string | No | What a followed clip shows where nothing is found: `fit`, the whole picture on a blurred copy, or `center`. Default `fit`. |
252	| `mics` | array of integers | With `speaker` | `speaker` only: two to four clip ids, each a clip of a sound file or a camera's detached sound on its own track, standing for that track as one person's microphone. |
253	| `mic_faces` | array of integers | No | `speaker` only: each microphone's face number, in `mics`' order, faces numbered 1, 2 and so on from left to right. Left out, Frame Job matches them. |
254	| `copy` | boolean | No | `true` opens the version as a new project. `false` applies it to the project you name. Default `true`. |
255	| `path` | string | No | With `copy` only: where to save the new project, as an absolute path. `.framejob` is added when missing. Nothing may exist there yet. Without it the copy opens untitled. |
256	| `captions` | boolean | No | `true` re-pages each word caption track on the new canvas. `false` keeps caption tracks as placed, like any other clip. Default `true`. |
257	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
258	
259	The new canvas keeps the old short side, rounded down to even. From 1920 × 1080 that's 1080 × 1920, 1080 × 1350 or 1080 × 1080.
260	
261	This call makes a 9:16 copy and saves it:
262	
263	```json
264	{ "shape": "9:16", "path": "/Volumes/Work/Interview vertical.framejob" }
265	```
266	
267	It answers these keys beside `ok: true`:
268	
269	| Key | What it holds |
270	| --- | --- |
271	| `canvas` | The new `width` and `height`. |
272	| `cached` | False when an analysis ran first. |
273	| `clips` | One row per clip with a picture, in id order: `clip`, `treatment`, and `reason` when it did less than asked. Clips on a re-paged caption track have no row. They're in `captions`. |
274	| `cursor` | The clips followed by their cursor. |
275	| `speaker` | The clips framed on whoever is talking, each `clip`, `mics` and `mic_faces`. |
276	| `relaid` | Each re-laid switch, in time order: `camera`, `at` (ticks), `from`, `to` and, for a corner, `shape`. `from` and `to` are `switch_layout`'s layout words. |
277	| `backgrounds` | Whether the **Backgrounds** track was kept. |
278	| `more_tracks` | How many further tracks were made behind it, where clips overlap. |
279	| `re_eased` | How many actions were eased again at a cut. |
280	| `moves_carried` | How many actions carry a framing move. |
281	| `summary` | The same text the sheet shows, in sentences. |
282	| `captions` | `relaid` and `kept`, as `relay_captions` answers them. It's absent with `captions: false`. |
283	| `graphics` | `resized` (a count), `updated` (names) and `listed` (each `name` and `reason`). |
284	| `project` | The summary of the copy, or of the project you named. |
285	| `carried` | A copy only: the `files`, `bytes` and `seconds` carried over. |
286	| `saved` | With `path`: where the copy was saved. |
287	
288	A clip's `treatment` is one of:
289	
290	| `treatment` | What happened |
291	| --- | --- |
292	| `followed` | It follows its subject, cursor or speaker. |
293	| `whole` | It's shown whole on a blurred copy for its full length. |
294	| `kept` | It's kept as placed, rescaled from the old canvas. |
295	| `refilled` | A blurred copy or plate is made to fill the new canvas. |
296	| `removed` | A blurred copy was removed, because its clip is now framed. |
297	| `resized` | A graphic was re-sized to the new canvas. |
298	| `relaid` | A camera or screen was re-laid. |
299	| `not_followed` | It wasn't followed, and `reason` says why and what it did instead. |
300	
301	### Subject following
302	
303	Each movie clip that fills the old frame on one side is framed with `reframe_clip` from the old canvas, using your `follow`, `zoom` and `where_empty`. Where nothing is found, it's shown whole on a blurred copy by default. The copies go on a new **Backgrounds** track at the back, which is removed when nothing needs it.
304	
305	With `follow: center` the picture's centre is held and nothing is analysed.
306	
307	- A clip Frame Job won't frame, because it's on a matte track, rotated or spinning, is kept as placed, as `not_followed` with the reason.
308	- A movie whose file is missing is kept as placed in the same way, unless `follow` is `center`.
309	
310	### Screen recordings follow the cursor
311	
312	A screen recording whose media has a cursor file follows its cursor, never faces, with any `follow` but `center`, which centres it. Its own zooms and pans are replaced. If the cursor file can't be read it's shown whole on a blurred copy, and its `reason` says so.
313	
314	### `follow: speaker` in a vertical
315	
316	With `follow: speaker`, a movie clip of two to four people, playing beside two or more of the microphones in `mics`, is framed on whoever is talking, as [`follow: speaker`](#follow-speaker) frames it. Every other movie clip follows its faces.
317	
318	- Each clip in `mics` stands for its track. Under a shot, the clip used is the one on that track that overlaps the shot most.
319	- A clip on a microphone's track is never framed this way, and neither is a screen recording with a cursor file.
320	- Faces are matched by Frame Job, or named with `mic_faces`.
321	- When one clip can't be framed on the speaker, such as a clip that changes shot, it follows its faces instead and its `reason` says why. The rest of the call goes ahead.
322	
323	See [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/).
324	
325	### Camera layouts re-laid
326	
327	A camera and the screen behind it laid out with **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸** are re-laid, not reframed, with [`follow: layout`](#follow-layout) once per camera. Each switch is solved again for the new canvas at its old time, length and curve, and **Side by Side** becomes **Stacked** on a tall canvas. They're never followed and get no blurred copy.
328	
329	Their `treatment` is `relaid`. A layout edited by hand is kept as placed, as `not_followed` with the reason. The answer's `relaid` lists each switch.
330	
331	### Stills, graphics, titles and plates
332	
333	| The clip | What happens | `treatment` |
334	| --- | --- | --- |
335	| A still picture or a nest that fills the frame on one side | Centred, with the reason | `not_followed` |
336	| A graphic exactly the old canvas's size | Re-sized to the new canvas. Its position and its action ends' positions move by the two sides' ratios, and its scale is kept. | `resized` |
337	| A title, a picture-in-picture, a shape or a graphic of another size | Kept as placed, rescaled from the old canvas | `kept` |
338	| An old **Blurred Background** copy | Removed when its clip is framed, else made to fill the new canvas | `removed` or `refilled` |
339	| A full-frame shape plate, or an image named **Background** | Made to fill the new canvas | `refilled` |
340	
341	### A copy or in place
342	
343	By default a new project opens, named `<name> (9:16)`, `(4:5)` or `(1:1)`, holding the change as its one undo step, **Make Vertical**. It carries the project's caches and analysis, and the project you named doesn't change. With `path`, the copy is saved there. The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks before a call that names a `path`.
344	
345	With `copy: false`, the change goes into the project you named as one undo step, **Make Vertical**.
346	
347	### Captions re-paged
348	
349	Each word caption track is split into pages again for the new canvas, from its own words, as [`relay_captions`](/mcp/tools-captions/#relay_captions) does. A track it can't re-lay is kept as placed. The answer's `captions` lists those `relaid` and those `kept`, each kept one with its reason. With `captions: false`, caption tracks stay as placed and the key is left out. See [Re-lay captions for a canvas](/captions/re-lay-captions/).
350	
351	### Bundled templates updated
352	
353	In a copy, the project's own older copies of the bundled `lower-third`, `title-card`, `callout`, `bar-chart`, `counter` and `kinetic-type` templates are rewritten with the current template, which fits a tall canvas. A module is known by its text, never its name, and its old text is kept as its previous revision. The names land in `graphics.updated`.
354	
355	With `copy: false` nothing is rewritten, and each one is in `graphics.listed` with the reason. A module that sizes itself by the canvas's height is listed either way, because it may not fit the narrow frame.
356	
357	### Analysis and refusals
358	
359	The tool analyses the movie clips on your Mac first, as `reframe_clip` does, and waits up to 60 s. A screen recording with a cursor file isn't analysed, and neither is anything with `follow: center`. Past 60 s nothing is made. The answer is `ok: true` with `analyzing` and a `note`, as in [The analysis wait](#the-analysis-wait), so call again.
360	
361	It's refused, with nothing made, when:
362	
363	- a nest is open. Leave it with `set_scope` first.
364	- `path` is given with `copy: false`
365	- another open project holds `path`, or something already exists there
366	- the canvas already has that shape
367	- the canvas can't change or the **Backgrounds** track can't be added, such as when the project already has too many tracks
368	- a clip can't be framed even with `keep`
369	- `follow: speaker` has no `mics`, or a clip id in `mics` isn't a clip
370	- `follow: speaker` finds no movie clip playing beside two of the microphones
371	- a microphone is still being analysed or never speaks
372	- the analysis fails or is stopped, or the project or the open nest changes during the wait

391	
392	These three tools cut between synced cameras: `copy_pieces` copies stretches of a clip onto another track at the same times, `switch_angle` re-picks one shot from another camera, and `switch_by_speaker` cuts a whole Program track from who is talking.
393	
394	<AtAGlance
395	  menu={['Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸', 'Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…']}
396	  tools={['copy_pieces', 'switch_angle', 'switch_by_speaker']}
397	  needs="Nothing to set up. When there's only one microphone, faces are read on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
398	/>
399	
400	Times are in ticks, 600,000 a second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). [Set up several cameras](/multicam/set-up/) says how the tracks should be laid out first.
401	
402	## `copy_pieces`
403	
404	Copies pieces of a clip onto another track at the same project times. It has no menu item of its own: it's what [**Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**](/multicam/switch-angle/) and [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) write with. An agent can cut a whole program with one `copy_pieces` per camera clip. See [Copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/).
405	
406	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
407	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
408	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to copy pieces of. |
409	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track the pieces land on. It must be free over every range. |
410	| `ranges` | array of `[from, to]` pairs | Yes | The stretches to copy, in project times, inside the clip and not overlapping. At least one pair. |
411	| `video` | boolean | No | Sets each piece's picture on or off. Default: the clip's own setting. |
412	| `audio` | boolean | No | Sets each piece's sound on or off. Default: the clip's own setting. |
413	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside that nest, where the times and tracks are the nest's. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
414	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
415	
416	Each piece is exactly what two splits at its range's ends would leave in the middle: the same source frames at the same times, with speed, a ramp, reversal, a graphic's own timeline, timed words and actions cut as a split cuts them. So a piece of a synced camera shows that camera's own frame at every time. Pieces get new ids, no transition and no link.
417	
418	This call copies the stretches from 0 to 2 s and from 5 to 7 s of clip 5 onto track 3:
419	
420	```json
421	{ "clip": 5, "track": 3, "ranges": [[0, 1200000], [3000000, 4200000]] }
422	```
423	
424	Each range's ends snap to the frame grid, a pair written backwards is the same range, and a range that's empty on the grid is skipped. Ranges may touch. If every range is empty, nothing changes.
425	
426	It answers `ok: true`, `new_clips` (the pieces) and the `project` summary. It's one undo step, **Copy Pieces**.
427	
428	An unknown clip or track stops the call, and so does an empty `ranges`. Then it's refused, with nothing changed, in this order:
429	
430	1. The clip is a nest clip, because a piece of it would replay the nest from its first frame.
431	2. A range is outside the clip.
432	3. Two ranges overlap.
433	4. The destination track is locked.
434	5. The destination track holds a clip over a range. The sentence names that clip and its ends.
435	
436	A copy that would take the project past 4,096 clips also fails.
437	
438	## `switch_angle`
439	
440	Re-picks one shot from another camera, as [**Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**](/multicam/switch-angle/) does.
441	
442	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
443	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
444	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The shot to re-pick: a clip on the program track. |
445	| `angle` | integer | Yes | The id of the track to re-pick it from. |
446	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
447	
448	An angle is a track whose video clips cover the shot's whole span. A clip with its picture off, or on a hidden track, still counts. The menu lists at most nine angles, and the tool can name any track.
449	
450	The shot is deleted and the angle copied over the same span, one piece per angle clip the span crosses, each with the shot's picture and sound settings. Where two angle clips overlap, the later one takes over at its own start. The clips either side are trimmed back to their old edges, so a dissolve on either edge is formed again with its kind, curve and sound shape.
451	
452	The shot's grade, punch-in, actions and other settings don't carry over.
453	
454	It takes no `scope`. It works in the nest `set_scope` has open.
455	
456	| Key | What it holds |
457	| --- | --- |
458	| `ok` | `true`. |
459	| `step` | **Switch Angle**, or **Switch Angle (transition removed)** when a dissolve couldn't be formed again against a short piece and was dropped. |
460	| `pieces` | The new clip ids, in time order. |
461	| `transitions_removed` | How many dissolves were dropped, from 0 to 2. |
462	| `project` | The summary. |
463	
464	It's one undo step, named as `step` says. An unknown clip or track stops the call. It's refused, with nothing changed, when:
465	
466	- the angle is the shot's own track
467	- the shot's track is locked
468	- the shot is linked to its detached sound
469	- the angle doesn't cover the shot. The sentence names the first tick with nothing to show.
470	- an edge is held short of where it needs to go, for example by a speed ramp. The sentence names the clip and the tick it reached.
471	- one of the edits that make up the re-pick can't be made. The sentence is that edit's own.
472	
473	## `switch_by_speaker`
474	
475	Cuts a Program track from synced cameras, showing whoever talks on each microphone, as [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) does. Run [`sync_audio`](/mcp/tools-audio/#sync_audio) first, because it trusts where the clips sit. Then select the clips with [`set_selection`](/mcp/tools-view-state/#set_selection), because it reads the selected clips.
476	
477	It takes no `scope`. It works in the nest `set_scope` has open.
478	
479	### Switch by Speaker options
480	
481	Every argument is optional. [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/) explains the ones the sheet shows.
482	
483	| Argument | Type | What it does |
484	| --- | --- | --- |
485	| `speakers` | array of `{mic, angle}` | Who is who: one object per person, both track ids. A camera's detached sound may be a `mic`. One `mic` named for two or more cameras is [faces mode](#faces-mode). Default: the pairing the selection implies. |
486	| `wide` | integer or null | The wide camera, which opens the cut and shows during crosstalk, or null for none. While nobody talks the current shot holds. It must be one of the cameras. Default: the one camera no speaker uses, when exactly one is left. With one microphone and no `speakers`, every camera is a speaker, so there's none. |
487	| `from` | integer | The range's start, in ticks. Give it with `to`. |
488	| `to` | integer | The range's end, after `from`. Give it with `from`. |
489	| `min_shot` | number | Seconds. A shorter shot merges into a neighbour. 0.5 to 30. Default 2, or 3 in faces mode. |
490	| `min_turn` | number | Seconds. A shorter turn, such as a reply, starts no shot. 0.2 to 10. Default 1. The sheet doesn't show it. |
491	| `lead` | number | Seconds a cut comes before the new speaker's first word. 0 to 1. Default 0.2. |
492	| `crosstalk` | string | What a second or more of crosstalk shows: `wide`, or `hold` to stay on the current speaker. Default `wide`. |
493	| `bleed_db` | number | How many dB below a speaker's own level counts as the other person's voice bleeding in, never a turn. 3 to 40. Default 15. |
494	| `dominance_db` | number | How many dB one active microphone must lead every other to count alone. 0 to 30. Default 8. The sheet doesn't show it. |
495	| `wide_after` | number or null | Seconds. Once one person has held the screen this long, cut to the wide for `min_shot`. 2 to 600. Default null, which is off. |
496	| `mute_cameras` | boolean | Turns the cameras' own sound off inside the range. Default: on when no microphone is a camera. |
497	| `track` | integer | Replaces the shots on this track, an earlier Program track, instead of adding one. It must be unlocked, in front of the cameras, hold no selected clip, and hold only pieces of the cameras over the range. |
498	| `apply` | boolean | `false` answers without editing. See [Preview with `apply: false`](#preview-with-apply-false). Default `true`. |
499	| `project` | string | The open project to act on, by path. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |
500	
501	A number outside its range stops the call and says the range, where the sheet would pull it back in.
502	
503	This call plans a cut with longer shots that stays on the current speaker during crosstalk, without editing anything:
504	
505	```json
506	{ "min_shot": 3, "crosstalk": "hold", "apply": false }
507	```
508	
509	### What it reads
510	
511	- **The cameras:** a camera is a track holding a selected clip with a picture.
512	- **The microphones:** by default these are the tracks holding a selected sound-only clip. With none, each camera with sound is its own microphone. Microphones are paired with cameras front to back, and a track you name in `speakers` still needs a selected clip with its sound on.
513	- **The range:** `from` and `to`, else the In–Out range, else the extent of the selected camera clips.
514	
515	It reads each microphone's loudness and speech, which Frame Job measures when a file is added. Then it cuts a shot `lead` before each new speaker's turn, holds through short replies and silence, shows the wide during crosstalk, and merges shots under `min_shot`.
516	
517	### What it writes
518	
519	It's one undo step, **Switch by Speaker**:
520	
521	- a new track named **Program** directly in front of the front-most camera, or with `track`, that track cleared over the range
522	- one [`copy_pieces`](#copy_pieces) for each camera clip a shot crosses, picture on and sound off
523	- the camera tracks hidden, or, when a camera track holds clips outside the range or a clip without a picture, its clips split at the range's ends with their pictures off inside
524	- with `mute_cameras`, the cameras' own sound off inside the range, never on a microphone's track
525	
526	Nothing outside the range changes, and the microphones are never edited. A selected clip that gets split keeps both halves selected.
527	
528	### What it answers
529	
530	| Key | What it holds |
531	| --- | --- |
532	| `ok` | `true`. |
533	| `applied` | Whether the project was edited. |
534	| `step` | **Switch by Speaker**. Only when applied. |
535	| `track` | The Program track's id. Null when not applied and no `track` was named. |
536	| `shots` | Each shot's `angle`, `start` and `end`. |
537	| `ops` | How many edits it makes. |
538	| `added` | How many clips it adds. |
539	| `speakers` | The pairing used, each `mic` and `angle`. |
540	| `wide` | The wide camera, or null. |
541	| `mute_cameras` | The value used. |
542	| `mode` | `microphones` or `faces`. |
543	| `note` | Faces mode only: "Faces guess who is talking; check the cuts." |
544	| `project` | The summary. |
545	
546	### Preview with `apply: false`
547	
548	Pass `apply: false` to see the planned shots without editing the project. The answer has the same keys, with `applied` false and no `step`. It's the same work as a real run, so it stops for the same reasons.
549	
550	### Faces mode
551	
552	When one microphone is shared by two or more cameras, their faces decide who talks. This is the default when the selection holds exactly one microphone, and you also get it by naming one `mic` for two or more cameras. See [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/).
553	
554	While the microphone hears speech, each camera's on-device face analysis says whose mouth moves most, going by the largest face in the picture. A camera wins with 1.5 times the next camera's movement and more than a small minimum, and otherwise it counts as crosstalk.
555	
556	- A named `wide` takes no part in deciding who talks. If you name it without `speakers`, that camera stops being a speaker when it shares a microphone.
557	- `min_shot` defaults to 3.
558	- `mode` says `faces`, and `note` says the cuts are a guess, so check them.
559	
560	Where **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…** would show its **Analyzing** sheet, the tool finds the faces it still needs and waits up to 60 s. Past that it's refused, and what it covered is kept. Call it again to continue.
561	
562	### Switch by Speaker refusals
563	
564	Nothing changes when a call is refused. It stops first on a value it can't read, such as an unknown track, a `wide` that isn't a camera, only one of `from` and `to`, or a `to` not after `from`.
565	
566	These are checked together, and the sentence names every one that applies:
567	
568	- fewer than two cameras, or more than nine
569	- a speaker without a microphone or without a camera
570	- one microphone for two speakers, outside faces mode
571	- a microphone still being analysed, or with no speech in the range
572	- speech detection isn't available on this Mac
573	- a camera whose faces are still being found, or that shows no face whose mouth can be read
574	- a stretch no camera covers
575	
576	These each stop the call on their own:
577	
578	- a faces analysis that failed, was stopped, or didn't finish within the wait
579	- the project or the open nest changed during the wait
580	- more clips than the project may hold. Raise `min_shot` to make fewer shots.
581	- a `track` that can't take the shots: it's locked, it holds a selected clip, it isn't in front of the cameras, it has nothing in the range, or it holds a clip that isn't a piece of a camera
582	- a camera clip linked by **Detach Audio**. Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first.

Times are in ticks, 600,000 to a second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/) explains the analysis itself.

613	## `get_media_analysis`
614	
615	Reads an analysis of one media file, or of the part of it one clip plays. No menu item shows these results as numbers. **View ▸ Show Subjects** [draws](/framing/show-subjects/) the selected clip's faces and subjects at the playhead, from what's already been found, and never starts an analysis itself.
616	
617	| `kind` | What it finds |
618	| --- | --- |
619	| [`shots`](#kind-shots) | The hard cuts. |
620	| [`masks`](#kind-masks) | Where a person is, as runs of frames. |
621	| [`faces`](#kind-faces) | Every face, 10 times a second, with its tilt and how open the mouth is. |
622	| [`subjects`](#kind-subjects) | People and the regions the eye is drawn to, 10 times a second. |
623	| [`sound_events`](#kind-sound_events) | How likely laughter, applause, cheering, a crowd, music and speech are, every 0.75 s. |
624	
625	**Arguments**
626	
627	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
628	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
629	| `kind` | string | Yes | What to find: `shots`, `masks`, `faces`, `sound_events` or `subjects`. |
630	| `media` | integer | One of `media` and `clip` | The media file to analyse. |
631	| `clip` | integer | One of `media` and `clip` | A media clip. Its file is analysed over the part the clip plays. |
632	| `from` | integer | No | Where to start, in the file's own time played forwards, in ticks, not snapped. The file's start, or the start of the part the clip plays, by default. |
633	| `to` | integer | No | Where to stop, not included, in the file's own time. The file's end, or the end of the part the clip plays, by default. Must be after `from`. |
634	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
635	
636	`from` and `to` are file times, not timeline times. They're held inside the file, and with `clip` they're held inside the part the clip plays.
637	
638	**What it answers**
639	
640	Every kind answers these, as well as its own keys below:
641	
642	| Key | What it holds |
643	| --- | --- |
644	| `kind`, `media` | What was asked for and the file it was read from. |
645	| `clip` | The clip, when you named one. |
646	| `from`, `to` | The window that was read. |
647	| `size` | The media's upright picture size, as width and height. |
648	| `cached` | True when the answer came from the cache alone. |
649	| `stamp` | What the cache was made with. |
650	| `run` | Present only when this call ran the analysis: `queued_at`, `started_at` and `ended_at`, in seconds of the app's uptime. |
651	| `project` | The project summary. |
652	
653	With `clip`, each cut, sample or window also has `clip_time`, in ticks from the clip's start in its playing direction, through its speed, ramp and reversal, and `timeline`, the clip's start plus `clip_time`.
654	
655	**When it refuses**
656	
657	- You named both `media` and `clip`, or neither.
658	- `kind` isn't one of the five. The answer lists them.
659	- A media or clip id names nothing, or the clip isn't a media clip, so it has no media to analyse.
660	- A picture kind is asked of a file with no moving picture, which includes a still image: "Media 4 has no moving picture, so it has no shots to find."
661	- `sound_events` is asked of a file with no sound, or of a clip that plays in reverse, whose sound runs backwards.
662	- The file is missing. `relink_media` points it at the file.
663	- `to` isn't after `from` once both are held inside the file or the clip.
664	- The analysis fails, or the Assistant's **Stop** ends it.
665	- The kept results can't be read. The answer says which cache files to remove so they're made again.
666	
667	### Long analyses and big answers
668	
669	A call waits at most 60 s. After that it stops and says how much of the window was covered, for example "The faces analysis of media 2 covered 41.0 s of the window's 120.0 s in the 60 s a call waits; what it covered is kept — call again to continue." What was covered is kept, so another call carries on from there.
670	
671	An answer over 512 KiB of cuts, runs, samples or windows is refused, and the sentence names the largest `to` that fits. So read a long file in `from` and `to` windows. Here's how much fits in one answer:
672	
673	| Kind | One row | One answer holds |
674	| --- | --- | --- |
675	| `faces` | About 176 bytes with one face, 221 with `clip` | About 296 s of samples, 236 s with `clip`, and less with more faces in frame. Read about 2 minutes at a time. |
676	| `subjects` | About 177 bytes with one person and one salient box, 222 with `clip` | About 294 s of samples, 235 s with `clip` |
677	| `sound_events` | About 130 bytes | About an hour of windows |
678	
679	### `kind: shots`
680	
681	Finds the hard cuts. It answers `count` and `cuts`, sorted by time. Each cut has `frame`, the file's frame index, and `source`, its time in the file.
682	
683	- A cut inside a gradual dissolve isn't reported.
684	- A single flash frame isn't a cut.
685	- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can show as one cut.
686	
687	[`split_at_shots`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#split_at_shots) cuts clips at these moments. See [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/).
688	
689	### `kind: masks`
690	
691	Finds a person's outline in every frame and answers where a person is, never the masks themselves.
692	
693	| Key | What it holds |
694	| --- | --- |
695	| `mask_size` | The masks' own width and height. |
696	| `frames` | How many frames in the window have been analysed. |
697	| `subject_found` | Whether any frame holds a person. |
698	| `count` | How many runs there are. |
699	| `runs` | Each run of consecutive frames that agree, with `from`, `to`, `subject_found` and `frames`, in the file's own time. |
700	
701	A frame holds a person when at least 0.5 % of its mask is above half strength. `runs` have no `clip_time` or `timeline`, even with `clip`.
702	
703	[Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) draws these masks. A still picture's masks aren't this tool's. Use [`analyze_cutout`](#analyze_cutout) for those.
704	
705	### `kind: faces`
706	
707	Finds every face at 10 samples a second of the file's own time. It answers `rate`, `count` and `samples`.
708	
709	| Sample key | What it holds |
710	| --- | --- |
711	| `source` | The sample's instant in the file. |
712	| `frame` | The time of the frame it read, the first at or after `source` within one sample, or null. |
713	| `faces` | Each face in the sample. |
714	
715	| Face key | What it holds |
716	| --- | --- |
717	| `box` | `[x, y, w, h]`, from 0 to 1 of the upright picture, measured from its top-left corner. |
718	| `confidence` | How sure the detection is. |
719	| `roll`, `yaw` | How far the face is tilted and turned, in radians. |
720	| `mouth_gap` | The inner lips' height, over the face box's height. |
721	| `mouth_width` | The outer lips' width, over the face box's height. |
722	
723	`mouth_gap` over `mouth_width` is how open the mouth is. Values are rounded to 4 decimals, and are null where no value was found.
724	
725	Faces are ordered from left to right and carry no identity or name. To follow one, follow its box from sample to sample.
726	
727	### `kind: subjects`
728	
729	Finds people and the regions the eye is drawn to, at 10 samples a second. Every sample instant is also a `faces` sample. It answers `rate`, `count` and `samples`.
730	
731	Each sample has `source` and `frame`, as `faces` does, then `people` and `salient`. Both are lists of `box` and `confidence`, with boxes measured as faces' are and ordered from left to right, with no identity. A person box covers the head and shoulders. See [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/).
732	
733	### `kind: sound_events`
734	
735	Listens to the file's first sound track with Apple's Sound Analysis, in windows of 1.5 s that start every 0.75 s, and says how sure it is of six kinds of sound: laughter, applause, cheering, crowd, music and speech. It needs a file with sound, and an audio file works.
736	
737	| Key | What it holds |
738	| --- | --- |
739	| `window`, `hop` | The window's length and the step between windows, in ticks: 900,000 and 450,000. |
740	| `groups` | Each kind of sound, with `name`, `labels`, `first_class` and `threshold`. `labels` are the classifier's own labels behind that kind, and its confidence is the highest of theirs. |
741	| `count` | How many windows came back. |
742	| `windows` | Each window, with `source`, its start in the file, and a confidence from 0 to 1 for each of the six kinds. |
743	
744	Confidences are rounded to 4 decimals, and are null where a window runs past the end of the sound.
745	
746	:::note
747	Treat these as hints, never as a finding on their own. None of the six has been checked against labelled recordings, so `first_class` is false and `threshold` is null for all of them.
748	:::
749	
750	## `analyze_cutout`
751	
752	Reports where Remove Background stands for cutout clips and makes their masks now. It's the agent's version of **Status** and [**Analyze Now**](/effects/remove-background/#analyze-now) in the Clip tab's **Picture ▸ Background** section.
753	
754	A cutout clip is one with Remove Background on, through **Clip ▸ Remove Background**, the section's checkbox, or `cutout` in [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/). A clip's masks are made as soon as that's set, so an agent needs this tool only to wait for them or to read how they went. A still picture counts, and its one frame is made from the picture itself.
755	
756	A call asks for every frame the clips play and runs again an analysis that failed or was stopped. Frames already analysed are never analysed again. It then waits up to `wait` seconds for every clip to settle, which means reaching any state but `analyzing`. Running out of time isn't an error. The answer gives the state so far, and you call again to keep waiting. The Assistant's **Stop** ends the wait.
757	
758	**Arguments**
759	
760	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
761	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
762	| `clips` | array of integers | No | The cutout clips to answer for. Left out, every cutout clip in the timeline or nest that's open, in timeline order. |
763	| `wait` | number | No | How many seconds to wait for every clip to settle, from 0 to 60. Left out, it's 0, which answers now. |
764	| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |
765	
766	**What it answers**
767	
768	`clips`, a row for each clip, and the `project` summary. Each row has these keys:
769	
770	| Key | What it holds |
771	| --- | --- |
772	| `clip`, `media` | The clip and its media file. |
773	| `state` | Where it stands. See the next table. |
774	| `progress` | From 0 to 1. |
775	| `quality` | The clip's cutout quality, `standard` or `best`. |
776	| `frames` | How many frames of the file the clip plays, which is 1 for a picture. |
777	| `covered` | How many of those are analysed. |
778	| `ready` | Whether `covered` equals `frames`. |
779	| `subject_found` | Whether a subject was found. |
780	| `centroid` | `x` and `y`, the subject's mean centre over those frames, in the media's upright pixels from the top left with y going down. Null unless the state is `ready`. The app doesn't show this figure. |
781	| `error` | With `failed`, the sentence saying why. |
782	
783	| `state` | What it means | The app's **Status** |
784	| --- | --- | --- |
785	| `analyzing` | The masks are being made. | **Analyzing N %** |
786	| `ready` | Every frame is analysed, and a person, or a picture's foreground subject, was found. | **Ready** |
787	| `no_person` | Every frame is analysed and no person is in the clip, so it draws whole. | **No person found** |
788	| `no_subject` | A picture with subject `foreground` has no subject, so it draws whole. | **No subject found** |
789	| `failed` | The masks couldn't be made. | **Failed:** and the reason |
790	| `no_picture` | The clip plays no frame of its file. | **No picture to analyze** |
791	
792	**When it refuses**
793	
794	Nothing is done when:
795	
796	- `wait` is outside 0 to 60: "wait must be from 0 to 60 seconds."
797	- A clip id names nothing, or `clips` is empty.
798	- A clip you named has no Remove Background: "Clip 3 has no Remove Background; set_video `{cutout: {}}` turns it on."
799	- With `clips` left out, no clip in the open timeline or nest has it on.

title: "Tools: captions and transcripts"
description: Make, import, write out and re-page captions, and read the spoken words of a clip or the whole timeline, ready to cut.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools make captions and read speech. Four of them work with caption tracks, and two hand an agent the spoken words with their times, so it can cut by what was said.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Generate Captions…', 'File ▸ Import Captions…', 'File ▸ Export Captions…', 'File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas']}
  where="The Transcript tab"
  tools={['transcribe', 'import_captions', 'export_captions', 'relay_captions', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript']}
  needs={['A speech model on this Mac for on-device words, which a person installs', 'Your AssemblyAI key to transcribe in the cloud']}
/>

| To | Use | Changes the project |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Turn speech into captions | [`transcribe`](#transcribe) | Yes, one undo step, unless `place` is false |
| Bring in an `.srt` file | [`import_captions`](#import_captions) | Yes, one undo step |
| Write a track out as `.srt` or `.vtt` | [`export_captions`](#export_captions) | No |
| Page word captions again for a new canvas | [`relay_captions`](#relay_captions) | Yes, one undo step |
| Read one clip's words | [`get_transcript`](#get_transcript) | No |
| Read every word heard on the timeline | [`get_timeline_transcript`](#get_timeline_transcript) | No |

All six work in the timeline, or in the nest that [`set_scope`](/mcp/nests/) has open. None of them takes a `scope` key. Times are in ticks, 600,000 to a second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). How a call reports an edit, and how it reports a problem, is on [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).

### Transcribe engines

**`apple`** is the default. Speech recognition runs on this Mac and nothing leaves it. It needs no permission and has no length limit. Each run recognises the audio again, because this engine keeps nothing for `transcribe` to reuse, and `refresh` doesn't apply.

Speech models are installed per Mac, from the **Download** row in **File ▸ Generate Captions…**. `language` matches a tag such as `en-US`, a language's display name, or a bare code such as `en`, which takes the first matching language on this Mac.

**`assemblyai`** sends the audio of every media file behind the clips you named to AssemblyAI, a cloud service that bills for it. It sends the whole file, not only the parts in use. The transcript is deleted from AssemblyAI once the words have been read back. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/).

:::caution
Don't choose `assemblyai` for somebody else's recording without their say-so. Audio leaves the Mac and the owner of the key pays for it.
:::

- **The engine is never remembered.** Left out, it's `apple`, whatever the Generate Captions sheet last chose. An agent that wants the cloud says so on every call.
- **Each file is kept.** One transcript per media file is kept in the project package, so a second run over the same files with the same settings makes no request and lists them under `cached`. See [Reuse a transcript](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#reuse-a-transcript).
- **`refresh`** ignores what's kept and uploads again, and the file is billed again.
- **The key.** A new transcription needs your AssemblyAI key. A run whose every file already has a current transcript needs no key and makes no network request, unless `refresh` is true. If AssemblyAI hasn't confirmed deleting a transcript and no key is set, `note` says so, and a later run with a key for the same account and region tries the deletion again.
- **`language`.** `auto`, the default, detects the language and the answer reports it. Any other code goes to AssemblyAI unchecked, and one it doesn't support comes back as AssemblyAI's own sentence after the upload.
- **The region.** It's a choice in [Settings](/captions/assemblyai-key/), and no argument sets it. `endpoint` tells you where a run's requests went.

The built-in Assistant can't use this engine. A call with `engine: "assemblyai"` is withheld from it, and it points you to **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, which shows what's uploaded and what it costs. See [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/).

### Speakers and vocabulary

Both need `engine: "assemblyai"`. The sheet's rows are described on [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#split-the-words-by-speaker).

`speakers: true` asks AssemblyAI who says what, and a change of speaker then starts a new cue. With `subtitles`, each speaker's cues take their own colour: white, yellow, cyan, then green in order of first appearance, then round again. A speaker is a label within one media file, so one person in two files can come back as two speakers.

`vocabulary` tells AssemblyAI the words and phrases to expect, such as pr

... [11341 characters truncated] ...

t comes from, the timeline track it plays on and its media file. A nested word's track is its nest clip's. |
| `engine` | `assemblyai` or `apple`. |
| `filler` | True for a [filler word](#fillers-in-a-transcript). |
| `speaker` | The speaker, when the transcript labelled one. |
| `editable`, `why` | Whether cutting it is safe, and why not when it isn't. |
| `id` | The word's identity across edits. |
| `cut_start`, `cut_end` | The range the Transcript tab cuts this word by. |

**When it refuses**

- `to` isn't after `from`, or the window is wholly outside the timeline.
- A `tracks` id names no track.
- The `language` tag is misspelt.
- A file needs this Mac's recogniser and the language's speech model isn't installed. The tool never downloads one.
- A read fails, or is stopped, and the answer gives the recogniser's sentence.

### Heard words and editable words

Words come from every clip that plays speech from a media file, clips inside nests included. A clip that's muted, soloed out or at volume 0 isn't heard and gives no words.

A clip whose words can't be read is listed under `no_words` with the reason instead: its audio switched off, played in reverse, or its file missing, for example.

`editable` is false, with a sentence in `why`, for a word:

- inside a nest. Open the nest with `set_scope` and read again to cut words inside it. A person opens one with **Clip ▸ Open Nest**, <kbd>⌘↓</kbd>.
- under a transition, where a cut would leave one clip's tail under its neighbour.
- on a locked track, where a cut would leave the word in place and move everything after it.

`id` names a word across edits elsewhere on the timeline. It has four parts:

| Part | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `nest_path` | The nest clips the word plays through. |
| `media` | Its media file. |
| `source` | Its start in the media's own time, in ticks, as the recogniser put it. |
| `k` | How many earlier words have the same three, which is 0 unless one piece of the file plays twice. |

### Read once per file

Each file without a current AssemblyAI transcript is read whole by this Mac's recogniser the first time it's needed, at about 0.7 s per minute of speech on an M2 Max. The words are saved in the project, so a later call answers at once.

Trimming a clip, adding another clip of the same file, or reading again later doesn't read the file again. The saved words are used while the file and the macOS version stay the same. The Assistant's **Stop** ends a read, unless the Transcript tab is reading that file too, and nothing is saved from a stopped read. The Transcript tab's own **Stop** leaves an agent's read running. See [Where the transcript's words come from](/captions/transcript-words/).

An on-device word's start is moved to its sound as in [`get_transcript`](#where-the-words-come-from), and `notes` names any file still waiting for voice detection.

### Duplicate speech

When two clips of different files carry the same speech at the same time, such as a camera's sound and a separate microphone, `notes` names the pair and both sets of words stay in `words`. Mute one, or switch its audio off, to read the speech once.

### Paging

At most 2,000 words come back in one answer. When there's more, `truncated` is true and `next_from` says where to call again. Pass it as `from`.

A word overlapping that point can come back again on the next page, with the same `id`, so match words by `id`. A pause is listed on the page that holds the word before it.

### Cut words and pauses

`cut_start` and `cut_end` are the range the Transcript tab cuts a word by when it alone is deleted, snapped to frames. The range runs from where the word's sound starts to where the next word's sound starts, at most 1 s past the word's end, widened over any other track's word it would cut into. See [Where a word cut falls](/captions/delete-words/#where-a-word-cut-falls).

To cut a run of words:

<Steps>

1. Call `get_timeline_transcript` and find the words.

2. Check that each word in the run has `editable` true.

3. Call [`ripple_delete_ranges`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete_ranges) once, with one range in `ranges`, from the first word's `cut_start` to the last word's `cut_end`.

4. Read the transcript again before the next cut, because everything after a cut moves. The ids still name the same words.

</Steps>

Each row of `pauses` is a silence over 1 s between two words of one clip, read from voice detection:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `start`, `end` | Where the silence runs. |
| `cut_start`, `cut_end` | What the Transcript tab cuts when the pause is deleted, with 0.2 s kept at each end, snapped to frames. |
| `clip`, `track`, `media` | Where it is. |
| `follows`, `precedes` | The ids of the words before and after it. |

To shorten a pause, call `ripple_delete_ranges` with `[[cut_start, cut_end]]` as `ranges`. Not every silence is listed. See [When a pause isn't shown](/captions/shorten-pauses/#when-a-pause-isnt-shown).
