content.content:
- **The region.** It's a choice in [Settings](/captions/assemblyai-key/), and no argument sets it. `endpoint` tells you where a run's requests went.

The built-in Assistant can't use this engine. A call with `engine: "assemblyai"` is withheld from it, and it points you to **File ▸ Generate Captions…**, which shows what's uploaded and what it costs. See [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/).

### Speakers and vocabulary

Both need `engine: "assemblyai"`. The sheet's rows are described on [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#split-the-words-by-speaker).

`speakers: true` asks AssemblyAI who says what, and a change of speaker then starts a new cue. With `subtitles`, each speaker's cues take their own colour: white, yellow, cyan, then green in order of first appearance, then round again. A speaker is a label within one media file, so one person in two files can come back as two speakers.

`vocabulary` tells AssemblyAI the words and phrases to expect, such as product names, people and identifiers. Terms are trimmed, repeats are dropped keeping the first spelling, and the list stops at 1,000 terms. `note` says so when it was cut.

### Check a transcript before placing it

`place: false` answers the cues and changes nothing, with no edit and no undo step. Use it to read a transcript before committing to it.

You can't combine it with `replace` or with a look set to true, because nothing is placed. To place the captions, call again without `place`. With AssemblyAI the second call reuses the kept transcript and uploads nothing.

### Caption styles and paging

`style` chooses how the words look. It's the same choice as **Style** in the sheet, and the default is never what the sheet last chose. See [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).

| `style` | What it makes |
| --- | --- |
| `subtitles` | Two-line cues in the Caption preset. The default. |
| `highlight` | Montserrat Black, upper case, the word being said in yellow with a pop. |
| `pill` | Montserrat ExtraBold, upper case, the word being said on a violet pill. |
| `karaoke` | Montserrat ExtraBold as written, up to two lines, words turning yellow. |
| `build` | Anton, upper case, words appearing one by one. |
| `one_word` | Bebas Neue, one large word at a time. |

Every style but `subtitles` is a word style, and makes pages rather than cues. A page is the group of words on screen at one time. Each page holds its words' timings, so the word being said is drawn as the style says.

A page is filled to the width it will measure on this canvas in that style, at most 0.86 of the canvas width, not to a word count. It sits on one line, or up to two with `karaoke`. A page also closes at:

- a change of speaker
- a gap of 0.25 s or more
- a word ending in `.`, `?`, `!` or `…`
- 3 s on screen

A lone word too wide for the canvas shrinks, down to 80 % of the style's size, before it wraps. Pages stay inside their own clip. A page holds for 0.5 s after its last word, or runs up to the next page if that starts sooner.

### Caption looks

`slide`, `fill` and `dim` add a look to a word style's pages, as the sheet's three boxes do. Each is false unless given, and never what the sheet last chose. See [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/).

| Argument | The sheet's box | What it does | Works with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `slide` | **Slide the pill** | The pill slides from the word before to the word being said, over 0.2 s or sooner, instead of jumping. | `pill` |
| `fill` | **Fill words as spoken** | The word being said fills from left to right as it's spoken, taking 0.6 s at most. | `highlight`, `karaoke`, `build` |
| `dim` | **Dim in pauses** | The page fades to half its opacity in a pause of 0.25 s or more. | All five word styles |

True with any other style, or with `place: false`, where it would show nothing, is refused and the answer names the argument. False is always accepted. Words from engine `apple` rarely carry a pause that long, so `dim` shows mostly with `assemblyai`.

Whenever one of the three was given, a placed run lists under `looks` the ones that were on.

### Restyle captions

To change a word style, run `transcribe` again with `replace: true`. See [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).

`replace` removes, in the same undo step, every track this command could have made over these clips: a track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips, each of which overlaps a clip being transcribed. The answer lists those tracks under `replaced`.

It needs a word style and `place` true. A style is only a display choice, so with AssemblyAI a kept transcript is reused whatever style you ask for, and restyling uploads nothing. Engine `apple` recognises the audio again.

## `get_transcript`

Reads one clip's spoken words with their times on the timeline, ready for `ripple_delete_ranges`. Use it when you care about one clip. To work across the timeline, or to cut exactly where the Transcript tab would, use [`get_timeline_transcript`](#get_timeline_transcript). The Assistant uses this tool to [cut a false start](/cleanup/false-starts/). No menu item shows these words clip by clip. The nearest view is the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/). The tool edits nothing, makes no undo step and never uploads anything.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip whose words to read, in its own timeline position and speed. |
| `language` | string | No | A language tag, such as `en-US`, for this Mac's recogniser only. By default this Mac's own language, or the nearest one installed. A kept AssemblyAI transcript answers in its own language. |
| `from` | integer | No | Where on the timeline to start, in ticks, snapped to frames. The clip's start by default. See [The from and to window](#the-from-and-to-window). |
| `to` | integer | No | Where on the timeline to stop, in ticks, snapped to frames. The clip's end by default. Must be after `from`. |
| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |

**What it answers**

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `words` | The words sorted by start, each with `text`, `start`, `end` and `filler`, and `speaker` where the transcript labelled it. |
| `count` | How many words came back. |
| `engine` | `assemblyai` for a kept transcript, or `apple` for this Mac's recogniser. |
| `language` | The language of the words, when known. |
| `fillers_reported` | Whether the transcript was made with filler words. See [Fillers in a transcript](#fillers-in-a-transcript). |
| `cached` | With engine `apple`, whether the answer came from what was already heard. |
| `clip`, `media` | The clip and its media file. |
| `from`, `to` | The window read, when one was given. |
| `note` | Anything to know: no words were heard, fillers may be missing, or word starts haven't been moved yet. |
| `project` | The project summary. |

**When it refuses**

- The clip doesn't exist, or it has no words to read: "Clip 3 has no words to read: its audio is switched off." The reason can also be that it isn't a media file, plays in reverse, has no audio track, or that its file is missing.
- The window is empty, or outside the clip.
- The `language` tag is misspelt. The answer lists the tags speech recognition knows, 24 at most.
- There's no kept transcript and the language's speech model isn't installed. The tool never downloads one. A person installs it from **File ▸ Generate Captions…**.
- A read fails, or is stopped, and the answer gives the recogniser's sentence.

### Where the words come from

The words come from the file's current AssemblyAI transcript, kept in the project, when it has one. That transcript comes from an earlier AssemblyAI run, such as [`transcribe`](#transcribe) or the sheet. Otherwise this Mac's own speech recogniser runs over the clip. Reading never uses the network and needs no key.

- **Where a word starts.** An on-device word's start is moved to where its sound begins, using the file's voice detection and waveform. The recogniser's own start is often early, inside the pause before the word. Until voice detection has finished with the file, starts are the recogniser's and `note` says so, so ask again once it has. AssemblyAI words and every word's end are as transcribed.
- **Saved for next time.** What the recogniser heard is saved in the project for each media file and language. A later request inside a stretch it has heard comes back at once, even from another clip of the same file at another speed, and `cached` says so. It's used only while the media file and the macOS version are unchanged.
- **Speed.** Words are placed through the clip's speed, including a speed ramp, so their times match what plays on the timeline.
- **Language.** On-device recognition uses this Mac's language unless `language` names another.
- **Stopping.** The Assistant's **Stop** ends a long on-device read, and nothing is saved from a stopped read.

### Fillers in a transcript

`filler` is true for um, uh, hmm, mhm, uh-huh, ah, huh, hm, m, er and erm, in any case and with punctuation at their edges trimmed.

`fillers_reported` says whether the transcript was made with filler words at all. It's false for every on-device read, and for a kept transcript made without them. A filler can then be in the audio and missing from `words`, and `note` says so. See [Transcripts for filler words](/cleanup/filler-transcripts/).

### The from and to window

`from` and `to` are timeline times, and they return only the words that overlap that part of the timeline. A word crossing an edge comes back whole, with its own times.

Either end can be given alone. A missing `from` is the clip's start and a missing `to` is its end. The window is held inside the clip, and the answer gives it back as `from` and `to`. An empty window, or one wholly outside the clip, is refused.

With a window, the on-device recogniser hears only that part and 2 s either side. That's faster, but a windowed read can differ slightly from a read of the whole clip.

## `get_timeline_transcript`

Reads every word heard on the timeline, or inside the open nest, in timeline order, with nested clips included. Each word carries the range the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/) would cut it by. It edits nothing, makes no undo step, never makes a network request and needs no key.

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | integer | No | Where on the timeline to start, in ticks, snapped to frames. The timeline's start by default. A word across this edge comes back whole. |
| `to` | integer | No | Where on the timeline to stop, in ticks, snapped to frames. The timeline's end by default. Must be after `from`. |
| `tracks` | array of integers | No | Only the words playing on these timeline tracks. Every track by default. |
| `language` | string | No | A language tag, such as `en-US`, for this Mac's recogniser only. By default this Mac's own language, or the nearest one installed. Each language is kept apart, and a kept AssemblyAI transcript answers in its own language. |
| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. The frontmost project when left out. |

**What it answers**

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `words` | Each word, ordered by start, then end, then the front track first. Its keys are below. |
| `count` | How many words are on this page. |
| `pauses` | Each pause. See [Cut words and pauses](#cut-words-and-pauses). |
| `media` | Each file read, with `media`, `engine`, `language` and `fillers_reported`. |
| `no_words` | Clips that can't be read, each with `clip`, `nest_path`, `tag` and `reason`. |
| `notes` | Sentences to read: the same speech twice, words not transcribed with fillers, or word starts not moved yet. |
| `from`, `to` | The window read, when one was given. |
| `truncated`, `next_from` | Present when there's more. See [Paging](#paging). |
| `project` | The project summary. |

Each word has these keys:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `text`, `start`, `end` | The word and its timeline times. |
| `clip`, `track`, `media` | The clip it comes from, the timeline track it plays on and its media file. A nested word's track is its nest clip's. |
| `engine` | `assemblyai` or `apple`. |
| `filler` | True for a [filler word](#fillers-in-a-transcript). |
| `speaker` | The speaker, when the transcript labelled one. |
| `editable`, `why` | Whether cutting it is safe, and why not when it isn't. |
| `id` | The word's identity across edits. |
| `cut_start`, `cut_end` | The range the Transcript tab cuts this word by. |

**When it refuses**

- `to` isn't after `from`, or the window is wholly outside the timeline.
- A `tracks` id names no track.
- The `language` tag is misspelt.
- A file needs this Mac's recogniser and the language's speech model isn't installed. The tool never downloads one.
- A read fails, or is stopped, and the answer gives the recogniser's sentence.

## Cut what the tools found

Pass the `ranges` from `detect_silence` or `detect_fillers` to [`ripple_delete_ranges`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#ripple_delete_ranges). That's what **Remove** does in each sheet, and it makes the whole cut one undo step.

```json
{ "ranges": [[1200000, 1500000], [3000000, 3240000]] }
```

For filler words, look at `needs_transcript` in the `detect_fillers` answer first. Any media named there needs [`transcribe_for_fillers`](#transcribe_for_fillers) before its fillers can be found, so make the transcript and call `detect_fillers` again.

An agent isn't held to the ranges it was given: it can drop some or change them first. `ripple_delete_ranges` takes `scope` like any edit, so it can reach a nest without opening it. See [How a clean-up cut works](/cleanup/how-cleanup-cuts-work/).

## Word timings and word style

A caption page is a text clip with a time on each word. `set_text` edits these like any other text key. See [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/) and [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).

### Word timings

`words` is one `{start, end}` per whitespace-separated word of `content`, in ticks from the clip's start, or `[]` for an untimed page.

- When the list isn't empty, it must hold exactly one timing for each word. If not, the call answers "this text is timed word by word: 5 timings for 6 words".
- A change to `content` that alters the word count must send `words: []` in the same patch.
- A word's `end` can't come before its `start`, and each `start` can't come before the one before it. Two words can start together.
- A negative `start` is allowed. It means the word was already being said when the clip began.
- The times snap to the frame grid, so two words can land on one frame.

`words` can't be animated: `set_action_end` refuses it.

### Word style

`word_style` is `null` or an object. It replaces `animation` on the page.

| Key | What it does | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `highlight` draws the whole page and picks out the active word. `build` makes words appear as they're said. | `highlight`, `build` | `highlight` |
| `active_color` | The active word's colour. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
| `active_scale` | Where the active word's pop settles. 1 is no pop. | 1 to 1.5 | 1 |
| `active_pill` | A rounded plate behind the active word. | `null`, or `{color, padding, radius, glide}` | No plate |
| `spoken_color` | The colour of words already said. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
| `upcoming_color` | The colour of words not yet said, in `highlight` mode. | Four numbers | The text's colour |
| `active_fill` | Fills the active word left to right as it's said. | `true`, `false` | `false` |
| `pause_dim` | How far the words and pill fade in a pause. | 0 to 1 | 0 |

**The pill.** Its `padding` and `radius` are fractions of the text's `size`, starting from 0.2 and 0.25, and its `color` starts as purple. `glide` set to `true` slides the pill from the word before to the active one over 0.2 s, or sooner when the next word starts sooner, instead of jumping.

**The fill.** `active_fill` runs from the word's start to its end, taking 0.6 s at most. The part already said draws in `active_color` and the rest in `upcoming_color`, or isn't drawn yet in `build` mode. In `highlight` mode it shows only where those two colours differ.

**The pause dim.** `pause_dim` fades the words and the pill to 1 minus `pause_dim` of their opacity, over 0.1 s each way, in a pause of 0.25 s or more. A pause runs from one word's end to the next one's start, before a late first word, and after the last word until the clip ends.

```json
{ "word_style": { "active_pill": { "glide": true }, "pause_dim": 0.5 } }
```

title: "Tools: animation"
description: Add actions to a clip from an agent, set what they animate to, zoom to a region, and move, re-curve or remove them.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An [action](/motion/actions/) is a span on a clip over which its properties ease from what they are to an end state. These tools add one, say what it ends at, change its timing and take it away.

<AtAGlance
  tools={['add_action', 'add_zoom_action', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']}
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where="Clip tab ▸ action lane"
/>

The usual order is two calls. First, `add_action` with these arguments:

```json
{ "clip": 12, "at": 600000, "duration": 1200000 }
```

Then `set_action_end`, with the id it answered in `new_actions`:

```json
{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "video": { "scale": 1.4 } } }
```

Every time here is in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and is rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). An action's times are clip time, measured from the clip's own start, not the timeline's. `get_project` lists each clip's actions and their ids.

For a speed ramp in one step, see [`add_speed_ramp`](/mcp/tools-speed/#add_speed_ramp).

## `set_action_end`

Sets what an action animates to. It mirrors every inspector field you change while an action is selected. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) and [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip's id. |
| `action` | integer | Yes | The action's id. |
| `patch` | object | Yes | The end state, with `video`, `audio`, `text` and `graphic` groups and a top-level `speed`. |
| `off` | array of strings | No | `"group.key"` paths to switch off at the end. See [Switching off at an end](#switching-off-at-an-end). |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

```json
{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "video": { "opacity": 0 }, "audio": { "volume": 0.2 } } }
```

The patch merges into the end state key by key, at every depth, so a one-key `shadow` keeps the rest of it. A key set to `null` is removed from the end state, so that property stops being animated, and a group set to `null` removes the whole group.

The `video`, `audio` and `text` groups take the same keys as [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/), [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/) and [`set_text`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/). A colour is four numbers here too, and it ramps in OKLab with straight alpha. So do the chroma key's three numbers. `cursor.click_color` is a CSS colour, not four numbers, so it switches when the action ends.

A bad key or value is refused by its path with the group in it, such as `video.filters[1].kind`. Values aren't range-checked, though: an animation can aim past what a stored property could hold.

**Sound.** These `audio` keys animate: `muted`, `pan`, `mono`, `channels`, `eq`, `hum`, `noise_reduction`, `gate`, `leveller`, `de_esser`, `compressor`, `limiter` and `isolation`, beside `volume` and the fades.

- Numbers ramp.
- A switch changes when the action ends: a group or an EQ slot turned on, `muted`, `mono`, `channels`, an EQ slope, hum's frequency and harmonics, and the leveller's response.
- `isolation` ramps from 0 on a clip with none.
- `duck`, `keep_pitch`, the fade shapes and `voice` are stored but never animate.

See [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).

**What it answers.** `ok` and the `project` summary. With `speed` in the patch it can add the keys listed under [Speed in an action](#speed-in-an-action).

**When it refuses.** These keys are errors, a `null` included:

| Key | Why, and what to do instead |
| --- | --- |
| `video.motion` | It's a preset tied to the clip's two ends. Set it with `set_video`. |
| `video.hide_silent` | It isn't an animation target. Set it with `set_video`. |
| `text.words` | Word times belong to speech. Set them with `set_text`. |
| `video.cutout.subject`, `video.cutout.quality` | They hold for the whole clip. Set them with `set_video`. A cutout's `edge`, `feather` and `background` do animate. |
| Any `shape` key | Shapes can't be animated, so `shape` isn't a group here. |

### Animating graphic props

A graphic clip's props are a fourth group: `graphic: {props: {<key>: <value>}}`, keyed by what its module declares. It mirrors the Graphic sub-tab's **Properties** with an action selected. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

```json
{ "clip": 18, "action": 44, "patch": { "graphic": { "props": { "accent": "#ff5500", "count": 96 } } } }
```

- A value is checked as `set_graphic` checks it, minimum and maximum included, against the module as the project's graphics folder holds it now.
- A number ramps along the curve and arrives with decimals, so 64 to 129 is 96.5 halfway. A module that needs a whole number rounds it.
- A colour blends in OKLab, with straight alpha.
- A string, a boolean and an enum switch to the end's value when the action ends.
- An image prop switches when the action ends. `""` names no image there.
- A prop the clip holds no value for starts from the module's current default, written into the clip in the same undo step.
- `graphic.props.<key>: null` removes that prop from the end, and `graphic: null` removes the whole group.

`get_project` shows `kinds` beside `props`. Frame Job writes that and ignores any you send, so an end you read back can be sent again.

**When it refuses.**

- A prop its module marks `animate: false` is refused. Set it with `set_graphic`.
- `name`, `width`, `height`, `in` and `length` are refused: an action animates `graphic.props` only.
- While the module is missing or doesn't compile, a value is refused, and `get_graphic` says why. A `null` still removes.
- On a clip that isn't a graphic: "clip 7 is not a graphic clip".

### Speed in an action

`speed`, a number beside the groups, is a media clip's rate. The clip ramps to it along the curve, from the rate it's playing at when the action starts, and holds it after. It keeps its start and length, and plays more or less of its source. It mirrors the Speed section's **Rate** with an action selected. See [Build a ramp by hand](/speed/build-a-ramp/).

```json
{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": { "speed": 3 } }
```

The rate is clamped to ×0.1–×1000, and `speed: null` removes it.

Above ×12 the clip's audio is left out, and the call that takes it there answers with `audio_left_out` (the clip ids) and `audio_note`. Captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are re-timed in the same step: `captions_retimed` lists them, and `captions_removed` lists those whose speech it no longer plays.

**When it refuses.**

- An end rate that would read past the end of the clip's media. The sentence names the largest end rate that fits, or, when none down to ×0.1 does, the latest clip end that fits at ×0.1.
- `speed: null` when the clip would then read past the end of its media. The sentence names the latest clip end that fits.
- A value that isn't a number or `null`, or a clip that isn't a media clip.
- A rate on a linked clip: "clip 7 is linked to clip 8: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction".

### Switching off at an end

`off` turns an optional property off at the end of the action. The path is stored as a `null` in the end state, where a `null` in `patch` removes the key instead. So `off` means "this shadow goes away by the end", and a `null` in `patch` means "stop animating the shadow".

```json
{ "clip": 12, "action": 40, "patch": {}, "off": ["video.shadow", "audio.eq.band_2"] }
```

- A path is `"group.key"`, with a group of `video`, `audio` or `text` and one of its top-level keys, such as `video.shadow`, `text.width` or `audio.limiter`.
- One deeper path exists: `audio.eq.<slot>` switches that EQ slot off. The slots are `high_pass`, `low_shelf`, `band_1`, `band_2`, `band_3`, `high_shelf` and `low_pass`.
- Only optional keys can go off. A required key such as `video.opacity` is refused.
- A path can't also be named in `patch`.
- `graphic` paths are refused: name the value a prop ends at in `patch`.
- `video.cutout` is refused: `set_video` with `{cutout: null}` removes a cutout.
- `video.motion`, `video.hide_silent` and `text.words` are refused here too.

## `set_track`

Changes a track's name, its four switches, its matte and its mix. Anything you leave out keeps its value.

The switches are the track header's toggles and **Track ▸ Hide Video**, **Mute Audio**, **Lock Track** and **Solo**, see [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) and [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). `volume` and `pan` are **Track ▸ Mix…**, see [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track's id. |
| `name` | string | No | The track's new name. Spaces at either end are dropped, and an empty name leaves the track unnamed. |
| `hidden` | boolean | No | Drops the track's picture from the composition. |
| `muted` | boolean | No | Silences the track's sound. |
| `locked` | boolean | No | Keeps every ripple, insert and range edit off the track. |
| `solo` | boolean | No | Silences every other track in the same container that isn't also soloed. Mute wins on a track that's both, and pictures aren't touched. |
| `matte` | string | No | `none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma` or `luma_inverted`. See [Track mattes](#track-mattes). |
| `volume` | number | No | The track's fader as a linear gain from 0 to 4, multiplying every clip's own volume on it. 1 is unity, 4 is +12.04 dB and 0 is silent. |
| `pan` | number | No | The track's balance, from −1 (left) to 1 (right). It's a constant-power balance after each clip's own pan, and a mono source isn't panned. |
| `compressor` | object | No | The track's compressor, or `null` for off. See [A track's compressor and limiter](#a-tracks-compressor-and-limiter). |
| `limiter` | object | No | The track's limiter, or `null` for off. See [A track's compressor and limiter](#a-tracks-compressor-and-limiter). |
| `scope` | integer | No | Look the track up inside this nest. |
| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |

A container is the timeline, or one nest's own tracks. `volume` and `pan` play through nests: a nested clip is affected by its own track and by the track of every nest clip around it.

**Answers** with the project summary. A call that sets what's already there answers "made no change".

**Refuses** a call that names none of the optional arguments, and a `volume` or `pan` outside its range. Neither value is clamped.

### Track mattes

`matte` makes a track cut the track directly behind it in its container, as **Track ▸ Matte** does. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/).

| Value | In **Track ▸ Matte** | What cuts the track behind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | **Off** | Nothing. It's an ordinary track again. |
| `alpha` | **Alpha** | The matte track's alpha. |
| `alpha_inverted` | **Inverted Alpha** | Its alpha, inverted. |
| `luma` | **Luma** | Its brightness. |
| `luma_inverted` | **Inverted Luma** | Its brightness, inverted. |

The matte track's clips aren't drawn, but they still sound. Where the matte track shows nothing, the track behind shows uncut. A back-most matte track, or one in front of another matte track, cuts nothing.

### A track's compressor and limiter

`compressor` and `limiter` are **Track ▸ Mix…**'s **Compressor** and **Limit peaks**, see [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/). They run on the track's sub-mix, after every clip, its volume and its pan, compressor first. The limiter's ceiling is on what the track hands the mix.

Each takes an object, and that object **replaces the whole setting**. A key you leave out takes its default, not the value the track had. This is the opposite of [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#set_audio), where objects merge. `null` clears the setting, and leaving the argument out keeps it.

| `compressor` key | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `threshold_db` | −60 to 0 dB | −18 |
| `ratio` | 1 to 20 | 3 |
| `attack` | 0 or more ticks | 6,000 (10 ms) |
| `release` | 0 or more ticks | 120,000 (200 ms) |
| `makeup_db` | 0 to 24 dB | 0 |

| `limiter` key | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ceiling_db` | −24 to 0 dBTP | −1 |
| `release` | 600 to 600,000 ticks | 60,000 (100 ms) |

An unknown key, a mistyped value or a value out of range is refused, naming the key.

- **Timeline tracks only.** A nest's tracks have no compressor or limiter, so either argument is refused inside a nest. The track holding a nest clip is that nest's bus.
- **Exact in every export.** The preview runs them approximately.
- **Measuring tools don't hear them.** Normalize, the Loudness readout, Enhance Voice and Match Audio all measure without the track's compressor and limiter.

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools let an agent write a motion graphic, look at it without placing it, and put it on the timeline. [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/) tells that story from the top. This page is the reference for each tool.

<AtAGlance
  tools={['graphic_reference', 'write_graphic', 'get_graphic', 'render_graphic', 'list_graphics', 'insert_graphic', 'add_graphic_clip', 'set_graphic']}
  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab."
/>

A graphic's code is a **module**, the file `graphics/<name>.js` inside the project, and `name` in these tools is that file's name without `.js`. Fonts, pictures, renames, deletes and packages are on [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).

Every tool here also takes `project`, the path of an open project. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/). Times are in ticks, 600,000 a second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).

## Write, place, change and check

A graphic made by an agent usually goes through these steps.

<Steps>

1. Read the API once with [`graphic_reference`](#graphic_reference).

2. Write the module with [`write_graphic`](#write_graphic). It returns the result of compiling that exact text. If it failed, fix the source and write it again.

3. Look at it with [`render_graphic`](#render_graphic), which draws frames with no clip on the timeline.

4. Place it with [`add_graphic_clip`](#add_graphic_clip), giving the track, the time and any values it should draw with. [`insert_graphic`](#insert_graphic) places a graphic at the playhead instead, as the Insert Graphic sheet does.

5. Change it with [`set_graphic`](#set_graphic). To animate a property, add an action with `add_action` and say what the property ends at with `set_action_end`. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

6. Check a frame of the finished timeline with [`render_frame`](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/#render_frame).

</Steps>

## `render_graphic`

Draws a module without a clip, to look at it before placing it. There's no control for this in the app, because a person looks at the preview instead.

### Render graphic options

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | The module to draw. |
| `frames` | array of integers | No | The frames to draw, 1 to 16 of them, in the order given. Not with `frame`. |
| `frame` | integer | No | One frame to draw, 0 or more. Not with `frames`. With neither, frame 0 is drawn. |
| `props` | object | No | The values to draw with, keyed by the schema's names. A key left out draws with the schema's default. |
| `width` | integer | No | The width to draw at, 1 to 8192 pixels. Default: `meta.width`, else the canvas. |
| `height` | integer | No | The height to draw at, 1 to 8192 pixels. Default: `meta.height`, else the canvas. |
| `format` | string | No | `png` (the default) for a contact sheet, or `svg` for one frame's text. |
| `max_width` | integer | No | The widest the sheet may be, 64 to 8192 pixels. The default is 2048. 8192 keeps a 1920-wide graphic's two cells at full size. |
| `background` | string | No | What the sheet is painted on: `transparent` (the default), `checker`, or a hex colour as `#rgb`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`, in either case. |
| `path` | string | No | Where to write the sheet. It's always a `.png`, and its folder must exist. Leave it out for a temporary file. |

`max_width`, `background` and `path` belong to the sheet, and `svg` won't take them.

Each frame is drawn as a clip would draw it. The frame rate is the project's, `durationInFrames` is the module's `meta` value or else 5 seconds, and a frame at or past that length is still drawn, with `progress` at 1, as a longer clip draws it.

### The contact sheet

The `png` format returns an image the model can see, a text block, and a file on disk. The frames sit on a near-square grid, top left first, and each frame's number is printed in a dark strip under its cell. Sixteen frames make a 4 by 4 grid.

- Only the cells scale down to fit `max_width`, never the 8-pixel gaps or the 24-pixel labels. Cells are never scaled up, and the sheet is never more than 8192 pixels tall.
- `checker` paints 16-pixel grey squares, which shows up a graphic's transparent areas.
- A frame that fails draws its error card in its cell. The sheet still comes back, and the text adds a sentence with the error and where it is. A frame that only warned adds a sentence too.
- The text says the frames, each cell's size and scale, the grid, the sheet's size and the background, and ends "Written to `<path>`."

A sheet draws at most 134,217,728 pixels of frames, counted as frames × width × height. That's two frames at 8192 × 8192, or sixteen at 3840 × 2160. Past that the call fails before any frame is drawn, so ask for fewer frames or a smaller size.

### One frame as SVG

With `format: "svg"`, it returns `name`, `frame`, `ok`, `svg` (the frame's SVG text), `diagnostics`, and `ctx`, the values the frame was drawn with: `fps`, `time`, `durationInFrames`, `progress`, `width`, `height` and `canvas`.

It draws one frame and writes no file. A frame that fails isn't an error here either: `ok` is false, `svg` is null and `diagnostics` say why.

### When it won't run

`render_graphic` won't run when:

- The module isn't in the folder, or doesn't compile. The error lists what the folder holds, or gives the first compile error.
- Both `frame` and `frames` are given, or `frames` doesn't hold 1 to 16 whole numbers of 0 or more.
- `format` is `svg` with more than one frame, or with `path`, `background` or `max_width`.
- `max_width`, `width`, `height` or `background` is out of range, or the folder of `path` doesn't exist.
- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range. The error names the key.

## Editing the folder with your own file tools

An agent can also edit the graphics folder directly, and Frame Job sees a change within a moment. Ask `get_graphic` with no `name` for the folder's path.

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Modules | `<name>.js` |
| Fonts | `fonts/`, as `.ttf` or `.otf` |
| Pictures | `assets/` |

`history/`, `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are Frame Job's own, so leave them alone. `history/` holds the kept versions that `restore_graphic` reads, and `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are the reference and its types.

A module's text is kept when Frame Job sees it replaced while the project is open, and that includes a save from an outside editor. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for how changes are picked up.

## What can and cannot be undone

The files in `graphics/` live beside the project, not in its undo history. A change to the clips on the timeline is an ordinary undo step.

| Tool | Undo step? | Marks the project edited? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `write_graphic`, `restore_graphic`, `delete_graphic` | No | No |
| `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset`, `import_graphic` | No | No |
| `add_graphic_clip`, `insert_graphic`, `set_graphic` | Yes | Yes |
| `rename_graphic` | Yes, as one step, for the clips that follow the new name | Only through those clips |
| `export_graphic` | No, it edits nothing | No |

Because a file write can't be undone, Frame Job keeps the last 10 versions of each module. A version is kept whenever Frame Job sees a module replaced while the project is open, whether by `write_graphic`, a save from an outside editor or a restore, and when `delete_graphic` removes one. [`restore_graphic`](#restore_graphic) brings one back. `insert_graphic`'s copy of a template can't be undone either, even though the clip it places can.

Fonts and pictures aren't kept this way. Importing over a file of the same name replaces it for good.

## Fonts and pictures together

A module draws with two kinds of file besides its code. [`import_graphic_font`](#import_graphic_font) adds a font and [`import_graphic_asset`](#import_graphic_asset) adds a picture.

Both take the `path` of a file on this Mac, with `~` expanded, and copy it into the project. The folders are made if they aren't there. Graphics can use the file as soon as the call returns, and a file already at that name is replaced. A `path` that names no file gives an error.

Each result tells the agent what to write in the module: the exact family names for a font, the name for `asset()` for a picture. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).

## `import_graphic_font`

Copies a `.ttf` or `.otf` file into the project's `graphics/fonts/` and returns the family names to use. It mirrors **File ▸ Add Font to Graphics…**. See [Add a font](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/#add-a-font).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | Yes | The font file to copy. |

It returns:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `families` | The family names read from this file. These are the exact strings a `font-family` must say, and they can differ from what other apps show. |
| `library_families` | Every family the project's graphics can now draw with. |
| `path`, `name` | Where the copy landed, and the file's name. |
| `replaced` | True when a file of the same name was replaced. |
| `note` | A reminder that this can't be undone. |

It won't copy a file that isn't `.ttf` or `.otf`, one it can't read, or one that loads no typeface. The last gives the graphics engine's own reason.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`

  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked

  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,

  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,

  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.
